These findings show that salt and sonication regulate the kinetic accessibility of elastically driven focal conic structures, providing a route to tune domain morphology, spectral bandwidth, and iridescence in CNC photonic films.
n0db9f0de878d: Interlayer sliding in two-dimensional (2D) materials is generally assumed to be weakly anisotropic, even as low-symmetry layered crystals with strongly direction-dependent properties continue to emerge. Here we adopt a mechanics-guided conformal probe design that enables quantitative measurement of crystallographically resolved interlayer friction between anisotropic 2D materials. Using Ta2NiSe5 as a model system, we demonstrate pronounced interlayer friction anisotropy approaching 2 orders of magnitude, substantially larger than its moderate in-plane friction anisotropy and the values reported for high-symmetry layered materials. Atomic-resolution lateral force mapping reveals a hierarchical friction landscape composed of atomic lattice corrugation and twist-induced moiré modulation, with the moiré wavelength evolving systematically with relative misorientation. These results show that interlayer friction in low-symmetry 2D materials is governed by a multiscale, orientation-dependent potential energy landscape and constitutes an independent mechanical degree of freedom. The conformal probe platform provides a general route to probe and engineer direction-selective interlayer mechanics in van der Waals systems.
n9569232f371a: The infiltration of CD8+ T cells into the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) microenvironment is a well-established determinant of immunotherapy efficacy and patient prognosis. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing this process and the therapeutic strategies capable of modulating it remain largely unexplored. Here, we identify HCC-IN-247 as a candidate compound that enhances IFNβ-driven CD8+ T cell infiltration both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the long noncoding RNA LINC02084 directly interacts with the transcription factor GLIS1 and facilitates its recruitment to the IFNβ promoter. HCC-IN-247 was identified through screening to target the LINC02084-GLIS1 binding interface, thereby stabilizing this RNA–protein complex. Stabilization of the complex significantly enhances IFNβ transcription, which in turn upregulates CXCL10 and CXCL11 expression and promotes CD8+ T cell infiltration. Furthermore, this study engineered a nanoparticle-based delivery system, designated Lip@RA@BSA-PD-L1/IN-247, for the codelivery of HCC-IN-247 and the anti-PD-L1 antibody atezolizumab in HCC treatment. These nanoparticles exhibited robust tumor-specific accumulation and elicited potent synergistic antitumor activity against HCC in mice. Collectively, our findings establish HCC-IN-247 as an activator of the tumor immune microenvironment and provide a preclinical basis for a combined immunotherapeutic approach to HCC.
n058eba69eaa0: Water under molecular-scale confinement is not simply a geometrically restricted form of bulk water, but can acquire distinct electronic, structural, and collective properties. However, how such an extremely confined state reshapes water’s intrinsic chemistry remains poorly understood. Here, using ab initio calculations and enhanced-sampling machine-learning potential molecular dynamics, we show that extreme two-dimensional confinement activates water for proton generation. Monolayer-confined water exhibits a substantially lower free-energy barrier for forming separated H3O+ and OH– ions than bulk water, and this tendency is further enhanced by lateral compression and nuclear quantum fluctuations. This enhanced reactivity does not arise from a uniform weakening of all water molecules. Instead, confinement makes OH bonds breaking selectively. The water molecule contains electronically distinct OH bonds, with weak in-plane bonds preferentially activated for proton release, while stronger dangling bonds remain relatively inactive. The surrounding hydrogen-bond network then provides disordered pathways for proton relocation, and the enhanced in-plane polarization stabilizes the charged products. Our results suggest that two-dimensional confined water can act as an active and superdielectric medium as indicated by recent experiments. Our findings reveal extreme confinement as a route to tune water-mediated chemistry, with implications for nanofluidics, geochemical pores, biological environments, and catalytic interfaces.
ne2e0d755ad81: Symmetry breaking has the potential to counteract the shortening of excited-state lifetimes with increasing nuclearity and metallicity but is difficult to accomplish in large nanoclusters, whose multishell frameworks are strongly coupled. Here, we report a four-shell silver nanocluster, Ag104, in which the principal reconstruction is concentrated in an Ag52S22 subsurface shell, and whose inner core and outer ligand-protected motifs retain closely similar topologies relative to its highly symmetric Ag100 analogue – a structurally related pair that enables the correlations accompanying localized symmetry distortion to be examined. The two clusters also differ in composition and thiolate substitution pattern, so the comparison probes coupled structural and electronic changes. Electronic-structure calculations and real-space charge analyses showed that subshell-confined symmetry breaking lifts electronic degeneracies, redistributes oscillator strength, and induces pronounced spatial charge separation, thereby reducing electron–hole overlap. Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy further revealed an unexpected order-of-magnitude increase in carrier lifetime from ∼500 ps in Ag100 to ∼5 ns in Ag104 and distinctly activated phonon-assisted relaxation in Ag100 compared to Ag104. This establishes a strategy for engineering large atomically precise nanoclusters with long-lived excited states.
ncee4836af18d: Electrochemical processes involve transient phenomena, including nucleation and growth, phase transformations, dissolution, ion transport, and interfacial restructuring, which are difficult to capture simultaneously at nanoscale and in real time under electrochemical controls. High-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM), originally developed for dynamic biological imaging, combines nanometer-scale spatial resolution with frame times of approximately 0.1–5 s/frame, extending into the subsecond regime, enabling direct visualization of electrochemical interfaces under operando conditions. This perspective highlights emerging applications of HS-AFM in electrochemistry, including electrodeposition, nanoparticle dissolution, corrosion, lithiation-induced morphological evolution, protein adsorption, and nanobubble dynamics. HS-AFM reveals that mechanistic insight often resides in transient, nonequilibrium pathways rather than equilibrium structures alone. Advances will enable real-time nanoscale correlation of interfacial structure, kinetics, and electrochemical function.
ncb93a24c3990: The solid electrolyte interphase in lithium metal batteries determines cycling stability but often suffers from the incomplete decomposition of fluorinated components. Herein, we demonstrate that suspending LiF and Li2O particles in a carbonate‐based electrolyte promotes the defluorination of fluoroethylene carbonate and lithium hexafluorophosphate. These particles preferentially adsorb fluorinated electrolyte species and induce electronic polarization, thereby modulating their redox reactivity and facilitating interfacial decomposition toward LiF. The generated LiF, together with the trace dissolution and interfacial reprecipitation of suspended LiF particles, continuously enriches the electrode surface with LiF‐rich inorganic species. This process results in the formation of a bilayer interphase on both the lithium metal anode and LiNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2 cathode, featuring a flexible inner layer and a dense LiF‐rich outer layer. The resulting interphase suppresses lithium dendrites, mitigates parasitic reactions, and enables 2400 h of stable cycling in symmetric cells and 85.6% capacity retention after 400 cycles in full cells. By introducing suspended LiF/Li2O particles to regulate the interfacial decomposition of fluorinated electrolyte species, this work provides an effective electrolyte‐design strategy for constructing robust interphases in lithium metal batteries.
n98c4f2c4faef: Aluminum‐ion batteries are a promising energy storage technology for high resource abundance, safety, and cost‐effectiveness advantages, but practical implementation is hindered by two degradation mechanisms in Al metal anode: electrically isolated metallic aluminum (iAl0) and electrochemical side‐reaction products (iSEI Al3+). Precise quantification of these inactive species and relationships with cycling reversibility have rarely been established, limiting rational anode design. Here, we develop a basic titration gas chromatography technology to accurately quantify iAl0 and iSEI Al3+, revealing a current density‐dependent Al loss mechanism: iSEI Al3+ loss dominates at low current, while metallic iAl0 loss prevails at high current. We discover that an inorganic‐dominated interphase favors significant suppression of inactive Al formation. Applying an optimal stack pressure strategy (780 kPa) constructs tip‐localized stack pressure/electric field, effectively reducing inactive Al loss by 81.99% and prolonging battery cycling life by ≥500%. These advancements offer fundamental theory and techniques for Al anode reaction mechanism research and provide design principles for high‐performance aluminum‐ion battery.
n6032d7cd2147: Endohedral metallofullerenes offer intrinsic cage‐confined dipoles and structural compatibility with fullerene electron‐transport layers, making them attractive for regulating perovskite interfaces. However, the encapsulated metal ion cannot directly coordinate with surface defects, while the outer carbon cage lacks specific anchoring sites, leading to disordered adsorption configurations, electrostatic heterogeneity, and nonuniform coupling with C60. Here, we employ 1‐pyreneboronic acid (PyBA) as a molecular director to regulate Gd@C82 at the wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite/C60 interface. The boronic acid group anchors to the perovskite surface and passivates undercoordinated Pb‐related defects, while the pyrene framework associates with the Gd@C82 cage and stabilizes favorable molecular configurations. This dual interaction enhances the dipolar character and spatial organization of Gd@C82, homogenizes the interfacial potential, and strengthens electronic coupling with C60, thereby accelerating electron extraction and suppressing nonradiative recombination. The optimized WBG cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 20.23%, enabling monolithic all‐perovskite tandem devices with 28.44% efficiency. The modified WBG devices retain over 90% of their initial efficiency after 1451 h of maximum‐power‐point tracking and 1563 h under damp‐heat conditions, while the tandem devices retain over 80% after 531 h of operation. This work establishes molecularly directed endohedral metallofullerenes as a strategy for coordinating surface chemistry and interfacial electrostatics.
n581a502a183c: Current robotic teleoperations rely on vision‐based detection and feedback of the operation environment. Establishing dual‐way tactile sensing and feedback remains challenging for improving comprehensive status awareness. Here, with the aid of laser induced graphene and silicone materials, we present a haptic chip capable of providing multi‐dimensional and multi‐modal tactile sensing and feedback for both the master side and slave side in a teleoperation system. A triboelectric and piezoresistive sensing array with three‐dimensional dynamic and static tactile sensing. The space of triboelectrification is re‐used as pneumatic haptic feedback at the master side, and the laser induced graphene layer of the piezoresistive sensor also can be used as a thermal heater. Moreover, a piezoelectric chip is also integrated to offer high‐frequency tactile sensing and feedback. Multiple haptic chips can implement a distributed tactile communication network. A hexapod with haptic chips allows the basic identification of territory, attitude, and texture during walking and climbing. Meanwhile, they can then be selectively regenerated at the haptic chip array of the master side directly, and control commands can be sent out by the haptic chip as well. Overall, the haptic chip‐based tactile communication system acts as a complementary control interface to the vision system, which possesses advantages for the teleoperation of robots in special tasks.
n6b64264d23fc: Stretchable electrodes are essential for next generation wearable electronics, but simultaneously achieving high conductivity, large stretchability, and long‐term reliability remains challenging. This work proposes a micro‐origami structured electrode (MOSE) that mitigates the conflicts between stretchability, conductivity and fatigue resistance. By prefabricating valley creases of origami pattern on an EcoFlex substrate, the Platinum (Pt) film/EcoFlex substrate bilayer undergoes bending deformation along the creases upon release of biaxial pre‐stretch, forming regular and controllable micro‐origami structures. Benefiting from the surface metal film, the initial conductivity reaches 19600 S·cm−1. Furthermore, the micro‐origami structure enables the electrode to withstand biaxial tensile strains over 80%, and the high regularity of the origami structure provides excellent fatigue resistance (after 10000 cycles at 50% strain, the sheet resistance remains below 20 Ω/sq). Based on this electrode, a capacitive pressure sensor with high signal repeatability is fabricated. Utilizing the anisotropy of the micro‐origami structure, handwriting signal classification using one single small pressure sensor (approximately 2 cm2) instead of large‐area sensor array is achieved, with an accuracy of 96%. The proposed MOSE provides a design route for metal‐film‐based stretchable electrodes.
n502ff64db317: Peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-based advanced oxidation processes are attractive for water purification but are often limited by short-lived radicals that are easily quenched in complex matrices. Here we report a halogen-modulation strategy to engineer the interfacial microenvironment of nitrogen-doped carbon (N-C) for robust, metal-free PMS activation. A family of halogen-doped carbons (NX-C; X = F, Cl, Br, and I) is synthesized via molten-salt-assisted conversion of ZIF-8, among which bromine-doped N-C (NBr-C) exhibits a lattice-strained, hierarchically porous framework with highly polarized graphitic-N sites. NBr-C delivers a 134-fold enhancement in the phenol degradation rate constant (k obs = 2.55 min−1) and 70.5% total organic carbon (TOC) removal within 5 min. Mechanistic experiments combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that Br doping steers PMS activation away from short-lived radicals toward dual nonradical pathways: singlet oxygen (1O2) oxidation and a catalyst-mediated direct electron-transfer process. The NBr-C/PMS system maintains nearly complete pollutant removal over pH 3–11, in the presence of common inorganic anions and natural organic matter, in real waters, and under continuous-flow operation. This work establishes halogen-regulated interfacial microenvironment engineering as a powerful principle for designing robust, metal-free PMS activators operating through selective nonradical pathways.
n43be3baf3807: Room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials hold immense potential for neuromorphic vision, yet achieving system‐level cognitive capabilities within a single material remains challenging. Here, we design a carbon dots (CDs)–epoxy composite wherein hydrogen‐bond‐mediated interfacial assembly between electron‐donating CDs surface groups and electron‐accepting epoxy moieties deliberately generates interfacial exciplexes. This engineered interface achieves a minimized singlet–triplet energy gap and enhanced spin–orbit coupling (SOC), enabling efficient intersystem crossing (ISC) into a long‐lived triplet reservoir that emits green phosphorescence (∼468 ms). We obtain multiple neuromorphic functions by exploiting the exciplex kinetics. Ultraviolet (UV)‐dose‐dependent triplet filling enables optical learning and noisy pattern capture. The cooperative effect in densely populated exciplex networks establishes an intensity‐gated threshold for spontaneous physical noise reduction at the sensory terminal. Alternating UV‐induced hydrogen‐bond strengthening and near infrared‐induced photothermal relaxation bidirectionally modulate exciplex populations, realizing all‐optical plasticity with high symmetry (AR = 0.33) that supports a fully connected neural network achieving >95% recognition accuracy on noisy digits. The millisecond‐lived triplet reservoir further transcribes dynamic motion trajectories into static 2D afterglow patterns, enabling contactless trajectory recognition and real‐time control without high‐speed cameras. This work provides a unified material strategy integrating sensing, memory, and computation within a single neuromorphic visual terminal.
nc6f5e75e7a20: Reducing the use of precious metals is essential for the commercialization of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). The Schottky contact formed between the catalyst layer and Ti porous transport layer (PTL) at the anode significantly degrades cell performance and necessitates high Ir loading or Pt coating. IrO2 catalysts with various crystallite sizes (1.7‒11.0 nm) were synthesized, and their membrane electrode assembly (MEA) performance was evaluated at a low Ir loading of 0.3 mgIr cm−2 using Pt‐coated Ti PTL and bare Ti PTL. The MEA performance exhibited opposite trends depending on the type of PTL, primarily due to variation in the work function, which is determined by the surface oxygen configuration of the IrO2 catalyst. Smaller crystallites exhibited a larger work function, resulting in a greater performance discrepancy between the two PTL types. To overcome the suboptimal performance of IrO2, we utilized the crystalline 7.1 nm‐sized IrO2 as an electron pathway and deposited highly active amorphous IrOx on its surface. This mixed‐phase Ir oxide exhibited good cell performance and durability even with a bare Ti PTL. This study highlights that the Schottky contact problem of IrO2 catalysts can be overcome through surface engineering, enabling low Ir use for PEMWE.
n761a3deee328: In situ electric tuning (ISET) integrated with scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy (STM/STS) has established itself as a highly effective methodology for controlling quantum electronic states in low‐dimensional materials. This approach combines the sub‐atomic spatial resolution and meV‐resolved spectroscopic capability of STM with the reversible and continuously tunable carrier modulation of field‐effect device architectures. To date, this approach has been applied to numerous systems, including graphene‐based van der Waals heterostructures, correlated electron systems, and moiré superlattice systems hosting emergent quantum phases. Herein, we systematically summarize the state‐of‐the‐art experimental implementations, including global electrostatic gating, tip‐induced local gating, tip‐induced voltage pulse, and in‐plane electric tuning, accompanied with distinct physics under each configuration. We then highlight key representative advances in resolving gate‐dependent band renormalization, correlated insulating states, charge ordering, symmetry breaking, and electrically driven metastable phases at the nanoscale. We discuss practical limitations, such as restricted carrier‐density ranges, tip‐induced perturbations, dielectric reliability, and challenges in decoupling electric effects from current injection and Joule heating. Looking forward, we outline future directions in device engineering, including programmable local electrostatics, scalable architectures, and integrated platforms for operando studies, highlighting their potential to enable deterministic control of emergent quantum phases in functional materials.
nfb39655f17f3: Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) is a widespread degradation challenge threatening metallic infrastructure in marine and industrial environments. Conventional materials‐based mitigation approaches act primarily as external barriers and do not directly control the coupled microbial, electrochemical, and microstructural processes that govern long‐term damage. Unlike previous reviews organized primarily by microbial taxa or protection technologies, this review establishes a mechanism‐oriented framework that maps distinct MIC pathways to guide the rational design of MIC‐resistant alloys. The fundamental MIC mechanisms, including metabolite‐induced corrosion, oxygen concentration cells, and extracellular electron transfer, are outlined to establish the basis for bespoke materials design. Three interrelated design strategies are proposed: (i) microbial‐level inhibition through antibacterial alloying; (ii) interfacial regulation through passive film engineering to regulate charge transfer; and (iii) microstructure‐integrated design, including nanoprecipitates, multiphase structures, and multicomponent alloys, to achieve synergistic antibacterial, mechanical and corrosion‐resistant performance. Finally, key challenges and future directions toward durable and adaptive MIC‐resistant materials are discussed, providing guidance for bridging mechanistic understanding and engineering applications.
n1953f7950989: Photomultiplication type broadband organic photodetectors (PM‐BOPDs) were fabricated by employing one wide bandgap polymer P3HT and one narrow bandgap non‐fullerene acceptor BTPSe‐Ph4F with a weight ratio of 100:2 as active layers. Plenty of isolated electron traps will be formed in the active layers due to the rather low BTPSe‐Ph4F content, leading to poor electron transport channels and efficient hole transport channels in the P3HT:BTPSe‐Ph4F (100:2, w/w) active layers. Photogenerated electrons will be trapped in the isolated BTPSe‐Ph4F; the trapped electrons near the Al electrode will induce interfacial band bending for hole tunneling injection from the external circuit. The dark current density of PM‐BOPDs can be further suppressed by ∼2 orders of magnitude by employing a 3‐BPIC‐F self‐assembled ultra‐thin layer to replace PEDOT:PSS. The optimal PM‐BOPDs display an external quantum efficiency of 2970%, an on/off current ratio of 79 020, and specific detectivity of 1.16 × 1013 Jones at a frequency of 90 Hz at 625 nm light under −10 V bias, indicating strong weak‐light sensitivity of PM‐BOPDs. The optimized PM‐BOPD was employed for photoplethysmography (PPG) monitoring. PPG signals were successfully recorded during rest and exercise, and their characteristics were analyzed to extract heart rate information and identify characteristic pulse wave features.
ncff6e1e722d3: Li metal anodes are promising for next‐generation high‐energy batteries, but their practical use is hindered by dendritic Li growth, unstable interfaces, and large volume fluctuations. Herein, we report a bidirectional sandwich‐structured Li metal anode (SLA) fabricated through a solvent‐free rolling and pressing strategy. The SLA integrates an ultrathin Li layer with thermally stable 3D Cu nanowire networks on both sides, forming a lightweight, flexible, and mechanically robust electrode. The interconnected Cu nanowire framework provides continuous electron pathways, homogenizes current distribution, and accommodates Li volume changes, thereby guiding uniform Li deposition and stripping within the electrode interior. Benefiting from this design, the SLA achieves a high Coulombic efficiency of 98.73% over 250 cycles at 1 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2, while symmetric cells operate stably for over 1350 h with low polarization. Full cells paired with high‐loading NCM811 cathodes deliver excellent cycling stability and rate capability. For a 4‐layer stacked pouch cell, the SLA‐based system delivers a gravimetric energy density of 279.11 Wh kg−1 and a volumetric energy density of 470.52 Wh L−1, outperforming the PLA counterpart. This work provides a simple strategy for advancing stable Li metal anodes and high‐energy‐density Li metal batteries.
n0171fef634b0: Solid-state lithium metal batteries are considered ideal candidates for next-generation energy storage systems due to high energy density and safety. However, NCM811||Li battery systems face severe issues in practical application, such as interface failure between the cathode and anode, lithium dendrite growth, and the insufficient stability of conventional electrolytes. Here, we proposed a synergistic modification strategy combined with nanoconfined polymerization and interface dynamic crosslinking to fabricate self-healing bimetallic MOF-based composite solid electrolyte with enhanced ionic conduction and interface stability. The as-prepared electrolyte exhibits high room-temperature ionic conductivity (12.63×10−4 S cm− 1), extended electrochemical voltage windows (5.14 V), excellent elongation at break (270%), high puncture resistance (5.28 N), superior thermal stability (200 °C), and outstanding cycling stability (94.77% retention over 150 cycles at 0.1 C), which exceeds previously reported electrolytes. Even under high mass loadings of 9.24 mg cm− 2 and 20.38 mg cm− 2 for the cathode, the capacity retention rates can still reach 90.88% and 86.35% after 150 and 100 cycles, respectively, demonstrating practical potential under high-loading conditions. This strategy reconstructs the Li+ transport, interface stability, and recyclability of composite solid electrolytes at the molecular level, paving the way for the development of next-generation high-performance solid-state batteries.
nf23d3c7c0d52: Despite significant progress in photocatalytic half‐reactions and photoelectrochemical water oxidation, achieving stable photocatalytic pure water splitting over Ta3N5 remains a long‐standing challenge. Herein, the incompatibility of cocatalysts between alkaline photocatalytic water oxidation systems and pure water splitting is identified as a critical bottleneck, leading to serious N2 generation through photocorrosion. To address this challenge, a highly dispersed RuCoOx cocatalyst is developed via a multi‐step incipient wetness impregnation strategy. The optimized Pt@Cr2O3/Ta3N5/RuCoOx achieves stoichiometric pure water splitting with an apparent quantum yield of 0.72% at 420 nm, representing the highest value reported for Ta‐based nitride/oxynitride photocatalysts to date. Mechanistic studies reveal that an enhanced interfacial electric field facilitates hole extraction, while a reduced formation barrier of key intermediates accelerates surface reaction kinetics, thereby overcoming the long‐standing bottleneck in photocatalytic pure water splitting over Ta3N5. This work establishes cocatalyst compatibility as a key design consideration for stable photocatalytic pure water splitting and provides mechanistic insight for the rational design of advanced nitride and oxynitride photocatalysts.
n5ba9d63c3e3c: Tin displays rich redox chemistry transitioning between metallic tin (Sn0), stannous (Sn2+), and stannic (Sn4+) states, among which the Sn4+/Sn2+ couple offers the highest theoretical potential ( >0.14 V vs. SHE) whereas remaining unrealized in practical batteries. Herein, we introduce the in situ and successive growth of CsSnI3 single perovskite and Cs2SnI6 double perovskite layers on the cathode surface during operation, enabling the first demonstration of the Sn4+/Sn2+ redox reaction in zinc‐ion batteries, with an increased potential to 0.39 V versus SHE due to enhanced tin‐halide coordination. Further integrated into Zn||SnCl4 full batteries, the design delivers dual discharge plateaus at 1.18 V (Sn4+/Sn2+) and 1.28 V (I0/I−), yielding a high areal capacity of 0.80 mAh cm−2 at 1 mA cm−2 and high energy density of 0.99 mWh cm−2 (660 Wh kg−1, per SnCl4·5H2O mass of the cathode). The three‐electron transfer design exhibits considerable longevity, with Swagelok cells retaining 7000 cycles at 16 mA cm−2 and pouch cells sustaining 200 cycles at 4 mA cm−2 without capacity loss. By enabling the high‐potential Sn4+/Sn2+ redox reaction, the perovskite interlayer provides a cross‐disciplinary strategy to advancing high‐energy aqueous zinc‐ion batteries.
n2ef42a12eec2: Perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) films intended for flexible optical applications are required not only to exhibit excellent luminescence performance, but also to simultaneously possess high stretchability, superhydrophobicity, patterned luminescence, and multicolor programmability under complex conditions such as large deformation, liquid intrusion, and long‐term service. Here we propose a dual‐phase synergistic engineering strategy, and in combination with replica molding and femtosecond laser direct writing technologies, achieve the construction of a biomimetic superhydrophobic surface and the controllable precipitation of PQDs while endowing the film with superelasticity. Benefiting from the dual‐phase structure and biomimetic surface design, the film still retains more than 52% of its initial luminescence intensity and a water contact angle above 150° under 800% tensile deformation. This strategy is applicable to full‐spectrum luminescent systems spanning 470–688 nm and supports proof‐of‐concept binary optical encoding. After continuous immersion in water for 240 days, the film still retains more than 90% of its initial luminescence intensity and more than 95% machine‐learning recognition accuracy. This work provides a new strategy for the design of multifunctional flexible PQDs films with stable luminescence under deformation and water exposure.
n8df6a876e109: Magnetic van der Waals (vdW) materials are promising for memory and logic applications because of their tunable magnetic properties and compatibility with vdW heterostructure devices. However, coupling between magnetic textures in stacked layers is difficult to resolve in conventional plan‐view measurements because the magnetic signal is integrated over the sample thickness. Here, these interactions are quantified in Fe3GeTe2 (FGT)/graphite/FGT heterostructures using cross‐sectional Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and off‐axis electron holography, enabling reconstruction of the local projected magnetic induction within and between the layers. Domain alignment weakens with increasing FGT separation, yielding a stray‐field coupling length scale of λ=37±7$\lambda = 37 \pm 7$ nm for the cross‐sectional geometry studied here, corresponding to the average separation at which domain misalignment first emerges. This length scale corresponds to an approximately 23% reduction in the interlayer magnetic induction relative to bulk FGT. The magnetic induction is reduced relative to bulk FGT up to ∼$\sim$100 nm from a surface. Comparisons with model‐based iterative reconstructions of the magnetization and micromagnetic simulations show that this near‐surface reduction is due to demagnetizing and stray fields. These results quantify the magnetic induction in stacked vdW magnets and guide the design of devices that require controllable coupling between magnetic textures.
nd7434225c3dd: Additive manufacturing has long struggled to bridge nanoscale functionalities with complex macroscale geometries, particularly for nanocomposites with high nanofiller loadings and ordered structures. Herein, we report shear alignment polymer extrusion (SHAPE) three‐dimensional (3D) printing, a strategy that uses high shear forces to align highly loaded nanomaterials (e.g., boron nitride (BN) nanosheets and carbon nanotubes) along defined directions in polymer matrices, enabling the scalable fabrication of macroscopic nanocomposites with complex 3D architectures. A key advancement is the development of high‐loading filaments (e.g., 55 wt% BN in polylactic acid) and a high‐shear extrusion system, overcoming the traditional challenges of poor processability and structural integrity in high‐filler composites. Post‐sintering yields pure nanomaterial architectures that fully replicate the 3D printed geometry with zero volume shrinkage and exceptional thermomechanical stability‐withstanding temperatures above the polymer melting and decomposition without structural failure. These materials exhibit tailored functionalities: vertically aligned BN composites show enhanced thermal conductivity (1.07 W/m/K); horizontally aligned BN structures offer efficient thermal insulation (0.071 W/m/K); and BN membranes display robust mechanical performance (a compressive strength of 3.4 MPa). Generalizable to diverse nanomaterials (0D to 2D), SHAPE opens new avenues for cross‐scale design in thermal management, energy storage, and advanced structural materials.
n52993c0f8792: Thermal radiation carries energy and information, making simultaneous control of its spectral profile and spatial propagation crucial for infrared camouflage, signaling, and communication. However, most thermal materials prioritize spectral manipulation, leaving the propagation direction of broadband thermal signals underexplored and tightly coupled to the spectral response. Here, a spatial and spectral decoupled meta‐window (SSDW) is demonstrated for independent control of the spectral profile and spatial distribution of broadband thermal radiation across 8–13 µm. By assigning directional reflection splitting and spectral tailoring to distinct geometric degrees of freedom, the SSDW exhibits visible haze, mid‐infrared semitransparency, and broadband suppression of specular reflection, including at 10.6 µm. It maintains a stable apparent thermal signature both without external heat interference and under variations in external‐source temperature, source incidence angle, and camera viewing angle. This enables visible–laser–infrared compatible camouflage, while preserving an outward channel for emergency signaling. As a proof‐of‐concept, the SSDW encodes the incidence direction of a 10.6 µm laser into spatial reflection patterns for assistive infrared communication, enabling reliable decoding over moderate angular variations. This work establishes spatial and spectral decoupling as a framework for thermal radiation engineering, extending control beyond radiative intensity toward coordinated heat and information pathways.
n9b046dcb80c8: Mixed A‐site compositions are an effective route to boost the x‐ray detection performance of perovskite single crystals, yet their growth is often accompanied by pronounced spatial compositional inhomogeneity. This macroscopic phase segregation originates from mismatched formation energies and crystallization kinetics among the different cation components, leading to internal composition gradients that hinder carrier transport but are rarely addressed in perovskite single‐crystal research. Here, we report an acetic acid‐enabled synergistic interaction‐engineering strategy for growing phase‐homogeneous mixed‐cation perovskite single crystals. Acetic acid simultaneously lowers the formation barrier of the formamidinium‐rich phase and suppresses the rapid assembly of the methylammonium‐rich phase, thereby balancing their crystallization rates and eliminating compositional gradients across the crystal. Owing to the improved uniformity and crystal quality, x‐ray detectors based on these single crystals deliver a sensitivity of 3.54 × 106 µC Gy−1 cm−2, a low detection limit of 2.65 nGy s−1, and excellent operational stability. This kinetic‐regulation concept offers a practical pathway to homogeneous mixed‐cation perovskite single crystals and supports their use in low‐dose, high‐performance optoelectronic devices.
n1d6e3084eac9: Absorbing honeycomb serves as a core structural material for aircraft stealth. It features both light weight, high mechanical strength and broadband wave absorption. This material realizes the integration of structure...
n88751165e147: Developing enzymatic strategies for diverse reaction manifolds is a major objective in modern biocatalysis. Here, we report the first biocatalytic asymmetric Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky (JCC) cyclopropanation via DNA catalysis. Unlike conventional small-molecule catalysis, which largely favors trans-cyclopropane formation, DNA catalysis enables diastereoselective access to both cis- and trans-cyclopropanes with excellent enantiocontrol from a single catalytic system. The platform accommodates sulfur ylides as well as amide- and ester-derived sulfoxonium ylides. In particular, phenolic ester-derived sulfoxonium ylides exhibit exceptional cis-selectivity while maintaining excellent stereocontrol, overcoming a longstanding limitation of small-molecule-catalyzed asymmetric JCC reactions. Preliminary mechanistic studies are consistent with a DNA scaffold-mediated pathway that promotes cis-diastereomer formation. Together with its scalability under low catalyst loading, this work establishes a previously inaccessible biocatalytic variant of the JCC reaction and expands the scope of DNA catalysis for diastereoselective synthesis.
naa0e9bba1b31: Sustainable mining and recycling of lithium (Li) have the potential to offer a secure and reliable global supply of lithium to meet rapidly growing energy-storage demands. Bioinspired technologies have the potential to increase sustainability and reduce the environmental impacts of lithium purification. In this study, we report the design of a class of bioinspired supramolecular membrane channels that, to the best of our knowledge, achieve one of the highest overall Li+ selectivities reported to date for artificial transmembrane ion channels, with conservative lower-limit selectivity estimates of Li+/Na+ ≥ 94, Li+/K+ ≥ 136, Li+/Mg2+ ≥ 286, and Li+/Ca2+ ≥ 228 under electrochemically driven transport conditions, thereby establishing a new benchmark for Li+-selective membrane channels. The single-channel conductance of this channel for Li+ ions was determined to be 13.35 pS, equating to Li+ ion transport rates of approximately 1.34 × 107 ions/s per channel at −160 mV. These channels were constructed using a central-ring pillar[5]arene appended with alkyl chains ending in diphenylphosphine oxide (DPP) ligands. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that Li+ selectivity arises from coupled hydration-shell retention, ion-ligand coordination at the DPP-functionalized entrance, and confinement effects within the LAP5n10-DPP channel. At the DPP-functionalized entrance, Li+ retains much of its compact hydration shell while engaging the phosphoryl oxygen through a favorable ligand-exchange interaction, whereas Na+ interacts with the DPP region primarily through a water-separated outer-shell geometry, and K+ interacts more strongly with the adjacent hydrophobic/phenyl-rich region. At the central constriction, all ions experience hydration-shell disruption, but divalent Ca2+ and Mg2+ face the largest dehydration penalties because pore passage would require near-complete dehydration of their strongly bound hydration shells.
nf995ac8a3358: Electrified metal–water interfaces govern charge storage and electrochemical reactivity, yet the microscopic origin of their metal-dependent Helmholtz capacitance has remained unresolved. Here, we use extensive density functional theory-based ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to reproduce and explain the long-established experimental capacitance trend at fcc(111) metal–water interfaces. We show that this trend is governed primarily by the electrode-side electronic response of the explicit metal–water interface, which controls the effective electron spillover length and, hence, the bias capacitance. This relation remains predictive for cross-geometry Pt/Au systems. Our findings clarify the microscopic origin of metal-dependent Helmholtz capacitance and suggest a physically grounded design principle for electrode materials in sustainable-energy technologies.
n7a2bcf4b1b0f: The structural transition from clustered water molecules to the hydrogen-bonding networks of bulk liquid defines one of the most fundamental problems in physical chemistry, yet the precise size at which the endohedral cages emerge remains experimentally elusive. While theory has long predicted that a fully encapsulated water molecule requires a minimum of 16–23 surrounding molecules, direct experimental identification has been hindered by the difficulty of size selection of neutral clusters. Using infrared spectroscopy coupled to vacuum-ultraviolet threshold photoionization, we provide the first experimental evidence that (H2O)17 forms the smallest water endohedral cage, achieving a decades-standing goal of establishing the molecular limit of a solvation shell. Surprisingly, the oxygen framework of this (H2O)17 cage defines an unprecedented, nonclassic polyhedron with four tetragonal, four pentagonal, and two hexagonal faces that breaks the symmetry constraints of all classical Platonic, Archimedean, and Johnson solids. This work establishes a critical structural precursor to the hydrogen-bonding network topology observed in condensed-phase water and offers new perspectives at the multidisciplinary sciences of mathematics, materials, physics, and chemistry.
n9cc514260b97: Ruthenium dioxide (RuO2) shows great promise as an acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalyst in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), yet its insufficient stability─often attributed to Ru overoxidation─actually has a hidden cause. Herein, we show that the true culprit is instead residual chloride impurities inherited from the most commonly used RuCl3 precursor. Owing to strong Ru–Cl coordination, substantial chlorine residues are trapped in the RuO2 lattice during conventional synthesis; during electrolysis, they gradually leach out, dramatically accelerating Ru dissolution and lattice oxygen loss and triggering structural collapse. Guided by this insight, we developed a small-molecule-assisted synthesis that yields Cl-free RuO2. The resulting catalyst preserves exceptional structural integrity, sustains its initial activity through 80,000 accelerated degradation cycles, and delivers stable PEMWE operation at 500 mA cm–2 for 500 h, outperforming all reported single RuO2 catalysts and rivaling even the best doped or composite Ru-based catalysts. Our findings resolve a long-standing paradox in RuO2 catalysis and establish chloride elimination as a critical design principle for durable oxide electrocatalysts.
n4a308ff28244: Li-rich layered oxides access high capacities through the combined participation of transition-metal and oxygen redox, but oxygen oxidation is often coupled with irreversible structural rearrangement and voltage decay. Here, we show that oxygen-vacancy-preconditioning modifies the local Ni–O electronic structure and promotes oxygen-derived ligand-hole character in a Li-rich layered oxide. High-temperature quasi-single-crystal (QSC) formation generates oxygen-deficient local environments while preserving the overall layered framework. Synchrotron spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveals enhanced Ni–O hybridization and redistribution of charge compensation toward oxygen-derived states. Mapping resonant inelastic X-ray scattering further shows earlier oxygen participation during charging, followed by increased delocalization of oxygen-derived holes within hybridized transition-metal–oxygen states. This modified redox pathway suppresses Mn reduction and is coupled to a distinct structural response in which transient lattice environments formed during the initial cycle progressively relax during prolonged cycling, while the layered framework is largely retained. The resulting cathode exhibits reduced voltage hysteresis and voltage decay, together with improved electrochemical reversibility. These results establish a direct connection between vacancy-modified ligand-hole character and oxygen-redox-driven structural relaxation, demonstrating how local electronic structure governs the structural pathway of oxygen-redox-active layered oxides.
nf3c5c05acfd8: Delayed emission, a long-lived nonexponential photoluminescence tail, is widely observed in quantum dots (QDs), but its microscopic origin and relationship with blinking and the quantum-confined Stark effect (QCSE) remain unclear. Here, we combine single-QD spectroscopy, time-gated photon analysis, and Monte Carlo simulations across CsPbX3 perovskite, CdSe-based, and InP-based QDs to identify a potential mechanism. Delayed emission correlates with band-edge carrier-trapping blinking, but is weak in QDs dominated by trion-mediated Auger blinking, suggesting delayed emission is not universally tied to charge-separated states. Delayed photons originate from nanosecond-scale carrier trapping and detrapping at nonradiative recombination centers: transiently trapped carriers return to the band edge and recombine radiatively. Time-gated analysis distinguishes this process from QCSE-driven intensity-lifetime fluctuations on slower blinking time scales. Furthermore, we demonstrate that delayed photons compromise the single-photon purity at a fixed excitation repetition rate. These findings establish a general framework of delayed emission in QDs.
nca8fa3e693a1: Uncontrolled Zn nucleation and growth at the electrode–electrolyte interface limit the reversibility and lifetime of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Nanoparticle (NP)-based anode protective layers are widely used to regulate Zn deposition, yet precise control over the exposed zincophilic facets of individual NPs remains challenging. Here, we show a facet-geometry engineering strategy based on threefold-symmetric Te nanoparticles (TF–Te NPs) to modulate Zn plating/stripping during cycling. The TF–Te NPs present a high density of zincophilic facets, while their threefold symmetric geometry spatially clusters nucleation sites within nanoscale proximity, promoting uniform Zn deposition and accelerating interfacial kinetics. As a result, TF–Te NP-modified Zn anodes exhibit reduced nucleation overpotentials, improved rate capability, and enhanced cycling stability. Our work establishes a direct link between NP geometry, facet-dependent zincophilicity, and Zn deposition behavior, offering a strategy for engineering NP protective layers across a broad range of aqueous batteries.
n2836f018169d: Carbonic anhydrase (CA) catalyzes CO2 hydration with turnover frequencies approaching 106 s–1, but native enzymes lack stability under conditions typical of industrial carbon capture. Small-molecule zinc mimics can be more stable under harsh conditions, but product inhibition by bicarbonate limits efficiency. A general framework for predicting turnover across ligand scaffolds has remained elusive. We report the analysis, by experiment and computation, of speciation and catalytic activity of zinc complexes as CA mimics. A literature data set of twelve Zn-ligand complexes was constructed, and the binding free energy (ΔGbind) of bicarbonate to zinc was calculated by DFT with DLPNO-CCSD(T) refinement. ΔGbind strongly correlates with the intrinsic rate constants of these Zn-ligand complexes for CO2 hydration with R2 = 0.90 at pH 9, 25 °C, and saturated CO2 (1 atm). By comparison, combining the commonly used descriptors ΣE(2), qZn, and %Vburied resulted in R2 = 0.74. Examining additional Zn catalysts (for example, the coordination species [ZnL4(OH)]+, where L is 1-methylimidazole) revealed that chemical speciation must be accounted for to describe the observed dependence of catalytic activity on ligand stoichiometry. Furthermore, accurate ranking of catalytic activity for several of the modified cyclens considered requires accounting for steric congestion (%Vburied), as ΔGbind alone does not capture active-site occlusion. These results define a transferable framework that integrates ΔGbind, speciation, and steric properties to enable the design of Zn-based CO2 hydration catalysts.
n26f49d4084d9: The ever-escalating accumulation of atmospheric CO2 and the growing demand for renewable energy conversion and storage have intensified research into solar-driven CO2 utilization technologies. Photothermal catalytic CO2 hydrogenation to methane has emerged as a promising approach for simultaneous carbon resource recycling and solar energy conversion, synergistically integrating the merits of photocatalysis and thermocatalysis. However, achieving high activity, selectivity, and long-term durability concurrently remains a central challenge, demanding precise control over photothermal conversion efficiency, charge transfer, and mass transport. Rational structural regulation spanning multiple length scales, from individual atoms to clusters, nanoparticles, and macroscopic reactors, is pivotal to overcoming such limitations. This review systematically summarizes research progress from a multiscale catalytic system design perspective, covering single atoms, nanoclusters, nanoparticles, supports, and macroscopic reactors. At each scale, the corresponding structure–activity relationships are analyzed, and the modulation mechanisms of active sites, photothermal effects, charge migration, and mass transport are elaborated. On this basis, we critically evaluate the advantages and bottlenecks of current research and put forward design guidelines and future development directions for next-generation high-performance catalytic systems. This review aims to provide both theoretical insights and practical references for the rational design of advanced photothermal CO2 methanation catalysts.
n2b35c9880e74: Ammonia decomposition provides a promising route for on-demand hydrogen production, but conventional thermocatalytic systems are constrained by severe kinetic limitations at low temperatures, limiting their compatibility with low-grade heat utilization. Herein, we develop an electric-field-assisted oxygen-vacancy engineering strategy to promote low-temperature NH3 decomposition over Ru/CeO2 catalysts. Ru/CeO2 catalysts with tunable oxygen-vacancy concentrations were prepared via a pre-impregnation and solid-state grinding method. Structural and spectroscopic characterizations reveal that oxygen vacancies intrinsically strengthen Ru–CeO2–x interfacial electronic interactions, promote charge redistribution, and generate relatively electron-enriched Ru sites. More importantly, the applied electric field further amplifies this vacancy-mediated interfacial regulation and facilitates H-species transfer/removal. The optimized Ru/CeO2-OV3 EF catalyst achieves 35.3% NH3 conversion at 150 °C under a high GHSV of 30,000 mL gcat–1 h–1 and exhibits an electric-field-assisted apparent activation energy of only 12.28 kJ mol–1. In situ DRIFTS, TPD measurements, impedance analysis, and DFT calculations collectively suggest that defect-associated O sites near oxygen vacancies provide favorable accommodation sites for migrated H species, while the electric field promotes interfacial polarization and accelerates H transfer from Ru sites to the CeO2–x surface. This synergistic effect reduces H coverage on Ru active centers, regenerates available Ru sites for sustained NH3 activation, and enables stable low-temperature operation. This work clarifies how an external electric field amplifies oxygen-vacancy-mediated interfacial electron/H transfer and provides a rational strategy for efficient low-temperature hydrogen production from ammonia.
nc20a192143aa: Chemical fixation of CO2 with CH3OH into value-added chemicals, such as dimethyl carbonate (DMC), plays a crucial role in carbon neutrality and resource recycling. However, its efficiency is limited by the ineffective synergistic activation of CO2 and CH3OH. Here, we employ a strategy to construct CeO2-CePO4 heterojunctions by phosphate-functionalized CeO2, introducing an asymmetric Ceδ+-O-P structure for CO2 and CH3OH activation. The prepared Ce0.8P0.2Oσ catalyst achieves a CH3OH conversion of 28.6% with nearly 100% DMC selectivity and retains its performance for 300 h during continuous DMC synthesis at 140 °C. Experimental characterization supports the formation of local Ceδ+-O-P sites in the catalyst. DFT calculations based on one selected idealized strained model containing a specific local Ceδ+-O-P site show a distinct Bader charge for Ce–O–P and Ce–O–Ce coordinated oxygen atoms within this model. Within the same model, the local Ceδ+-O-P site is associated with elongation of the C–O bond in CH3O* and a lower energy barrier for its dissociation into *CH3 and *O, providing a model-specific interpretation of the enhanced DMC yield. This work develops a design strategy for asymmetric catalytic site via composite oxide heterojunctions engineered for CO2 and CH3OH activation, exhibiting great potential for large-scale continuous CO2 chemical fixation to high-value-added chemicals.
nddaa440b2141: Valence dynamics of transition metals are central to oxygen evolution reaction (OER) mechanisms, yet in situ spectroscopic studies capturing these dynamics within amorphous catalysts remain limited. Here, we present in situ X-ray spectroscopy of amorphous catalysts, where CoBi exhibits higher OER performance compared to CoPi. While our data shows successive valence changes toward high-valent states in both catalysts, distinct initial electro-structural states dictate the intermediate evolution. Co(III) dominates in both catalysts at open-circuit potential, yet the Co(III)–O–Co(III) bridge structure observed in CoBi is absent in CoPi. Under active OER, Co(IV) species are identified as distinguishable spectral intensities; these are assigned to highly hybridized low-spin (LS) Co(IV) with reduced electron–electron repulsion, as validated by resonant inelastic X-ray spectroscopy (RIXS) analysis of Li0.75CoO2. Density functional theory supports the conversion from tetrahedral (Td) Co(II) to octahedral (Oh) Co(III) and suggests that factors other than thermodynamic pathways are likely responsible for the performance gap. The lower formal oxidation, larger Co–O length, smaller Co–O–Co angle, prominent pre-edge dipole character and absent oxo-bridging in CoPi suggest a kinetically inefficient Co(IV) state. These findings demonstrate that the initial electro-structure strongly influences the formation of productive high-valent active species and the resulting OER activity.
ne230db331c05: Solar-driven conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals provides an effective pathway for carbon resource utilization. However, the sluggish kinetics of CO2 reduction and the reliance on sacrificial electron donors limit its practical viability. Herein, we present a bifunctional photocatalyst consisting of spatially separated Ag2S and Au cocatalysts anchored on hollow CdS (Ag2S-Au/CdSH), which enables efficient concurrent CO2 photoreduction to CO and selective oxidation of aryl alcohols to benzaldehyde in a sacrificial-agent-free system. The rational integration of dual-active sites induces oriented charge flow, significantly enhancing photogenerated carrier separation and utilization, as evidenced by ultrafast spectroscopy showing extended electron lifetimes. This synergistic architecture delivers markedly higher production rates of 1.2 mmol g–1 h–1 for CO and 2.5 mmol g–1 h–1 for benzaldehyde, representing approximately 8-fold and 5-fold enhancements over pristine CdS, respectively. Comprehensive in situ spectroscopic studies combined with density functional theory calculations elucidate the distinct roles: Au sites strengthen CO2 adsorption and stabilize intermediates for reduction, while Ag2S promotes alcohol dehydrogenation. This synergistic dual-site architecture maximizes redox efficiency by matching reaction potentials and minimizing carrier recombination. This work provides mechanistic insights into catalyst design for integrated CO2 valorization and biomass upgrading, providing a basis for efficient chemical production.
n334c79cb8698: The selective oxyfunctionalization of C(sp3)–H bonds remains a central challenge in chemical synthesis. Although oxygenases and peroxygenases provide biocatalytic alternatives to metal-based chemical methods, their practical use is constrained by costly cofactor regeneration, toxic co-substrates, or limited selectivity. Molybdenum (Mo)-dependent alkyl dehydrogenases circumvent these limitations by employing water, rather than O2 or H2O2, as the oxygen source for hydroxylation in conjunction with an electron acceptor. Here, we combine enzymatic, structural, and computational analyses to characterize a Mo-dependent p-cymene dehydrogenase (pCDH) from an anaerobic hydrocarbon-degrading bacterium. Isolated pCDH selectively hydroxylates a variety of benzylic and allylic C(sp3)–H bonds. A 2.0 Å cryo-EM structure of the heterotrimeric enzyme in complex with p-cymene captures key states of the catalytic cycle. Structure-guided QM/MM modelling and docking rationalize the substrate scope and radical mechanism. These results identify water-dependent Mo-dehydrogenases as promising catalysts for selective C(sp3)–H oxyfunctionalization.
n80df4c9d9ab6: Efficient H2 dissociation and subsequent spillover of active hydrogen species are critical factors for achieving high activity in CO2 hydrogenation reactions. Herein, we constructed a well-designed and highly dispersed Cu–In bimetallic catalyst supported on CeO2. This catalyst enables the spatial separation of plasmonic enhancement, H2 activation, and CO2 conversion sites, thereby significantly improving H2 dissociation capability and H-spillover efficiency. Comprehensive investigations using multiple transient characterizations, together with in situ/operando spectroscopy, reveal that the three components are tightly coupled through H-spillover, electron transfer, and interfacial interactions. Specifically, the Ce sites on the CeO2 surface serve as the active centers for CO2 conversion via a redox mechanism, while the available indirect but consistent evidence suggests that In species likely act as the primary H2 dissociation sites, promoting the reduction of Cu species and the regeneration of oxygen vacancies on the CeO2 surface through H-spillover. Meanwhile, the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect of Cu significantly enhances the light absorption and photothermal conversion efficiency of the catalyst. The photoexcited LSPR electrons generated by Cu are further transferred to the In species and CeO2 surface, thereby facilitating H2 dissociation and the redox cycling of Ce sites. Such a “functional separation–synergistic enhancement” strategy effectively improves the catalytic activity, and the optimal catalyst achieves a CO yield of 230.1 mmol gcat–1 h–1 W–1 cm2 under 1.5 W cm–2 light irradiation at the surface temperature of 300 °C, significantly outperforming both the corresponding dark reaction and the monometallic Cu/CeO2 and In/CeO2 counterparts. This work provides important design principles and mechanistic insights for constructing highly active CO2 hydrogenation catalytic systems by enhancing H2 dissociation and H-spillover processes.
nb868a2c8a215: LiNiO2 (LNO) is a promising high-capacity cathode, but its practical application is hindered by severe structural and microstructural instability. Herein, we develop a two-step calcination strategy that decouples lithiation from Ta introduction. This approach promotes the segregation of a Ta-rich phase at grain boundaries, producing nanosized, radially aligned primary particles that mitigate strain and suppress microcracking. It also preserves a layered–rocksalt nanostructured multiphase that reversibly transforms into a layered–spinel-like state during charging, which may contribute to structural stability and Li-ion transport. The optimized TS-Ta-LNO delivers 252.7 mAh g–1 and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 100 cycles. Furthermore, a TS-Ta-LNO/Li-metal pouch cell maintains stable voltage profiles under an electric vertical take-off and landing dynamic-load protocol, demonstrating its potential for high-energy, high-power batteries.
n615084cc7254: Hot carriers (HC) offer a potential route to surpass conventional efficiency limits in solar cells. Generated after light absorption, these high-energy carriers can significantly boost device performance if extracted before dissipating energy as heat. Although HC cooling has been studied in tin-based perovskites, interpreting these dynamics is challenging because high-energy, high-fluence pump pulses required to generate HCs have shallow penetration depths, confining excitation near the surface. In tin-based perovskites, surface properties differ from the bulk, and surface defects may strongly contribute to the optical response. Here, by using pump-push-probe ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, we photo-excite the semiconductor thin film with a low-energy pump, in a photon density range typical for solar cell operation, making relevant the bulk electronic properties, and selectively re-excite the photo-carriers only once they cool down, enabling direct tracking of HC relaxation in the relevant spectral region while minimizing surface contributions. We track the cooling process in FA0.85Cs0.15SnI3 (FA = Formamidinium) as a benchmark sample and extend the analysis to single-cation FA+, MA+ (MA = methylammonium), and Cs+ tin perovskites. Across all compositions, and at different doping densities, we find cooling timescales in the 150–600 fs time range. These results highlight the central role of phonon-mediated interactions and show that ultrafast cooling fundamentally limits hot carrier extraction in tin halide perovskites.
n472b3f592c93: Sodium-metal batteries present a more abundant alternative to lithium-based batteries, with high theoretical capacity and comparable reduction potential. Ether electrolytes perform well in sodium-metal batteries under continuous cycling and are presumed to have a stable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI). However, the solubility of sodium SEI components is a cause for concern, and SEI evolution during calendar aging is not commonly studied for the ether sodium-metal system. In this work, SEI mass formation and dissolution are quantitatively measured for NaPF6 in diglyme. For varying potential hold levels, significant SEI dissolution is observed, from 55 to 76% of the originally formed SEI. Characterization shows that in addition to organic component dissolution, inorganic salts such as NaF and NaxPOyFz are unstable in SEI during open circuit rest. This instability results in continuous corrosion of sodium metal during calendar aging, highlighting an important understanding and concern of SEI stability in sodium-metal batteries.
n352917b010cd: Fast Na+ transport and durable interfacial stability remain challenging for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries. To address these issues, we developed a synergistic solvation-interphase regulation strategy by integrating methyl propanoate (MP) with a combined VC/NaDFOB additive pair. MP modifies the Na+ solvation sheath and facilitates Na+ desolvation, while VC and NaDFOB cooperatively generate a mechanically robust hybrid organicinorganic interphase. This coupled regulation enables enhanced ion transport and interfacial stability over a broad temperature range. The EC/EMC/MP + VC/NaDFOB electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.52 mS cm–1 at –40 ̊C and an increased Na+ transference number. Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells retain 96.5% of their initial capacity after 1000 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% at room temperature. At –20 ̊C, the cells deliver 69.4 mAh g–1 for over 900 cycles, corresponding to 82% of their room-temperature capacity. This work establishes a practical solvation-interphase regulation approach for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries.
n001f71cde773: The efficacy of peptide-based tumor vaccines is often constrained by the size-exclusion barrier of the subcapsular sinus (SCS), which restricts infiltration of macromolecules into the lymph node (LN) parenchyma essential for T-cell priming. Here, inspired by the clinical contrast agent Sonazoid, we developed an ultrasound-assisted vaccine platform with tunable phase-transition behavior for the active modulation of the LN microenvironment. The system integrates phosphoserine-decorated lipid chemistry to promote cell-mediated LN trafficking, a covalently conjugated adjuvant–antigen construct for synchronized immunostimulation, and liquid-state perfluorocarbon nanodomains programmed for ultrasound-triggered liquid–gas transition. Upon localized ultrasound irradiation, the chemically programmed phase transition triggers cargo release, while the resultant acoustic cavitation generates transient openings in the SCS endothelium. This process enables deep parenchymal infiltration of vaccine components that would otherwise be excluded. Beyond the physical barrier disruption, RNA sequencing reveals that acoustic stimulation drives both structural and immunological reprogramming of LN into an immune-permissive niche. By synergizing mechanical stimulation with biological modulation, this strategy induces benign and persistent LN expansion, amplifies antitumor T-cell responses, and establishes durable immunological memory, resulting in both prophylactic and therapeutic outcomes. This approach is versatile across both model antigens and neoantigens, offering a bioinspired, two-stage LN-targeted delivery strategy that serves as a framework for designing more effective therapeutic vaccines.
n04986efcd5d2: In stark contrast with traditional refraction phenomenon in isotropic media, refraction of hyperbolic polaritons enables extreme confinement and nanofocusing of mid-infrared light. However, the tuning of hyperbolic refraction typically relies on plasmonic systems (e.g., gating graphene and phase-change materials), and therefore, the electron–electron scattering introduces inevitable propagation losses of polaritons. Herein, we demonstrate that refraction of highly confined hyperbolic polaritons in α-phase molybdenum trioxide (α-MoO3) crystal strongly depends on the dielectric superstrate. We theoretically and experimentally indicate that both the wavevector (its direction and magnitude) and the propagation direction of refracted hyperbolic polaritons can be controlled by varying the twist angle between the vdW dielectric layers of tungsten diselenide (WSe2) and α-MoO3 crystals. Moreover, we observe the total internal reflection and zero-phase propagation of nanoscale-confined polaritons in hyperbolic media. Our study of the propagation of hyperbolic polaritons not only deepens the understanding of polariton refraction at the nanoscale and in strongly anisotropic media but also promises the development of functional nanophotonic elements and devices.
nf084b8590f19: Silicon-based solid-state batteries (Si-SSBs) offer enhanced safety and higher energy density over conventional liquid-electrolyte systems, yet their practical realization is critically hindered by severe volume expansion of silicon anodes and poor interfacial compatibility with solid-state electrolytes. This review provides a comprehensive evaluation of recent advances from a coupled design perspective, integrating silicon anode engineering, electrolyte compatibility optimization, and interfacial stabilization. We systematically examine emerging strategies for silicon anodes alongside compatibility approaches tailored to each electrolyte type, with a particular focus on the coupled chemo-mechanical degradation at the silicon/electrolyte interface. A systematic compatibility mapping linking different Si architectures with specific electrolyte families reveals the most promising material combinations and their underlying design principles. Beyond materials design, we address critical manufacturing challenges including stack pressure management, scalable processing, and prelithiation techniques essential for industrial translation. Finally, we propose a forward-looking roadmap integrating multiscale characterization, AI-assisted design, and scalable fabrication, providing both theoretical guidance and practical strategies for developing high-performance, commercially viable Si-SSBs.
n20c2405e443b: Dynamic DNA nanomachines are programmable devices capable of executing certain controlled movements, structural reconfigurations, and functional tasks. Over the past few decades, extensive advancements have been made in designing DNA-based molecular systems driven by strand displacement, catalytic reactions, enzymatic processes, chemical or physical stimuli. The development of DNA nanotechnology has further enabled the construction of highly precise and complex DNA nanomachines. Herein, we review dynamic DNA nanomachines from a motion-to-function perspective, emphasizing how programmable movement, structural reconfiguration, or autonomous operation can be converted into biomedical output. Structural platforms, driving mechanisms, biomedical functions, and translational barriers are discussed. Particularly, we focus on the systems in which DNA dynamics directly contribute to biosensing, bioimaging, therapeutic activation, cell regulation, and molecular decision-making. This framework distinguishes dynamic DNA nanomachines from static DNA nanostructures, which also highlights the design requirements needed to move these systems toward practical biomedical applications.
n9345afcbbafa: Conductive hydrogel electrodes are vital components for achieving human-machine interfaces. However, the inherent trade-off between high conductivity and favorable mechanical/adhesive properties remains a significant challenge for hydrogel-based epidermal electrodes. Here, we developed a multifunctional MXene/WPU/PAA (MWA) hydrogel electrode that combines robust mechanical properties, strong adhesion, and excellent conductivity. The introduced MXene nanosheets can induce free-radical polymerization, resulting in fast gelation (<5 min) at room temperature. Theoretical analyses reveal that MXene nanosheets form abundant hydrogen bonds with polymer chains, thus enhancing the cross-linking density and mechanical strength of the hydrogel electrode. The MWA hydrogel can form a stable skin-electrode interface, enabling high-fidelity multimodal physiological signal monitoring. Specifically, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for sEMG reached 36.0 dB, while the SNR for ECG was 30.1 dB, outperforming the Ag/AgCl electrodes. The MWA hydrogel exhibits outstanding adhesion under repeated cycles and simulated sweat conditions, reaching 94.2 and 55.5 kPa, respectively. Furthermore, the MWA hydrogel electrode demonstrates precise scalp EEG monitoring, enabling wireless drone flight control via real-time brainwave decoding. This work provides insight into MXene-polymer interactions and demonstrates the applicability of the developed electrode to brain-computer interface applications.
n231920bd57fc: Atomically thin materials can strongly confine light into quanta of lattice vibrations, leading to strong light–matter interactions. Some of these materials can exhibit topology, which protects the edge states embedded inside the bulk from backscattering, while some host magnetism, providing another degree of freedom to control topological properties. The simultaneous observation of all of these phenomena in a single material can lead to various applications by enabling light-controlled topological electronic and nanophotonic devices. Here we demonstrate via first-principles density functional perturbation theory calculations that atomically thin MnBi2Te4 is a promising platform for hosting three highly confined, tunable, and long-propagating magnetophononic polaritons. These polaritons strongly modulate exchange interactions, especially the second polariton in 2 SL MnBi2Te4, inducing strong light–matter coupling in the presence of light. Intriguingly, this coupling not only induces an antiferromagnetic-to-ferromagnetic phase transition but also drives an electronic phase transition from trivial to topologically nontrivial states in 2 SL MnBi2Te4. We also show that these polaritonic modes have relatively weak electron–phonon scattering rates and that these scattering rates change with layer thickness and magnetic ordering due to spin–phonon coupling. Overall, our results suggest that MnBi2Te4 is a promising material for topological electronics, nanophotonics, and nanophonics capable of providing greater control of data signals via light.
nd55a381048d4: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are versatile precursors for nanostructured, heteroatom-doped carbons. However, understanding the spatiotemporally resolved mechanisms that govern crystalline-to-amorphous framework collapse, diffusion-mediated reorganization of transient intermediates, and the subsequent formation of graphitic carbon remains challenging. Here, we elucidate the transformation of the 2D leaf-shaped zeolitic imidazolate framework ZIF-L into Zn-dispersed N-doped carbon using a combination of in situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD). These measurements directly capture the sequential collapse of the layered MOF framework and the associated morphological evolution under controlled heating, decoupled from beam-induced effects during electron microscopy. Complementary ex-situ pyrolysis (700–1100 °C), together with high-resolution TEM, synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function (X-PDF) analysis, and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), reveals the diffusion of Zn-containing species, ligand decomposition, and progressive graphitization within the amorphous matrix. We identify temperature-dependent stages involving ligand breakdown, migration of Zn–Nx species, followed by Zn loss, and ultimately forming porous N-doped carbon at 1000 °C that exhibits the strongest electrochemical response within this series. These findings establish temperature-dependent structure–property relationships that enable the thermal engineering of MOF-derived ORR catalysts.
n900c122acae3: Acute lung injury (ALI) is characterized by an uncontrolled cycle of inflammation and oxidative stress. However, conventional therapeutics are limited by physiological pulmonary barriers and poor targeted bioavailability. In this study, an inhalable multifunctional liposomal system (designated as R&I/Lip@PEG-M) was elaborately engineered to codeliver Resveratrol and IMD-0354 to disrupt the inflammation-oxidative stress cycle for ALI therapy. Upon nebulized inhalation, the negatively charged R&I/Lip@PEG-M liposomes would efficiently penetrate the mucus barrier, extensively accumulate in the pulmonary alveoli, and be specifically taken up by alveolar macrophages via mannose-mediated targeting recognition. Particularly, the internalized liposomes could exert combined therapeutic effects by scavenging intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and blocking the NF-κB signaling pathway to inhibit inflammation. In the LPS-induced ALI mouse model, the designed R&I/Lip@PEG-M significantly reduced the population of inflammatory macrophages, reprogrammed the redox microenvironment, and successfully mitigated lung damage and pulmonary edema.
n18e48ff0f97f: Two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offer tunable interlayer spacing and accessible surfaces that can overcome key limitations of conventional sodium-ion battery (SIBs) anodes. Here, we investigate Na+ storage mechanisms in three-layer 2D heterostructures composed of horizontally stacked graphene (G), nitrogen-doped graphene (NG), and MoS2 (M) by combining cyclic voltammetry with operando spectroelectrochemical Raman spectroscopy. Restricting the active thickness to three atomic layers enables direct spectroscopic access to interfacial charge transfer and strain during cycling. Electrochemical analysis reveals that Na+ storage is governed by two coupled factors: the permeability of the electrolyte-facing outer layer, and the electronic–mechanical interactions within the interlayer space. NG outer layers facilitate ion access and deliver up to 40-fold higher capacities than pristine graphene stacks, whereas MoS2 top layers suppress ion infiltration. Operando Raman correlates faradaic features with reversible structural changes, allowing separation of charge-doping and strain effects during cycling. The results demonstrate that Na+ storage proceeds predominantly via reversible accumulation in confined interlayer and blister-like reservoirs formed during solvent cointercalation. Incorporating MoS2 as a middle layer redistributes charge and buffers mechanical strain, enhancing cycling stability. These findings provide insights into charge storage mechanisms in 2D materials.
n344f6e871368: Optogenetics enables highly specific regulation of neuronal activity with exceptional spatiotemporal precision, providing powerful tools for neural circuit interrogation and the treatment of neurological disorders. However, the limited tissue penetration of visible light restricts its application to deep neural tissues. Near-infrared (NIR) neuromodulation has emerged as a promising alternative by leveraging the superior tissue penetration and minimal invasiveness of NIR light. Recent advances in NIR-responsive nanomaterials, optical engineering, and neurotechnology have rapidly transformed the field from nonspecific photobiomodulation to cell-specific nanotransducer-mediated neuromodulation and integrated neuromodulation systems. In this review, we summarize the optical principles governing NIR propagation in biological tissues and the mechanisms underlying NIR-mediated neural stimulation. We then discuss recent advances in representative NIR nanotransducers, including photothermal, optoelectric, photoacoustic, and NIR-to-visible upconversion platforms together with integrated neuromodulation systems that combine NIR stimulation with multimodal neural recording and closed-loop feedback. We further highlight emerging applications in the central nervous system, optic nerve, and peripheral nerve disorders. Finally, we discuss the key challenges toward clinical translation, including improving tissue penetration, cell specificity, biosafety, and translation, developing intelligent multidisciplinary neuromodulation platforms, and integrating artificial intelligence with closed-loop neural interfaces to achieve adaptive, precise, and personalized neuromodulation.
n81f9458e755a: Lanthanide-doped luminescent nanocrystals (NCs) hold significant promise for bioimaging, theranostics, catalysis, sensing, lighting, and displays, motivating an in-depth understanding of their optical properties. This work reveals the profound, yet widely disregarded, impact of surface structure changes on the luminescence of growing NCs through a model study of Eu3+ surface-exchanged Sr2YF7 NCs. Contrary to expectation, a stark drop in luminescence intensity exceeding several orders of magnitude was observed as the particle size increased. Atomic-resolution electron microscopy imaging shows that the NCs evolve from spheroidal to cuboidal morphologies during growth, with a shift in preferentially exposed crystal facets from {111} to {200} that renders lattice distortion less favorable. High-resolution optical spectroscopy probing surface Eu3+, together with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy and reaction kinetics study, reveals a high extent of Eu3+ exchange in the small spheroidal NCs with lattice distortion extending far from the surface into the interior.
