nffe48c158979: Reconciling exceptional catalytic activity with operational durability at ultralow noble‐metal loadings remains a central challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. Herein, an in situ acid‐etching‐assisted defect engineering strategy is reported for constructing an ultrahigh‐loading electrocatalyst (Ir@CM4) that predominantly features atomically dispersed iridium anchored on hierarchical mesoporous CeMn oxides. Directional Mn dissolution generates a dense oxygen vacancy network that traps Ir species, inducing a profound strong metal‐support interaction to establish a highly electron‐deficient, rigid Ir‐O‐Ce covalent framework. Consequently, Ir@CM4 delivers an exceptional mass activity of 948.15 A g−1 at 1.53 V versus RHE (31‐fold higher than commercial Ir Black). In a PEMWE full cell with an ultralow loading of 0.28 mgIr cm−2, it sustains robust operation for 6350 h at an industrial‐relevant 1 A cm−2. Multimodal in situ tracking confirms that this covalent rigidity thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, bypassing degradation‐prone pathways to strictly enforce the highly stable adsorbate evolution mechanism. Density functional theory uncovers the quantum‐mechanical origin: strong metal‐support interaction‐induced charge transfer downshifts the Ir d‐band center to ‐3.93 eV, which circumvents traditional scaling relations by weakening antibonding orbital filling. This multiscale structural and electronic synergy effectively decouples the activity‐stability trade‐off, providing a translatable paradigm for industrial‐grade acidic water electrolysis.
ncf71a8efe79d: High‐voltage Ni‐rich cathodes coupled with sulfide solid electrolytes suffer from coupled instability of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and Li+ transport discontinuity under deep delithiation. Conventional oxide coatings mainly act as passive barrier layers that separate reactive contacts but remain structurally isolated from layered cathodes without simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and Li+ transport. Here, we report an oxyhalide‐enabled interfacial chemistry strategy based on a reconstructive Nb‐O‐Cl framework on LiNi0.83Co0.07Mn0.10O2 cathodes (denoted as C‐NCM). Derived from a mixed‐anion LiNbOCl4 (LNOC) precursor, the Nb‐O‐Cl framework undergoes mechanochemically assisted interfacial reconstruction, forming an amorphous oxyhalide interphase coupled with a Nb‐containing near‐surface region. Unlike passive oxide barriers, this chemically integrated architecture simultaneously reshapes the local Ni‐O electronic environment and mediates interface‐crossing Li+ transport. Nb‐O/Nb‐O‐Cl coordination redistributes local charge and is associated with improved retention of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and mitigated oxygen‐related irreversible evolution, while the Cl‐containing oxyhalide framework provides an ionically conductive transition region that facilitates Li+ migration across the cathode/electrolyte interface. Accordingly, C‐NCM exhibits reduced sulfide‐derived interphase formation and slower resistance growth, together with 88.17% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 4.5 V under high cathode loading. This work shifts cathode/sulfide‐electrolyte interface design from passive oxide‐barrier protection toward reconstructive mixed‐anion interfacial chemistry.
ne30e3fb6ac4e: Lithium carbonate (LC) is markedly cheaper than lithium hydroxide (LH) but remains underused for layered oxide cathodes because LC‐derived materials perform poorly. Here, using a mid‐Ni cathode, LiNi0.65Co0.05Mn0.30O2 (N65), we trace this performance gap to LC‐induced defects that span length scales, from atomic‐scale disorder to nanoscale and microscale porosity. These defects originate from three features of the carbonate pathway that act across the solid, liquid, and gas phases, namely decoupled dehydration and lithiation, late melting of the carbonate, and a locally oxygen‐deficient atmosphere from evolving CO2. Guided by this picture, we heal the defects with a single secondary heat treatment (SH) that adds an optimized amount of LH, simultaneously replenishing lithium, restoring an oxidizing atmosphere, and densifying the structure. The resulting N65‐LC SH achieves discharge capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability comparable to those of the LH counterpart, while cutting the lithium precursor cost by 9% to 16% relative to conventional all‐LH synthesis. More broadly, the gap between LH and LC is not an intrinsic property of the carbonate but a consequence of a precursor‐specific pathway that, once traced, can be engineered around to unlock low‐cost, high‐performance Ni‐based layered oxide cathodes.
n1be1486fcdc2: Two‐dimensional heterostructures combining sp–sp2$^2$ hybridization—blending graphene with graphyne‐based allotropes—offer substantial potential for enhancing the tunability of electronic and transport properties while providing significant structural flexibility, which are desirable characteristics for next‐generation nanoscale electronics. Despite such potential, their experimental realization remains elusive, as synthesized carbon heterostructures are limited to doped, graphene‐based systems exhibiting exclusively sp2$^2$ hybridization. Here, the on‐surface synthesis of covalently bonded sp–sp2$^2$ lateral heterostructures between graphene nanoribbons and graphdiyne networks on Au(111) is demonstrated. Atomic‐resolution scanning tunneling microscopy, combined with density functional theory, reveals the formation mechanism of the covalent interfacial bonds between nanoribbons and graphdiynes, also highlighting the key role of surface chemistry. Bromine atoms, deriving from the molecules dehalogenation and chemisorbed along the nanoribbon, inhibit junction formation, but bonding efficiency can be boosted up to 66% by controlled removal of these byproducts. Electronic structure and transport calculations show that the 2D heterostructure by itself is characterized by disentangled properties for the two subsystems, forming an atomically narrow junction, enabling voltage‐tunable spatial current separation in two dimensions. These results define a viable strategy for engineering graphene‐based sp–sp2$^2$ heterostructures, paving the way for the design and synthesis of all‐carbon nanoscale electronic architectures.
n42c97edef5de: Autonomous soft actuators are essential for untethered intelligent robotic systems. However, achieving energy‐efficient operation and long‐term shape retention in solid‐state platforms remains a significant challenge, as most conventional systems rely on continuous power input or complex fluidic architectures. Here, we report an environmentally adaptive ionic actuator inspired by the Venus flytrap, capable of self‐sensing and bidirectional deformation without sustained external energy. By incorporating azobenzene moieties into an ionogel network, we trigger a unique nanopore‐mediated Janus actuation. A single, low‐power UV pulse (35.3 mW cm−2) induces rapid photoisomerization and localized dehydration, forming surface nanopores that facilitate asymmetric moisture uptake. This structural reconfiguration drives directional bending that is passively maintained for over 10 min, which is an exceptionally long retention time compared to conventional soft actuators. Furthermore, electrification‐induced voltage signals enable zero‐bias proximity sensing. By integrating these synergistic characteristics, we demonstrate a biomimetic ionograsper that combines ion‐redistribution‐induced sensing with energy‐efficient light‐triggered actuation for sophisticated object manipulation. Overall, this work provides a robust strategy for developing multifunctional and power‐efficient soft robots capable of intelligent environmental interaction.
n2e53476b6aec: Bioinspired Ionic Soft Actuators In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74981), Hong Chul Moon, Yong Min Kim, and co‐workers propose a multifunctional ionic soft actuator that integrates ion‐redistribution‐based proximity sensing with structural‐reconfiguration‐driven bidirectional actuation. UV‐induced photoisomerization and dehydration generate a nanoporous surface that promotes asymmetric rehydration, enabling long‐lasting deformation after a single low‐power stimulus, while mobile‐ion redistribution provides self‐powered non‐contact sensing for energy‐efficient soft robotic manipulation.
n626fd9beb0a4: Mucosal inflammatory disorders such as dry eye disease (DED) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), driven by TNF‐α‐mediated immune‐epithelial crosstalk, remain therapeutically challenging. Conventional inhibitors often suffer from poor mucosal permeability and transient efficacy with 1:1 binding. Although extracellular protein degradation (eTPD) technologies can eliminate pathogenic proteins, most of them operate stoichiometrically, limiting dosage efficiency and durability. Here, we report a receptor‐mediated endolysosomal recycling chimera (RECYC) platform that enables catalytic, recyclable degradation of TNF‐α with multiple turnovers, achieving sustained suppression of mucosal inflammation. RECYC integrates a pH‐responsive peptide that binds TNF‐α at physiological pH and releases it in acidic endosomes, with a CI‐M6PR‐targeting aptamer that remains pH‐stable to drive continuous recycling. The anti‐TNF‐α RECYC achieved efficient uptake and recyclable clearance of extracellular TNF‐α across conjunctival and colonic epithelial cells and macrophages, achieving superstoichiometric TNF‐α clearance with up to 7.5 catalytic turnovers. The ∼30 kDa RECYC exhibited superior tissue penetration in murine cornea and colon compared to inhibitory antibodies. In murine DED and IBD models, RECYC restored ocular surface homeostasis and reduced colon inflammation with low‐dose, infrequent administration. Human corneal limbus organoids further confirmed prolonged anti‐inflammatory activity. Together, RECYC establishes a modular, recyclable eTPD platform for sustained treatment of TNF‐α‐driven mucosal inflammation.
nb7a3ca15d683: Simultaneously achieving high visible transparency, high refractive index (n), and a large Abbe number (υ D) in organic polymers remains a fundamental challenge. Here, a facile and efficient dual sulfur-mediated Michael addition strategy is reported to synthesize transparent high refractive index polymers (HRIPs) with large υ D. By combining main backbone de-conjugation to preserve visible transparency with rational side-chain engineering for n-tuning, the optimal polymer (H4) achieves an ultrahigh n of 1.86 at 589 nm alongside a large υ D of 34.93 and robust stability. Moreover, polymer H4 exhibits remarkable performance in nanoimprint lithography, replicating features down to 75 nm with aspect ratios up to 8.5 and a low volumetric shrinkage of only 3.23%. Notably, a nanoimprinted metalens prototype fabricated from H4 delivers a relative focusing efficiency of 49.8% at 550 nm (NA = 0.5), approaching the theoretical design value (52.94%). Therefore, the high refractive index polymer H4 bridges molecular design and manufacturable meta-optics, showing tremendous potential in scalable, flexible, next-generation photonic platforms by translating side-chain polarizability engineering into practical wavefront control.
n64a6df8ab309: In structural energy storage devices (SESDs) that simultaneously store electrochemical energy and bear mechanical loading, the external force will normally affect the electrochemical performance of SESDs. One example is that, under cyclic bending stress, voltage ripples emerge in charge‐discharge curves, which cause voltage instability. In this study, we demonstrate that these voltage ripples originate from spatially heterogeneous electric field distribution within the mechanically deformed region. By using polarized electric fields formed through hydrogen bonding networks in MXene additive electrolyte, we can effectively homogenize the distribution of the electric field, thereby attenuating voltage ripples and smoothing the voltage curves. Moreover, the uniform electric field distribution promotes uniform Zn deposition and extends the device lifespan. As a result, the fabricated Zn‐ion‐based structural hybrid supercapacitor (CSHS) with MXene additive electrolyte exhibits a capacity retention of 93.6% after 10 000 three‐point bending cycles at a strain of 0.5%, much higher than that of CSHS without the addition of MXene (80.4%). The investigation into the suppression of voltage ripples of SESDs paves a viable way to design high‐performance structural power sources capable of exhibiting stable voltage under mechanical loading.
n1594ca0dfe47: Aerogels have emerged as a unique class of ultralight porous materials that combine exceptional thermal insulation with low density, high porosity, and remarkable structural versatility, enabling broad opportunities across aerospace, energy, electronics, environmental remediation, and wearable technologies. However, their widespread adoption has been constrained by the high cost, limited scalability, and energy‐intensive nature of conventional manufacturing processes, particularly supercritical CO2 drying. This review highlights recent advances in scalable and cost‐effective aerogel fabrication, including ambient‐pressure drying, templating strategies, top‐down manufacturing, chemical vapor deposition, and solution spinning, which collectively enable enhanced performance while significantly reducing production complexity and cost. We further present a unified perspective on the thermal transport physics of porous materials by systematically discussing the mechanisms of solid conduction, gas conduction, convection, and thermal radiation, and comparing aerogels with other porous architectures such as cellular foams. These fundamental insights establish rational design principles for engineering next‐generation aerogels with tailored thermal functionalities. Finally, we showcase emerging applications that extend well beyond thermal insulation, including moisture‐ and water‐driven energy harvesting, oil–water separation, high‐temperature acoustic insulation, and thermoregulating smart textiles. By bridging scalable manufacturing, fundamental thermal science, and emerging multifunctional applications, this work provides a comprehensive framework for the rational design and commercialization of next‐generation aerogels, paving the way toward their widespread adoption in advanced materials and engineering systems.
nfacb45ed1c36: Efficient wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite top cells are essential for high‐performance perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs), yet their fabrication in humid ambient air remains difficult because moisture‐ and oxygen‐induced reactions deteriorate film quality and stability. Here, 4‐[[4,6‐bis(octylthio)‐1,3,5‐triazin‐2‐yl]amino]‐2,6‐bis(1,1‐dimethylethyl)‐phenol (BTDP) is introduced into the perovskite precursor to enable WBG perovskite formation under high‐humid ambient air conditions. BTDP scavenges superoxide radical anions, inhibits I− oxidation to I2, absorbs ultraviolet light, coordinates with Pb2+ to regulate crystallization and forms a hydrophobic barrier at surfaces and grain boundaries. With this strategy, blade‐coated WBG perovskite solar cells (PSCs) fabricated at 60% relative humidity deliver a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 23.45%, which represents the highest PCE reported for air‐processed WBG PSCs with bandgap ≥1.68 eV. Mini‐modules with an aperture area of 14.81 cm2 reach 20.12% efficiency. Moreover, the method enables ambient‐air fabrication of two‐terminal perovskite/tunnel oxide passivated contact (TOPCon) TSCs with a certified efficiency of 32.59%, among the highest PCEs reported for two‐terminal perovskite/TOPCon TSCs. This study provides a scalable route to efficient, stable single‐junction and tandem perovskite photovoltaics.
nb0b4a69f1d1d: AlScN is an emerging semiconductor material that exhibits pronounced ferroelectric switching and enhanced piezoelectric responses through the incorporation of scandium (Sc) into aluminum nitride (AlN). These properties make AlScN a promising candidate for next‐generation ferroelectric in‐memory computing architecture and radio‐frequency circuits. However, challenges arise when preparing high‐quality epitaxial films with high Sc content, including insufficient ferroelectric endurance, interface instability, and leakage current, which collectively compromise device performance and reliability. This review provides a systematic overview of the ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties of AlScN with underlying physical mechanisms, highlights the challenges in material growth and device integration, and summarizes recent advances of emerging applications in piezoelectric devices, optoelectronic devices, ferroelectric memories, and high‐electron‐mobility transistors (HEMTs). Finally, perspectives are presented on future research directions, focusing on overcoming key barriers to device implementation. With ongoing advances in material optimization and system‐level integration, AlScN presents broad prospects for energy‐efficient computing and sensing hardware, accelerating the development of artificial intelligence (AI).
n5b0d605e0c61: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a multifactorial degenerative joint disease characterized by irreversible cartilage deterioration associated with chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, tissue acidosis, and abnormal mechanical loading. During OA progression, inflammation‐associated metabolic reprogramming and hypoxia‐enhanced glycolysis promote lactate accumulation and local acidosis. OA‐associated acidosis may function as an exacerbating factor within this pathological microenvironment by engaging acid‐sensing pathways and contributing to chondrocyte senescence, apoptosis, and SASP‐associated inflammatory amplification, thereby exacerbating cartilage degeneration. Accordingly, therapeutic strategies that actively neutralize pathological acidity while concurrently modulating inflammatory and oxidative stress cascades may provide a more robust, disease‐modifying approach for OA intervention. Herein, we designed a nanoreactor termed OLDH‐DP@POM by integrating mildly alkaline layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanosheets with active acid‐neutralizing capability and anchoring polyoxometalates (POM) with antioxidant activity, thereby enabling coordinated regulation of pathological acidosis and oxidative stress. Meanwhile, lubrication‐enhancing zwitterionic poly(2‐methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine) (PMPC) polymer brushes were grafted, endowing the nanoreactor with superior joint lubrication and chondroprotective capability. Both in vitro and in vivo results demonstrated that OLDH‐DP@POM effectively neutralized local acidosis at osteoarthritic lesions, substantially ameliorated synovial inflammation, suppressed Piezo‐mediated mechanotransduction, delayed chondrocyte senescence, and ultimately attenuated cartilage degeneration. Overall, this work provides a promising nanotherapeutic platform for disease‐modifying treatment of OA.
ncdcb9062b087: Designing two-dimensional (2D) materials from atomically precise nanocluster building blocks is a challenging task, yet crucial for next-generation electronic devices. By tuning cluster nuclearity and ligand environment, well-defined assemblies can be designed, enabling control over optoelectronic properties at the atomic level. Herein, we report the bottom-up synthesis of two structurally distinct 2D nanocluster-assembled materials constructed from Ag12 (2D Ag12-CAM) and Ag11 (2D Ag11-CAM) nanocluster building blocks. The change in cluster nuclearity arises solely from ligand tuning; benzenethiol yields the Ag12-based framework, whereas 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzenethiol (BTFMBT) directs formation of the Ag11 analogue. Lateral memristive devices fabricated from these materials (D-1: 2D Ag12-CAM; D-2: 2D Ag11-CAM) exhibit coexistence of negative differential resistance (NDR) and robust resistive switching with endurance stable over 4000 switching cycles. Device D-2, based on 2D Ag11-CAM, shows a markedly enhanced on-off (I on/I off) ratio (∼ 642) compared to device D-1 (∼ 200), and more pronounced NDR. Furthermore, the 2D Ag11-CAM (D-2)-based device was evaluated for neuromorphic functionality, mimicking the adaptive behavior of biological synapses. It exhibits analogue potentiation and depression under pulse stimulation, while experimentally extracted synaptic weight updates enable an artificial neural network to achieve a test accuracy of 84.2%, approaching that of a machine learning (ML)-trained network (93.2%).
n4ccac956fd53: Bifunctional electrocatalysts that simultaneously drive CO2 reduction (CO2RR) and oxygen evolution (OER) in neutral electrolytes are essential for aqueous Zn‐CO2 batteries (AZCBs), but conventional designs prioritize CO2RR and are often incompatible with OER, resulting in low energy efficiency, poor reversibility, and rapid degradation of batteries. Here, we introduce a unified catalyst architecture integrating Cu and Ni single atoms with boron‐, nitrogen‐co‐doped carbon (CuNi@BNC‐T). Heteroatom co‐doping stabilizes high single‐atom loadings, enhances metal‐support interactions, and suppresses carbon corrosion, while N‐coordinated Cu+ and Ni3+ sites cooperatively boost CO2RR‐OER, enabling ethanol formation and low‐overpotential OER. This strategy achieves a 0.7 V voltage gap at 5 mA cm−2, 522 h cycling at 20 mA cm−2, and first ethanol production via AZCBs with energy efficiency of 88% (flow‐cell). By elucidating previously unresolved degradation pathways, this work also correlates catalyst dynamics with battery failure, establishing design principles for durable bifunctional catalysts in aqueous Zn‐CO2 systems.
nd6e55a3132e3: Emergency hemostasis during prehospital care significantly reduces trauma‐related mortality. Nanoclay exhibits potent procoagulant properties, but its detachment from the substrate leads to non‐negligible adverse reactions and diminished hemostatic efficiency, hindering its clinical application. Despite improved immobilization via polymer incorporation, irreversible surface encapsulation undermines the procoagulant efficacy of nanoclays. Here, inspired by the anchoring mechanism of fish scales to skin via collagen fibers, we introduce a nanofiber‐bridged design that enables robust immobilization of nanoclay and maximized loading density, while also achieving its full exposure for optimal hemostatic performance. The microfiber‐derived nanofiber network expands the interfacial contact area and anchors nanosheet inner surfaces via synergistic covalent and non‐covalent interactions, effectively redistributing stress to resist dynamic shear forces. The resulting kaolin‐cotton hemostatic dressing demonstrates superior physical stability (no detectable kaolin leakage) and enhanced hemostatic efficacy in rat (62%), rabbit (58%), and pig (35%–43%) hemorrhage models compared with conventional hemostatic agents. Importantly, no leakage‐induced chronic inflammation was observed. Moreover, laboratory‐scale preparation and processing of 5 kg products demonstrate the feasibility of industrial‐scale production, making them further processable into various cotton‐based materials. This bioinspired dressing offers improved efficacy and safety, along with affordability, underscoring its potential for clinical translation.
n0e6592222268: Nonuniform sodium deposition limits the cyclability of anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs), and current research mainly focuses on anode-targeted strategies. However, the influence of the cathode kinetics on sodium deposition behavior has been overlooked. Here, we firstly reveal the critical role of cathode polarization on sodium deposition uniformity via electric field coupling. Accordingly, cathode-specific charging (CSC) protocols are established for AFSBs to depolarize the cathode, where the charging current is dynamically regulated based on the state of charge (SOC)-dependent direct current inner resistance (DCIR). As expected, the CSC protocols effectively depolarize the cathodes and thus homogenize sodium deposition on the anode. Impressively, a 1.6 Ah Al/C||NFPP pouch cell reaches a record-high cyclability of 1370 cycles at 2 C, and a 3.6 Ah pouch cell reaches a high energy density of 180 Wh kg− 1 with stable cycling for 890 cycles at 0.5 C. More importantly, the cathode depolarization strategy shows application universality for diverse anode-free full cells based on Na4Fe3(PO4)2 (NFPP), Na3V2(PO4)3 (NVP), and NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM) cathodes. This work opens an avenue for fabricating durable practical AFSBs.
n26fb167361c7: Thermal conductivity is one of the fundamental manifestations of how the underlying atomic arrangement in materials facilitates heat flow. The critical role of thermal conductivity in influencing the performance of materials in the energy and quantum technologies arena makes engineering it to match functionality a crucial challenge to address. Here, we focus on intrinsically tuning thermal transport in inorganic crystalline solids through the strategic design of crystal structures. As structure is determined by the underlying chemical bonding, light is also shed on the influence of chemical bonding on thermal transport, including the concept of multicentered bonding and the role of antibonding states. In this review, we distill global research efforts into key design features rooted in chemical bonding and structural principles that enable an intrinsic property‐based descriptor‐framework for the purposeful manipulation of thermal conductivity in inorganic solids. We survey examples in which lattice thermal conductivity of crystalline solids has been pushed to extremes, specifically toward the diffusion limit or even rendered glassy. The broad and significant applicability of these principles across functional materials such as thermoelectrics, superionic conductors, ferroelectrics and halide perovskites is thus demonstrated. Finally, we explore emerging directions in the field, including topological phonons, thermotronics, and the phonon wave‐particle crossover, alongside the impact of artificial intelligence and machine learning on materials discovery.
n22b86b29462d: Artificial photosynthesis technology holds great promise for sustainable energy conversion and value‐added chemical synthesis, yet integrating efficient light absorption with high product selectivity remains a major challenge. This study constructs an Ni‐La2O3/La2NiO4 catalyst through in situ perovskite derivation that mechanistically and functionally mimics the chloroplast for artificial photosynthesis by coupling photo and photothermal catalysis with the integration of broad‐spectrum light harvesting, directional charge transfer, as well as CO2 adsorption and hydrogenation. Three functional interfaces are formed: La2O3‐La2NiO4 (Z‐scheme), Ni‐La2NiO4 (Schottky junction), and La2O3(adsorption)‐Ni(activation). The two heterojunctions facilitate electron transfer to metallic Ni nanoparticles, which activates H+ to form an NADPH‐like surface Ni‐H species by enabling the collection of photo and photothermal generated electrons. Meanwhile, the Lewis‐basic La2O3 captures CO2 and promotes its activation at the La2O3‐Ni interface. In CO2‐to‐CH4 conversion, Ni‐La2O3/La2NiO4 demonstrates an exceptional CH4 production rate of 9.96 µmol h−1 g−1 and a selectivity of 92.5% under natural conditions (i.e., AM 1.5 irradiation, ambient temperature, and atmospheric pressure) without external assistance, which outperforms pure La2NiO4 by 10.2 and 4.6 times, respectively. This work advances a new strategy for efficient solar‐to‐fuel conversion.
nc1105fddef5e: Conventional self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) are conformationally rigid. They cannot buffer interfacial strain during rapid perovskite crystallization, limiting both film quality and device stability. We introduce a conformational engineering strategy using 2‐benzhydrylidene‐succinic acid (BSA), a rigid diphenylmethylene anchor with flexible succinic acid chains to create an elastic buried interface. Atomic simulations show BSA acts as a compressible buffer, delaying stress accumulation by ∼6 Å under displacement. This dynamic strain dissipation improves heterojunction contact and enhances hole extraction and transport. BSA‐modified p‐i‐n devices reach 26.89% (0.045 cm2, certified 26.52%). Large‐area modules (22.95 cm2) deliver 24.30% (certified 23.95%), which is among the highest certified values for this area. The devices retain 90% of initial efficiency after 316 h of diurnal cycling and 88% after 300 extreme transient thermal shock cycles from ‐20 °C to 100 °C. This conformational design integrates mechanical compliance with electronic functionality in scalable perovskite photovoltaics.
na2dbf3dff9bf: Particle packing in battery electrodes is pivotal to the fast‐charging performance of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, precise control of particle packing structure remains a major challenge in electrode fabrication, primarily owing to the absence of robust interfacial bonding between micron‐scale particles. Herein, we propose a novel layer‐by‐layer single‐layer particle assembly technique to fabricate electrodes with well‐defined particle packing structures. Using this approach, we prepared a 12‐meter‐long graphite (Gr)/hard carbon (HC) hybrid anode featuring a body‐centered cubic (BCC)‐like structure, which maximizes intimate Gr/HC contact interfaces and facilitates solid‐state Li+ transport. Coupled with LiFePO4 (LFP) cathodes, the as‐fabricated anode exhibits a high‐capacity retention of 80.7% after 1650 cycles at 4C. From an electrode design standpoint, this controllable particle‐packing strategy paves the way for a universal framework for developing sustainable, long‐cycling, and fast‐charging electrodes, potentially applicable to many types of battery anodes and cathodes.

ne667dcdb9bfb: Sulfur-assisted oxidative coupling of methane (SOCM) provides a direct route for methane conversion to ethylene over transition-metal sulfides (TMSs), with sulfur-rich surface environments involved in methane activation and ethylene formation....
n987d1ceb5bfc: Identical-location electron microscopy enables particle-resolved tracking of structural evolution, providing deep insights into catalyst stability and the structure–function relationship beyond what ensemble-averaged analysis can offer.
nc2b183cdb892: Electrocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction reaction to high-value multicarbon products represents a highly promising strategy for achieving carbon neutrality goals. Among various electrocatalysts, copper-based materials occupy a central position due to their unique capability for *CO adsorption and dimerization; however, they still face severe challenges, including high overpotentials and limited product selectivity. Orbital engineering, particularly the construction of p-d bimetallic systems through the introduction of p-block metals, has emerged as a pivotal approach to surmounting the performance bottlenecks of Cu-based catalysts. This review systematically summarizes the recent research progress in copper-based p-d bimetallic catalysts designed via orbital engineering for efficient CO2 reduction reaction. We provide an in-depth discussion on the modulation mechanisms of p-block metals on the performance of Cu active centers from three key dimensions: electronic effects, geometric effects, and microenvironment regulation. Furthermore, we summarize the primary challenges currently facing the field of p-d orbital matching and offer perspectives on the rational design of future CO2 reduction catalytic systems that possess high activity, stability, and energy efficiency, aiming to provide theoretical guidance and practical insights for the large-scale application of green energy conversion technologies.
ne4de33ef25b8: Conventional elastomer networks can provide mechanical stability but offer limited capacity for network rearrangement and reprocessing. In this work, a sulfur-rich oligomeric crosslinker (S-VBGE) was introduced into epoxidized natural rubber (ENR) to construct a filler-free dual-dynamic network containing reversible hydrogen-bonding associations and sulfur-containing dynamic structures. The optimized ENR-SV15 formulation reached a tensile strength of 14.84 MPa and a toughness of 85.07 MJ·m−3. Based on three independent fatigue crack growth measurements, its apparent fatigue threshold was 310 ± 14 J·m−2, compared with 41 ± 1 J·m−2 for ENR-0. Temperature-dependent stress relaxation and reprocessing experiments indicate thermally activated network rearrangement, while variable-temperature FTIR supports the thermal responsiveness of the hydrogen-bonding associations. Together, these results show that balancing reversible associations, sulfur-containing dynamic structures, and network constraints can improve crack growth resistance while retaining solid-state reprocessability in dry ENR elastomers.
n7ce8d9e34583: Interfacial reactions at the electrolyte/Zn anode critically influence the reversibility and cycling stability of aqueous Zn-ion batteries (AZIBs). Here, we employ an in operando electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring (E-QCMD) to investigate the dynamics of Zn deposition/dissolution in three representative ZnSO4, Zn(OTf)2, and Zn(ClO4)2 electrolytes at concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 M. Using a three-electrode configuration under a constant overpotential of ± 100 mV, current density, mass change, and dissipation were simultaneously monitored in real time. A comparison between the measured mass change (ΔMf) and the theoretical Faradaic mass (ΔMq) reveals that both electrolyte anion identity and concentration strongly affect Zn redox behavior. Zn(ClO4)2 promotes the formation of rigid, highly reversible Zn deposits, although accompanied by hydrogen evolution, whereas concentrated Zn(OTf)2 forms viscoelastic interfacial layers, consistent with the accumulation of alkaline byproducts and the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). ZnSO4 exhibits intermediate behavior with improved reversibility at higher concentrations. Complementary analyses of Coulombic efficiency and mass-per-electron (MPE) further show that concentrated Zn(ClO4)2 and ZnSO4 electrolytes provide more reversible Zn deposition/dissolution than Zn(OTf)2. Ex situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations corroborate this picture by resolving the anion-dependent interphase chemistry and the underlying solvation and hydrogen-bond structures, respectively. These findings provide mechanistic insights into electrolyte-dependent Zn interfacial chemistry and demonstrate the capability of in operando E-QCMD for elucidating Zn redox processes in AZIBs.
n903958ec794a: The development of near-infrared (NIR) organic lasers has long been constrained by inefficient excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) and limited electronic delocalization, which restrict both performance and scalability. In this study, we demonstrate that subtle molecular modifications can improve laser properties. By introducing a π-bridge-enhanced donor-π-acceptor (D-π-A) architecture in the molecule MDS-DHAQ, we improve molecular planarity and extend π-conjugation. This strategic adjustment is associated with predominantly K*-type emission, consistent with an ESIPT-based four-level lasing scheme. Through self-assembly, MDS-DHAQ molecules spontaneously form well-ordered micro/nanocrystals that serve as the gain medium and resonant cavity for lasing. These self-assembled crystals exhibit single-mode lasing at 940 nm, with a low threshold of 3.8 μJ cm−2 and a linewidth of approximately 0.37 nm. Furthermore, they show a 10% reduction in lasing intensity after 10,000 pump pulses. This work highlights how molecular alterations can tune the physical properties of materials, offering an approach that integrates molecular engineering and self-assembly. The resulting NIR organic lasers have potential applications in integrated photonics and optoelectronics.
n5c6b50385098: Reversible lithium intercalation in layered transition metal oxides is often accompanied by irreversible phase transformation, setting fundamental limits on the capacity and longevity achievable in lithium-ion batteries. Here, we engineer...

n0dcc5fba13cd: Optimizing the LSTC defect-adaptive oxide catalyst to 45 µm balances NH 3 diffusion and H 2 release, delivering a record peak power density of 0.753 W cm −2 and 200 h stability at 650 °C for direct ammonia protonic ceramic fuel cells.
nb8517e4e6f55: Ferroelastic switching enables nonvolatile reorientation of piezoelectric and optoelectronic anisotropies in Janus TP/HP ScS 2 M (M = P, As, Sb), offering opportunities for vector sensing, memory, and strain-tunable photocatalytic water splitting.
n8ed4596c0e1e: MECA integrates transient nuclear deformation with multi-omics-guided selection of CRISPRa target loci to enhance endogenous gene activation and enable efficient, programmable cell-fate engineering.
ne2eea2301a87: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains difficult to treat because of tumor heterogeneity and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Although combining chemotherapy with cuproptosis offers complementary antitumor effects, its efficacy is constrained by poor tumor-selective delivery and ATP7B-associated copper efflux. We developed YC@BS-MOF, a yuanhuacine (YC)-loaded copper metal–organic framework (MOF) with Golgi-targeting capability, to integrate chemotherapy, photodynamic therapy, and cuproptosis. Composed of Cu2+ nodes and Golgi-targeting BS-TCPP photosensitizing ligands, BS-MOF acted as a copper reservoir and, upon light irradiation, induced Golgi disruption that impaired ATP7B-associated Cu handling and promoted intracellular copper retention. Copper retention amplified YC-mediated apoptosis and copper-dependent oxidative stress, leading to enhanced cuproptosis, immunogenic cell death, and activation of the immune microenvironment. Biodistribution analyses showed increased YC tumor accumulation, and in vivo studies demonstrated potent tumor suppression, immune remodeling, and favorable biosafety. This work establishes Golgi-directed regulation of copper trafficking as a subcellular strategy to potentiate chemo–cuproptosis for CRC treatment.
nb037cd1707b1: Patternable liquid metal particle (LMP) conductors with stable performance under deformation are highly desirable for wearable electronics but remain limited by activation-dependent conductivity and structural instability. Here, we report an activation-free conductive ink based on nickel-coated carbon nanotubes (NiCNTs) and nanoscale LMPs. A solvent-mediated stabilization strategy suppresses droplet coalescence, yielding uniformly dispersed and stable LMPs. Strong interfacial coupling enabled by hydrogen-bond-assisted adsorption and Ni–Ga alloying promotes the formation of a dynamically reconfigurable “island-bridge” network, where conductive LMP domains are interconnected by compliant NiCNT bridges. This architecture achieves high electrical conductivity (5.9 × 105 S m–1) without external activation and maintains excellent electromechanical stability (4.6 × 105 S m–1 at 100% strain) and printability on various soft substrates. Printed epidermal electrodes enable low-impedance electrocardiogram monitoring over 7 days and support machine-learning-assisted activity recognition with accuracies above 99%, providing a general strategy for intrinsically conductive and mechanically resilient soft electronics.
nc157d9b907c8: Engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising therapeutic carriers for cancer treatment, but preserving intrinsic therapeutic activity while incorporating multiple immunomodulatory functions remains a challenge. Here, we developed a modular engineering strategy that combines the genetic engineering of EV-producing cells with bioorthogonal click chemistry to construct multifunctional oncolytic extracellular vesicles (OEVs). Azide-functionalized OEVs were generated from CD40L-expressing cells infected with a capsid-engineered oncolytic adenovirus. A toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) agonist was subsequently conjugated to the OEV surface through click chemistry, integrating immune stimulation while retaining the oncolytic activity. The engineered OEVs efficiently infected tumor cells, induced antigen-presenting cell activation, enhanced intratumoral CD8+ T-cell responses, promoted B-cell activation and tumor-specific antibody production, and improved the therapeutic efficacy of the immune checkpoint blockade. These findings demonstrated that combining genetic engineering with bioorthogonal chemistry provided a strategy for constructing multifunctional oncolytic EVs with coordinated cytotoxic and immunomodulatory activities, offering an approach to next-generation cancer immunotherapies.
n0365ea73fa24: Controlling the energy scales of a quantum system is essential for defining robust qubits. In silicon, the nearly degenerate conduction-band valleys create a leakage channel from the single-spin computational basis. Here, we perform spectroscopic measurements of single- and two-electron states in buried silicon quantum wells. Across a linear array of four quantum dots with an average orbital energy of 2.4(2) meV, we report an average single-electron valley splitting of 0.40(6) meV and an average two-electron singlet–triplet splitting of 0.24(7) meV. In three dots, we observe a strong correlation between valley splitting and orbital energy, with an average linear coefficient of ≈0.22 (meV/meV). In contrast, the remaining dot exhibits the highest valley splitting of 0.76(2) meV and low correlation. Our findings show that strong confinement can effectively enhance valley splitting in buried quantum wells, thereby establishing a viable path toward shuttling and sparse-occupation-based architectures in low-disorder heterostructures.
ncc0cc87dcf84: Ti3C2Tx MXene is widely employed in energy storage because of its unique interfacial charge-storage properties. Understanding its intrinsic capacitive properties, especially the surface characteristics of a monolayer flake, is critical to optimizing device performance, but direct measurement at the monolayer level remains elusive. Here, we report, for the first time, direct experimental quantification of the intrinsic capacitance of monolayer Ti3C2Tx MXene by integrating optimized flake protection and parasitic-capacitance-shielding strategies. The quasi-static areal capacitance is 141 μF cm–2 in acidic electrolytes and 61–74 μF cm–2 in alkali-metal-ion electrolytes. Decoupling the pseudocapacitive and electric-double-layer contributions by resolving the concentration dependence reveals that pseudocapacitance accounts for ∼45% of the total in acidic electrolytes but <10% in alkali-metal-ion electrolytes. Temperature-dependent kinetics show that a lower proton-transfer activation energy facilitates the pseudocapacitive charge storage. This work quantifies how redox and double-layer mechanisms coexist on a monolayer Ti3C2Tx MXene surface and establishes a benchmark across the field.
n6de2b53e5f7a: The proliferation of spent lithium-ion batteries demands efficient, environmentally sustainable recycling technologies, yet regenerating spent cathode materials remains challenging. Here, we present a mild, scalable direct regeneration strategy for spent LiFePO4 (S-LFP) cathodes leveraging the synergistic effect of ethanolamine and LiNO3. Ethanolamine with moderate alkalinity and strong reducing capability gently removes surface passivation layers and amorphous impurities, selectively reducing Fe(III) to Fe(II) for lattice-stabilized valence balance. Thanks to its low steric hindrance and favorable mass-transport properties, it penetrates particle interiors and cooperates with Li+ from LiNO3 to fill Li vacancies, eliminating Li–Fe antisite defects and repairing distorted lattices. During subsequent annealing, ethanolamine acts as an in situ N source to form a uniform N-doped interfacial layer that suppresses side reactions and boosts charge-transfer kinetics. Regenerated LiFePO4 (R-LFP) achieves 106.04 mAh g–1 at 5.0 C with 100% capacity retention over 500 cycles. EverBatt-based assessments confirm its favorable economic and environmental benefits.
n7de30920fc86: Metal–organic frameworks offer powerful platforms for intracellular delivery and tissue regeneration, yet their membrane-level interactions are poorly defined. Here, we show that cationic zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF8) remodels the electrostatic landscape of the anionic plasma membrane, triggering caveolae-dependent endocytosis and promoting the intracellular delivery for bone regeneration. ζ-potential analysis and Kelvin probe force microscopy demonstrated that ZIF8 rapidly increased membrane surface electrostatics and induced localized electrostatic polarization at the nanobio interface. Simulations and adsorption kinetics revealed rapid saturation and a strong pH dependence, supporting a charge-dominated adsorption mechanism. Transmission electron microscopy captured sequential uptake events, including caveolae formation, membrane invagination, and lysosomal trafficking. Transcriptomics further identified CAV2-associated endocytosis and mechanosensitive fluid shear-stress pathways as key contributors. On the basis of this mechanism, we constructed an OGP-loaded ZIF8 coating on polyethyleneimine-functionalized titanium implants, enabling intracellular peptide delivery, partial lysosomal escape, enhanced osteogenesis, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory responses, and improved osseointegration in rat bone defect models.
nf69e6e333187: Metal–sulfur batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage, yet the origins of their distinct reaction behaviors remain elusive. Here, we employ a noncatalytic vapor-grown carbon fibers/sulfur (VGCF/S) interface to regulate sulfur electrochemistry. In situ TEM reveals highly reversible two-step redox reactions and rapid reaction-front propagation in Li–S nanobatteries. Coin-cell measurements further show reversible cycling and rate capability for Li–S under specific testing conditions. DFT calculations in idealized graphitic and sulfur–carbon environments provide a qualitative comparison of alkali-species-dependent migration. The observed divergence may reflect coupled contributions from alkali-species transport, interfacial processes, electrolyte-dependent sulfur-redox pathways, and product evolution. This work highlights noncatalytic interfaces as a platform for probing sulfur electrochemistry.
n92a18ff81ca0: The pH-responsive two-dimensional nanofiltration membranes enable tunable separation, yet existing membranes suffer from weak charge gating. Herein, we prepared a mica–polyethylenimine membrane using a “coupled charge flip” strategy. The membrane exhibits a strong charge flip (zeta potential from +46.1 to −36.4 mV) across pH 2–12, originating from the synergy between polyethylenimine (zeta potential from +35.2 to +2.5 mV) and mica (zeta potential from −3.1 to −55.7 mV), yielding a charge-flip amplitude (82.5 mV) 41% greater than that of the best performing bipolar pH-responsive membranes. This enables superior pH-dependent molecular gating (e.g., methyl orange) with rejection ranging from 96.98 to 5.03% (pH 2–12) and a gating ratio of 19.28, which is 1.76 times that of the best reported pH-responsive membranes, while maintaining a water permeance of 155 L m–2 h–1 bar–1 and stable cycling over eight pH switches. This work provides a new framework for designing pH-responsive nanofiltration membranes with high gating ratios.
n8e69287f69e9: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion in heavy metal | ferromagnet heterostructures are compact, broadband THz sources with bandwidths exceeding conventional semiconductor-based emitters. However, achievable current amplitudes per unit area are fundamentally limited by spin-current transport across a single heavy metal | ferromagnet interface. Here, we demonstrate a multilayer spintronic THz emitter architecture comprising repeated heavy metal | ferromagnet bilayers separated by ultrathin MgO barriers, enabling constructive addition of generated charge currents. Using GHz-bandwidth electrical sampling and THz-bandwidth electro-optic sampling, we observe monotonic amplitude enhancement with increasing layer number. This scaling behavior is quantitatively captured by a model incorporating optical absorption and impedance matching effects. Finally, by integrating multilayer emitters into coplanar waveguide structures, we demonstrate on-chip THz current generation and propagation. These results establish multilayer spintronic THz emitters as a scalable platform for ultrafast current generation and integrated on-chip THz electronics.
n2f2cbc367b01: We present PtyRANNOSAUR, a data-driven neural network approach that reconstructs atomic-resolution electron ptychography data in seconds, 100–1000 times faster than iterative methods. PtyRANNOSAUR uses convolutional autoencoders to map 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy data to 2D phase images. Each model is trained on a large database of crystal structures and is tailored for a range of experimental parameters, such as accelerating voltage, convergence angle, defocus, and sample thickness. This approach yields high-quality reconstructions without requiring any fine-tuning of hyperparameters, significantly increasing the accessibility and usability of electron ptychography. In addition, the code handles spatial partial coherence, multiple scattering, and scan position errors, which are critical for the highest-quality electron ptychography reconstructions but have not been available without hours-long computations. By testing PtyRANNOSAUR on experimental and simulated data, we show that the neural networks accurately reconstruct atomic structures on a broad range of systems of materials and achieve high spatial resolutions of <0.5 Å, comparable to the best iterative reconstructions of the same data. These advances enable live, easy-to-use, state-of-the-art electron ptychography reconstructions. These features make it possible to conduct hundreds of electron ptychography reconstructions in minutes and should unlock new operational modes for nanocharacterization, such as in situ and high-throughput electron ptychography.
n4eefed355d25: Superconducting qubit fabrication innovations continue to be explored to achieve higher performance. Despite improvements to base layer fabrication and processing, resist-based Josephson junction (JJ) schemes have largely remained unchanged. The polymer mask during deposition causes chemical contamination and limits in situ and ex situ surface preparation, junction materials, and scalability. Here, we demonstrate a resist-free approach to junction fabrication based on etched silicon trenches that is compatible with standard silicon microfabrication processes and easily integrated into existing innovations in qubit base layer fabrication and chemical processing. We fabricate Al-AlOx-Al JJs and qubits using this method, measuring median energy relaxation times up to 188 μs. We find minimal contamination at the substrate–metal interface and fluctuations of energy relaxation on a 45 h time scale that are narrow and normally distributed. The method widens the process window for substrate preparation and new materials platforms.
n372635d0e536: Tip-enhanced photoluminescence in scanning tunneling microscopy nanocavities has emerged as a powerful tool to probe intermolecular electronic energy transfer (EET) at the single-molecule level. Single-atom modifications at a metallic tip apex can drastically alter the near-field, yet their quantitative impact on intermolecular EET has remained elusive. By exploiting a multiscale fully atomistic quantum mechanical (QM)/electrodynamical approach, we show a nontrivial modulation of the EET-driven fluorescence, jointly determined by the atomistic morphology and single-atom features of the silver tip apex. Remarkably, we demonstrate that a fully atomistic QM/Classical description, able to treat systems of more than ten thousand atoms, is essential to capture how subtle apex rearrangements affect intermolecular EET. Our results quantitatively reproduce experimental fluorescence spectra and Förster-type distance behaviors, providing a direct structure–property connection at the atomistic level, crucial for predictive simulations of tip-enhanced spectroscopies.
n8e33ce4437ed: The spin Hall effect, a key effect in creating spin currents and controlling magnetic order at the nanoscale, presupposes a population of mobile carriers in a conducting state, in which a driving charge current generates a perpendicular spin-current. Here we show an ultrafast light-wave driven spin Hall analogue exists in altermagnetic semiconductors and insulators, in which a laser pulse generates both a charge current and a co-occurring perpendicular pure spin current. Employing the example of the theoretically predicted 2d altermagnetic Lieb-lattice semiconductor Cr2SO, we demonstrate that pulse design allows lightwave control over the postpulse spin/charge current ratio ξres, with values exceeding unity obtained in the multicycle regime. Our findings thus both considerably broaden the materials base for spin Hall/spin splitter physics, as well as establishing 2d altermagnets as a platform providing a new route for valleytronic lightwave control of spin- and charge currents at ultrafast times.
nfca1b8bbea1e: Introducing tensile strain into copper-based (Cu-based) catalysts is a promising strategy for improving the performance of the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). However, isolating the influence of the strain effect remains challenging owing to the convoluted contributions from grain boundaries, ligands, and facets. Herein, we utilize in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) to isolate the effect of strain on the CO2RR performance and determine the strain–activity correlations by taking advantage of synthesizing colloidal nanoparticles with well-defined structures. Tensile strain is shown to modulate CO2RR performance by tuning the CO binding strength of the Cu-based catalysts. Medium tensile strain leads to moderate CO adsorption, which is beneficial for the formation of multicarbon products. Excessively strong CO adsorption would instead hinder the CO2RR and promote the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work provides experimental evidence for the rational design of high-performance CO2RR catalysts to produce C2+ products via strain engineering.
n40179a89b536: Carbonate precipitation at the cathode caused by local alkalinity during electrocatalytic CO2 reduction represents a major limitation to carbon efficiency and system durability. Now local heating induced in ferromagnetic high-entropy alloys by an alternating magnetic field reduces carbonate precipitation, extending durability in alkaline and neutral electrolytes.
n918aab8bc949: Understanding interfacial processes is important for achieving efficient CO2 electrolysis at high current densities. Now, two-dimensional correlated operando Raman spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics provide insight into the relationship between interfacial species, water structure and product selectivity under application-relevant conditions, revealing the role of water in regulating CO2 availability at the electrode–electrolyte interface.
nd2ca4f0d72d7: This study models how heatwaves raise demand and reduce generation and transmission capacity across Western European power grids, showing how heatwaves can expose bottlenecks that simplified models may miss and providing a basis for resilience planning.
n9de0e00551bb: The high ring strain of cyclic hydrocarbons enables alternating copolymerization with carbon dioxide to produce polyesters amenable to closed-loop recycling.
n55fe2a93b2a0: Ferrimagnetic nanostructures with low spin-wave damping are used to demonstrate the reprogrammable routing of spin-wave signals across a wide range of frequencies.
n6d96ff4ab2b3: A reticular coordination strategy is developed in which coordinating one Pt atom per Ce-oxo cluster in a metal–organic framework before calcination yields ceria containing 14.9 wt% atomically dispersed Pt. The resulting lattice confinement inhibits migration and suppresses sintering under harsh reducing conditions.
nf8700478bd76: Enantiopure α-stereogenic ketones constitute prevalent scaffolds in numerous natural products and pharmaceuticals while also serving as versatile and valuable building blocks for diverse synthetic transformations. Conventional methods for constructing chiral α-stereogenic ketones typically rely on the reaction of ketone enolates or enamines with electrophiles. However, the need for strong bases to generate these intermediates often limits the substrate scope. Additionally, achieving stereo- and regioselective formation of enolates or enamines from unsymmetrical dialkyl ketones remains a significant challenge. This review provides an overview of recent advances in the enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones, highlighting emerging strategies beyond classical chemistry, such as radical reactions, nucleophilic reactions, acyl–nickel-enabled cross-coupling, and enzyme-catalyzed dehalogenation.
ne738e7d14c2d: Carbonyl α-C(sp3)–H functionalization is a key approach to access functionalized pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and bioactive peptides. Conventional two-electron enol tautomerization strategies for this transformation often suffer from harsh reaction conditions and limited substrate tolerance. While valence tautomerism (VT) enables radical-type C–H activation, such reactivity has been exclusively realized with nickel catalysis, and copper-mediated VT remains unexplored for α-C(sp3)–H activation of carbonyls. Here, we present a dual photoredox/copper catalytic strategy that exploits copper-mediated VT to generate α-carbonyl alkyl radicals. These radicals undergo radical–radical cross-coupling with nucleophilic radicals generated by photocatalytic decarboxylation, delivering α-carbonyl alkylation products. The protocol features mild conditions and broad functional group tolerance, supporting peptide late-stage modification and gram-scale synthesis. Mechanistic studies and density functional theory (DFT) calculations validate a Cu(III)-mediated VT pathway for radical generation. This work establishes copper as a viable VT catalytic platform, expands the scope of dual photoredox/metal catalysis, and offers a versatile tool for biomolecular derivatization.
n0463ac656c42: Breaking the pervasive activity–selectivity–stability trade-off in catalytic hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a bifunctional nanoisland catalyst (GaNPs-Pt/Beta) that overcomes this limitation by utilizing liquid gallium nanodroplets anchored on Beta zeolite as mobile nanoislands. These islands effectively restrict platinum single-atom migration and agglomeration. Concurrently, Brønsted acid sites provided by the zeolite sea facilitate the dehydration-etherification process. This synergy enables highly efficient transfer hydrogenation at the gallium–platinum interface, achieving selective C–O bond cleavage while preserving C═C bonds under mild conditions. Benefiting from this island-sea architecture, the GaNPs-Pt/Beta catalyst delivers high catalytic activity, achieving >99% cinnamyl alcohol conversion and 93.8% β-methylstyrene selectivity within 6 h at 160 °C, with recyclability demonstrated over nine cycles involving intercycle regeneration. This strategy is scalable to diverse α,β-unsaturated aldehyde/alcohol chemicals, demonstrating that zeolite-based liquid metal nanoislands provide a versatile platform for the sustainable synthesis of high-value chemicals.
n3ad4eb073ecb: Enantioselective hydrosilylation of alkenes represents a direct and economical route to chiral organosilanes. However, achieving good regio- and enantioselectivity from the same alkene for the divergent synthesis of chiral silanes remains a formidable challenge, particularly for internal alkenes. In this work, we present a ligand-controlled nickel-catalyzed regiodivergent and enantioselective hydrosilylation of 1,2-disubstituted alkenes. This approach provides a direct access to both α- and β-trifluoromethylsilanes with high regio- and enantioselectivity. The resulting enantioenriched silane products are amenable to various stereospecific transformations. Moreover, density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate the origin of the observed regio- and enantioselectivity.
n12e8064668fb: Catalytic enantioselective alkylation is a fundamental strategy for constructing molecular frameworks bearing chiral carbon centers. Herein, we report a photoinduced highly enantioselective catalytic α-alkylation of active methine compounds with nonactivated alkenes to construct chiral quaternary stereocenters. Cooperative catalysis using an organophotocatalyst and a chiral ytterbium Lewis acid bearing an Indapybox ligand efficiently promotes the alkylation of open-chain 2-substituted β-ketoesters, affording the desired products in high yields with high enantioselectivities (up to 96% yield and 96% ee). The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope with respect to both the alkene and β-ketoesters components. Furthermore, the resulting products can be readily transformed into optically active 5-pyrazolone and 5-isoxazolone derivatives while maintaining high optical purity.
n92c2548e3702: Acidic CO2 electroreduction offers a promising route to improve carbon utilization compared with alkaline or neutral systems. However, maintaining high product selectivity at industrially relevant current densities remains challenging because local CO2 depletion and excessive proton availability intensify the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we develop a bismuth sulfide (Bi2S3) catalyst modified with a long-chain imidazolium poly(ionic liquid) layer (PIL@BS) for electrocatalytic CO2-to-formic acid conversion at pH 2. In a flow cell containing 3 M KCl, PIL@BS catalyst delivers a high Faradaic efficiency for formic acid (FEFA = 98.4%) at a current density exceeding 300 mA cm–2 and maintains over 80% FEFA after 120 h of continuous operation. Even at low 15 vol % CO2 concentration typical of industrial flue gas, PIL@BS retains higher FA selectivity than unmodified BS, underscoring the effectiveness of PIL in suppressing HER under CO2-limited conditions. Structural characterizations and electrochemical analyses reveal that the PIL backbone creates a hydrophobic interface while preserving CO2 affinity and high ionic conductivity, effectively mitigating the flooding issues and enhancing the local availability of CO2. Operando spectroscopies further show that PIL-regulated interface facilitates access to weakly hydrogen-bonded water. Such interfacial water reorganization disrupts the extended hydrogen-bond network, attenuating the continuous proton-relay pathways that promote the competing HER while maintaining localized proton transfer for CO2 reduction. Combined with theoretical calculations, these findings indicate that the PIL-modified microenvironment enables a direct and energetically favorable hydrogenation pathway toward FA formation. This work highlights the PIL-engineered interfacial microenvironment as a key factor for overriding the intrinsic selectivity of a catalyst and enabling practical CO2 valorization.
ndfce51730e5d: Pulsed electrolysis is a promising operating strategy for electrochemical CO2 reduction, but understanding how products form, accumulate, and are released during dynamic operation remains challenging, particularly in membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs). Conventional product analysis methods provide limited time resolution, making them poorly suited for resolving product-specific changes during pulses that are on the timescale of seconds. Here, selected-ion-flow-tube mass spectrometry (SIFT-MS) was used as a quasi-real-time analytical technique to measure the product concentrations during pulsed CO2 electrolysis in a MEA using a copper oxide nanoparticle-derived cathode catalyst. Methodology development for the SIFT-MS technique established the sampling and pulsing criteria required for reliable semi-quantitative analysis of the concentration of reaction products. Applying these methodology developments to pulsed electrolysis experiments unveiled how molecular structure influences product retention within the electrode and subsequent transport into the MEA outlet stream under pulsed CO2R conditions. A comparison of the measured concentrations of ethanol, ethylene, and acetaldehyde provided evidence that the formation of ethanol occurs through multiple contributing reaction pathways. The analysis of the measured concentrations of acetaldehyde, propionaldehyde, and 1-propanol provided evidence for the sequential formation of products through which the formation of aldehydes precedes the formation of 1-propanol. Overall, this work establishes SIFT-MS as a product-specific, quasi-real-time analytical technique for probing pulsed CO2R in membrane electrode assemblies that can unveil crucial information to aid in the development of future MEA electrolyzers and operational strategies.
n02d8930fb5d1: The selective oxidation of methane to value-added oxygenates represents a formidable challenge in heterogeneous catalysis, fundamentally limited by the thermodynamic trade-off between activating the reactant and preventing the subsequent overoxidation of fragile products. This vulnerability is deeply tied to the spatial accessibility within the catalytic microenvironment; highly open channels, while facilitating mass transfer, indiscriminately expose the generated products to secondary oxidation. Herein, we develop a site-selective construction strategy to establish spatially decoupled reaction-diffusion microenvironments within mordenite (MOR). By utilizing pyridine as a pore-blocking agent to occupy 12-membered ring (12-MR) channels, we preferentially localize the active Cu species, identified as bent mono-μ-oxo dicopper cores, within the well-defined 8-membered ring (8-MR) side pockets. This architecture induces a profound dual spatial effect. At the reaction level, the 8-MR acts as a nanoscopic kinetic shield by providing a customized local topology that suppresses the reactivity of oxygenated intermediates while retaining sufficient methane activation capability. Crucially, at the mass-transfer level, Cu incorporation into the 12-MR main channels is largely suppressed, allowing these channels to serve as unobstructed diffusion pathways and reducing the probability that desorbed methanol recontacts oxidative Cu sites during outward transport. Furthermore, by eliminating the structural heterogeneity inherent to non-selective synthesis, this spatially defined microenvironment and homogeneous Cu coordination structure enable the elucidation of the intrinsic structure-performance relationship. Under continuous operating conditions, this spatially engineered catalyst exhibits high methanol selectivity and productivity, ranking among the leading Cu-MOR systems for methane-to-methanol conversion. These findings demonstrate that designing a decoupled reaction-diffusion microenvironment can regulate catalytic selectivity beyond electronic-structure modulation, while also offering a generalizable method for the site-selective placement of metal ions within zeolite.
n5b1cbf4def2e: Pure-iodide wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites (∼1.68 eV) featuring eliminated photoinduced halide segregation are compelling top-cell absorbers for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells. However, their complex crystallization readily induces heterogeneous composition and structural defects, hindering performance improvements in the resulting devices. Here, we develop a cesium triiodide (CsI3)-mediated strategy to regulate intermediate-phase evolution of pure-iodide WBG perovskites. The CsI3-derived precursor chemistry reconstructs Pb-I coordination networks, suppresses premature organic-dominated intermediate nucleation, and promotes homogeneous phase conversion. The modulated crystallization pathway yields highly crystalline films with improved iodine uniformity and reduced non-radiative recombination losses. Consequently, single-junction solar cells achieve a stabilized power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 22.40%, which retains 95% of its initial efficiency after 1500 h of maximum power point tracking. More importantly, the associated perovskite-silicon solar cells deliver a stabilized PCE of 30.74% along with improved thermal stability, highlighting the great potential of pure-iodide WBG perovskites for efficient and durable tandem photovoltaics.
nea3b036467e1: Ceria-based thermochemical cycles offer a promising route to solar hydrogen, but require reduction above 1400 °C and large temperature swings. Here, building on electrically assisted CeO2 reduction, we demonstrate repeated isothermal CeO2-based water-splitting cycles at 700–900 °C and 0.5–2.0 V. Porous CeO2−YSZ bilayer pellets with different composition ratios undergo electrically assisted reduction and steam re-oxidation at the same temperature, producing O2 and H2 in separate steps without thermal cycling. The process reaches H2/O2 ratios up to 1.9, reproducible H2 productivity over 10 cycles, and H2 yields up to 49 ± 2 μmol gCeO2−1 cycle−1 after only 20 min of electrically assisted reduction. Extended-reduction experiments show that the best composition remains only ∼0.10 V below the applied bias on an equivalent thermodynamic-voltage basis. Reactor-scale projections based on gas utilization in an existing ceria reactor give a solar-to-H2 efficiency of 5.6% without assuming improvements to the CeO2−YSZ architecture.
ncc880a219f5a: Ionomer engineering offers a powerful yet underexplored strategy for electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR), since the polymer tailors the microenvironment at the catalyst surface. Here, we rationally design high-performance ionomers by applying fixed-charge sign and hydration as design criteria. Synthetic anion-exchange ionomers (AEIs) enhance NO3– accessibility, and the highest AEI hydration is accompanied by a shift in the dominant hydrogenation pathway toward a favorable *H-mediated regime. Time-dependent attenuated total reflection surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) coupled with numerical simulation yields a 40.7-fold higher NO3– diffusion coefficient for the AEI than for Nafion. Potential-dependent in situ ATR-SEIRAS combined with kinetic isotope effect measurements and *H scavenging supports a pathway shift arising from a hydrated microenvironment enriched in free and weakly hydrogen-bonded water. The AEI-modified commercial Cu nanoparticle electrode reaches an NH3 yield rate of 13.8 mg h–1cm–2 and 98.0% Faradaic efficiency, positioning the fixed-charge sign and hydration as accessible design descriptors potentially transferable to other electrocatalytic reactions.
n4414b5c3fc93: Recent advances in high quadrupole moment (Q̂$\hat{Q}$) non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) have improved exciton diffusion and charge separation in organic photovoltaics (OPVs). However, conventional bulk heterojunctions (BHJs) with a balanced donor‐to‐acceptor ratio often exhibit amorphous mixed domains, introducing energetic disorder and limiting the optoelectronic potential and stability of high‐Q̂$\hat{Q}$ NFAs. Here, a diffusion‐driven 3D crystallization strategy is demonstrated using an NFA‐rich BHJ model (Non‐fullerene Matrix‐BHJ, NM‐BHJ) that suppresses electron trap states and charge localization, thereby reducing energy losses driven by static disorder. Notably, the laterally oriented 3D superstructures significantly enhance thermodynamic stability and improve resistance to morphological changes under thermal stress. OPVs incorporating the optimized NM‐BHJ retain 88.2% of their initial efficiency after 720 h at 65 °C and over 99% after 2400 h at room‐temperature. The obtained T90 of 644 h is, to the best of our knowledge, one of the longest experimentally verified lifetimes reported among Y‐series‐based BHJ systems in the literature, including those employing chemically modified oligomeric derivatives. Combined with its generality across different NFA systems, this study suggests that the NM‐BHJ strategy opens a new era for highly efficient and thermally robust OPV devices by morphologically overcoming the inherent thermal limitations of high‐Q̂$\hat{Q}$ NFAs.
na881d99924cb: This Special Issue commemorates the fifteenth anniversary of Advanced Energy Materials and reflects the evolution of energy materials research from fundamental discovery toward practical technologies. Assembled in conjunction with the 2025 Wiley Forum Spring Meeting, the collection brings together 28 Research Articles and 10 Reviews spanning photovoltaics and optoelectronics, electrochemical energy storage and conversion, flexible and distributed energy technologies, and data‐driven materials discovery. Collectively, these contributions demonstrate how advances in materials chemistry, defect and interface control, multiscale characterization, scalable manufacturing, and predictive computation are enabling more efficient, stable, and deployable energy systems. The breadth of the collection underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and of evaluating innovations under realistic technological constraints. The Special Issue is dedicated to the memory of Professor Taiho Park, whose scientific vision, leadership, and service left a lasting legacy in the field. Sincere appreciation is extended to all contributing authors, reviewers, and the editorial team whose efforts made this anniversary collection possible.
nc9a261396bd6: Perovskite solar modules (PSMs) attract significant attention for their superior optoelectronic properties, but significant cell‐to‐module (CTM) losses remain a critical issue to be addressed. Among the various factors, the primary reason for CTM losses is the incomplete, non‐conformal coverage of the electron transport layer (ETL) over large‐area, P1‐scribed transparent conductive oxide (TCO) substrates. In this work, we report an alcohol‐adduct mediated precursor stabilization strategy to achieve high‐quality, uniform SnO2 layers via controlled hydrolysis reaction kinetics. We employ a tin isopropoxide isopropanol (TIPI) adduct, which effectively modulates the electrophilicity and stabilizes the Sn center atom, followed by a sequential deposition of SnO2 nanoparticles. This double‐layer (DL) architecture exhibits superior optical properties, improved electron transport, and conformal coverage over large areas. As a result, PSMs fabricated with the TIPI (DL) SnO2 ETL exhibit a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.6% (reverse/forward average), with a certified PCE of 19.7% (aperture area = 213 cm2). In addition, the PSMs with TIPI (DL) SnO2 ETL demonstrated a wide processing window, maintaining a PCE over 20% regardless of variations in concentration or deposition speed, highlighting potential for in‐line commercialization. Furthermore, the modules exhibited good long‐term stability under damp‐heat and in outdoor field tests.
n75e799262947: Although halide perovskite solar cells have achieved remarkable efficiencies close to their theoretical limits, durability against external factors and reproducible processing remain major barriers to commercialization. Conventional ammonium halide‐based surface passivation strategies enable effective defect passivation and charge selectivity via 2D/3D heterostructure formation, but their metastability and strong sensitivity to processing conditions limit long‐term stability and process window. In this work, we report an amorphous π‐conjugated passivator, (4‐(3‐iodo‐9H‐carbazol‐9‐yl)butyl)phosphonic acid (I–4PACz). The asymmetric iodine substituent enhances the molecular dipole moment while simultaneously altering intermolecular interactions, thereby suppressing ordered molecular packing and enabling the formation of a uniform interfacial layer. The characteristics of I‐4PACz result in efficient charge extraction as well as widening process window. Perovskite solar modules applied to I‐4PACz as passivator between the perovskite and hole transport‐layer show a power conversion efficiency of 21.2% with 24.5 cm2 aperture size, and excellent long‐term stability retaining 85% of the initial efficiency for 884 h under 65°C and 40% relative humidity, and 98.7% of the initial efficiency for 525 h under continous illumination, respectively. Moreover, the minial dependence on blade‐coating speed also reinforces the suitability of this interfacial control strategy for inline and large‐area manufacturing.
n97b23657d656: Perovskite Solar Modules In article number e06809, Jaemin Lee, Nam Joong Jeon, Eui Hyuk Jung, and co‐workers demonstrate that an amorphous p‐conjugated passivator enhances performance and improves durability in perovskite solar modules. Treatment of the perovskite surface with the passivator renders a broader processing window to fabricate scalable perovskite solar modules due to diminishing thickness sensitivity.
n8fcfa453b0e7: Organic–inorganic halide perovskites have emerged as promising materials for next‐generation optoelectronic devices due to their exceptional photophysical properties. Among them, α‐formamidinium lead tri‐iodide (α‐FAPbI3) with a cubic symmetry (space group of Pm3¯m$Pm\bar{3}m$) has garnered attention as a potential absorber in solar cells for its narrow bandgap and superior stability. The fundamental mechanisms governing its high performance have yet to be fully elucidated. In this study, we demonstrate that centrosymmetry breaking in [001] preferentially oriented α‐FAPbI3 thin films (POF) arises from inevitable anisotropic strain during film formation. Using circular polarization‐dependent pump‐probe transient absorption spectroscopy, we observe Rashba‐type band splitting exclusively in POF, indicating symmetry breaking. Angle‐dependent X‐ray diffraction and photoluminescence (PL) reveal significant residual stress in POF compared to randomly oriented films (ROF), confirming strain‐induced lattice distortion. Furthermore, time‐resolved PL and microwave conductivity measurements reveal top‐back inhomogeneous carrier dynamics and anisotropic charge carrier mobility, supporting the presence of the anisotropic strain‐induced symmetry breaking. Our findings provide direct experimental evidence that inevitable strain in POF induces static Rashba effects, offering new insights into strain engineering for high‐performance perovskite optoelectronics and potential quantum applications.
n7197dea19481: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) promise safer energy storage and the potential to outperform current lithium-ion batteries. Ni-rich cathodes deliver high energy density, whereas sulfide solid electrolytes offer exceptional Li+ conductivity and inherent mechanical compliance, making their combination particularly attractive. Yet their capacity fades rapidly because (electro)chemical and mechanical degradation occur concurrently within the cathode. Here, we propose an approach to decouple these two factors in LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2|Li6PS5Cl0.5Br0.5|Li metal cells by monitoring the state-of-charge window.
