Uncoated cathodes experience capacity fading primarily due to (electro)chemical degradation: interfacial reactions form resistive interphases consisting of NiO-like rock salt, SO x , PO x , and related species that hinder Li+ extraction, resulting in pronounced charge fading. A conformal LiNbO3 coating on the cathode surface suppresses interfacial reactions, significantly mitigating charge fading but revealing dominant discharge fading arising from mechanical degradation, such as particle cracking and interfacial delamination. While the protective coating stabilizes the interface and improves initial performance, the increased capacity intensifies electrode volume changes, underscoring the need for integrated electro-chemo-mechanical design strategies. Evaluating charge and discharge fading outlines the interplay between (electro)chemical and mechanical degradation and offers a new diagnostic framework to guide the development of more durable, high-energy-density ASSBs.
nb42e0b243059: Antimony selenosulfide (Sb2(S,Se)3) has recently attracted intense interest as an earth‐abundant, non‐toxic, and bandgap‐tunable photovoltaic absorber. However, conventional one‐step deposition routes typically produce films with inadequate crystallinity and inhomogeneous elemental distribution through the film thickness, which severely hamper charge transport and limit device performance. Herein, we introduce an innovative selenium‐source switching driven two‐step sequential deposition (SDE) strategy that decouples framework formation from compositional engineering to overcome these limitations. First, a selenourea‐based precursor is used to deposit a thick Sb2(S,Se)3 film serving as a primary light‐harvesting scaffold. Then, a sodium selenosulfate‐based precursor solution is applied for secondary deposition. Owing to the high reactivity of this solution system, selenium species readily penetrate into the as‐deposited film, inducing extensive ion diffusion and recrystallization throughout the bulk Sb2(S,Se)3 material. This SDE strategy simultaneously optimizes the vertical Se/S grading, tailors the bandgap profile, and eliminates bulk deep‐level traps and surface recombination centers. Consequently, the SDE‐Sb2(S,Se)3 device achieves a remarkable efficiency of 10.90%, placing it among the highest efficiencies for this material system. This strategy not only resolves the intrinsic bottlenecks of one‐step techniques but also provides a generalizable route for synthesizing high‐quality multicomponent chalcogenide films and offers new insights into ion‐exchange kinetics during sequential deposition.
nb779560329aa: Silicon offers high theoretical capacity as an alternative to graphite, yet it undergoes much more severe degradation, resulting in substantially poorer cycle and calendar life. In this context, a mechanistic understanding of degradation pathways is essential for designing silicon‐based anodes with performance comparable to graphite. In this review, we present a comprehensive overview of the degradation mechanisms governing silicon‐based anodes. The mechanisms are organized around active materials degradation at the particle level, which is governed by both intrinsic factors of silicon and extrinsic factors. At the electrode scale, we discuss electrode integrity loss, which arises from the breakdown of mechanical and electrical continuity. In addition, we differentiate solid electrolyte interphase instability into mechanical and chemical degradation mechanisms to clarify how each contributes to performance decay. We further describe lithium trapping as an additional source of irreversible capacity loss. Finally, we address crosstalk degradation that arises when silicon is used together with graphite, driven by mechanical and thermodynamic interactions between the two materials. This review provides an integrated understanding of the degradation pathways of silicon‐based anodes, offering insights that can guide material design and improve the performance of lithium‐ion batteries.
ncac0ba99fb2a: The reliable operation of lithium‐based batteries (LBBs) under subzero conditions remains a fundamental challenge due to sluggish ion transport, increased interfacial impedance, and unstable solid–electrolyte interphases (SEIs). Popular high‐ and localized high‐concentration electrolytes partially alleviate these issues but still suffer from excessive viscosity and strong Li+‐solvent binding that hinder low‐temperature kinetics. Weakly solvating electrolytes (WSEs) offer a new paradigm by weakening Li+ coordination, promoting anion‐dominated solvation, and accelerating desolvation and interfacial charge transfer. This review provides a comprehensive review of WSEs, focusing on working mechanisms, structural design strategies, and interfacial chemistries. We also address molecular‐level solvation insights with electrolyte engineering to discuss how WSEs promote uniform lithium deposition, inorganic‐rich SEIs, and stable cycling at subzero temperatures. Finally, the review highlights future research directions—from quantitative solvation–performance correlations and data‐driven electrolyte design to interfacial diagnostics and scalability. By integrating molecular‐level understanding with predictive modeling and engineering validation, WSEs offer a transformative route toward all‐climate rechargeable batteries capable of stable and efficient operation from arctic to desert environments.
na444700d2a14: All‐perovskite tandem solar cells leverage the solid‐solution nature of metal halide perovskites to tune the band gaps of wide‐ and narrow‐bandgap subcells for current matching and high photovoltage. Sn–Pb mixed perovskites with band gaps of approximately 1.2–1.3 eV are attractive bottom absorbers, but Sn‐rich surface regions, depth‐dependent compositional inhomogeneity, and associated band‐alignment issues limit both photocurrent and photovoltage. Here, we introduce a layered‐perovskite‐assisted dry‐contact trimming (LDT) strategy to reconfigure Sn–Pb narrow‐bandgap perovskites after film formation. A Dion–Jacobson‐phase ethylenediammonium lead iodide (EDAPbI4) film is brought into transient solid‐state contact with the Sn–Pb perovskite and then removed after contact annealing. EDAPbI4 functions as a temporary solid‐state contact partner that removes Sn‐rich surface species and reduces depth‐dependent lattice and compositional inhomogeneity without forming a retained 2D capping layer. This reconfiguration alleviates reverse band bending at the Sn–Pb perovskite/transport‐layer interface, suppresses nonradiative interfacial recombination, and reduces open‐circuit‐voltage losses. The improved lattice/compositional uniformity also enables thick Sn–Pb absorbers to maintain efficient charge collection and high short‐circuit current density. Consequently, single‐junction Sn–Pb devices exceed 24% efficiency, and monolithic all‐perovskite tandem devices surpass 30% with reproducible performance and operational stability. These results identify LDT as a complementary post‐crystallization strategy for engineering mixed perovskite solid‐solutions and their interfaces.
n934881f1791e: Organic semiconductors are key photoactive materials for solar energy conversion, including organic photovoltaics (OPVs) and photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. Here, we uncover a paradox: materials optimized for efficient charge extraction in OPVs exhibit different behavior when used as photocatalysts in aqueous colloids. To probe this contrast, we study nanoparticles (NPs) prepared from PM6:Y6 and its structural analogue D18:Y5, comparing their photophysical responses across photovoltaic and photocatalytic regimes. We observe an inverse relationship between power conversion efficiency in thin films and hydrogen evolution activity in dispersions. Y5‐based NPs show stronger aggregation, longer exciton lifetimes, and slower hole transfer, indicative of localized charges that promote interfacial redox chemistry. Density functional theory calculations reveal that Y5 possesses more negative electrostatic potential, facilitating charge localization favorable for hydrogen evolution. D18 also exhibits higher photoluminescence quantum yield and reduced non‐radiative recombination relative to PM6. Molecular dynamics simulations show that D18 forms stronger donor–acceptor interactions, stabilizing localized charges for proton reduction, whereas Y6 displays more higher acceptor–acceptor coordination, enabling efficient charge extraction in blends. Collectively, these findings establish the pivotal role of long‐lived, localized carriers in governing the charge dynamics of organic semiconductors and offer design principles for reconciling their dual photovoltaic and photocatalytic functionalities.
nee2ca886ad75: Organic Photocatalysis Organic donor–acceptor nanoparticles harvest sunlight and regulate charge carrier dynamics to drive hydrogen evolution. Unlike organic is favored, restricted interfacial hole transfer can generate long‐lived, localized carriers that persist near reactive interfaces. Their prolonged availability for proton reduction highlights how controlling charge localization and lifetime can guide the design of efficient organic photocatalysts. More in article number e70952, Chang Yun Son, Sae Byeok Jo, Dae Sung Chung, Hyojung Cha, and co‐workers.
ndad31728877e: Solid oxide electrochemical cells (SOC), encompassing fuel‐cell, electrolysis, and reversible operating modes, represent a pivotal technology for high‐efficiency conversion between electrical energy and chemical fuels. However, practical deployment at intermediate‐temperatures (IT, 600–800°C) is constrained by intertwined limitations in ionic transport, surface reaction kinetics, and thermo–chemical stability. This review summarizes and analyzes the recent developments in SOC electrodes and electrolytes through a unified structure‐defect‐property‐durability framework. Emphasis is placed on how crystal symmetry, lattice distortions, and defect chemistry dictate charge‐carrier concentrations, oxygen and proton migration pathways, and interfacial compatibility under realistic oxidizing and reducing environments. By correlating electrochemical performance with oxygen‐vacancy formation energetics, transport coefficients, and degradation processes such as cation segregation and secondary‐phase evolution, the potential of different materials for SOC was further analyzed. Finally, prospective strategies involving multifunctional electrolyte architectures, defect and interface‐engineered electrodes, and multiscale microstructural control are outlined, offering guidance to the rational design of durable, high‐performance SOC systems capable of sustained operation in the IT regime.
n05ccf793965d: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are promising candidates for next‐generation photovoltaics thanks to their high power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) and cost‐effective fabrication processes. However, reliance on noble metal electrodes, such as gold (Au) and silver (Ag), significantly increases overall device cost. This work demonstrates high‐performance PSCs with noble‐metal‐free multilayer electrodes comprising molybdenum oxide (MoOX), chromium (Cr), and aluminum (Al). These PSCs achieve a PCE of 25.6%, which is competitive with that of Au‐based devices (26.3%). Furthermore, a mini‐module with an aperture area of 25.5 cm2 shows a PCE of 21.3%, which indicates the scalability of the proposed electrode architecture to large‐area devices. Systematic investigation of each layer shows that the MoOX layer functions as an effective diffusion barrier that suppresses metal‐ion migration. The intermediate Cr layer enhances interfacial adhesion and reduces series resistance. In addition, the MoOX/Cr/Al multilayer electrode exhibits significantly higher resistance to external scratching than Au electrodes, which demonstrates improved mechanical durability. These results show that MoOX/Cr/Al multilayer electrodes provide a practical alternative to noble metals and substantially enhance the cost competitiveness of PSCs.
na99130324c13: Perovskite Solar Cells Perovskite solar cells typically employ high‐cost precious‐metal electrodes, which increase overall device cost. In article number e70950, Young Yun Kim, Bonkee Koo, Min Jae Ko, and co‐workers demonstrate high‐performance perovskite solar cells with low‐cost MoOX/Cr/Al electrodes, achieving device performance similar to that of conventional Au‐electrode devices. Notably, the Cr interlayer improves MoOX/Al adhesion and suppresses the formation of insulating aluminum oxide, thereby enhancing electrode conductivity.
n53677dad4501: Monolithic III–V multijunction photovoltaics are promising candidates for both space power systems and solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion, yet their deployment in flexible, chemically aggressive, and radiation‐rich environments requires simultaneous control of epitaxial quality, conformability, and barrier properties. Here, we present a flexible InGaP/GaAs/InGaAs triple‐junction platform that addresses these requirements within a single device architecture. The optimized epitaxial stack and its growth process enable almost fully relaxed subcells with low dislocation density, supporting power conversion efficiencies above 33% under AM1.5G and ∼31% under AM0, even after transferring the epitaxial stack to a thin plastic substrate to improve mechanical compliance. To ensure environmental robustness, the flexible triple‐junction cells are encapsulated with an ultrathin glass sheet that provides strong protection against aqueous and strongly alkaline conditions, as well as against high‐energy proton and electron irradiation. By exploiting the high output voltage and durability of this platform, bias‐free electrocatalysis with formate as the predominant product is demonstrated using a simple electrocatalyst configuration. These results establish a unified III–V multijunction photovoltaic architecture that couples space‐relevant efficiency, flexibility, and radiation hardness with chemical durability suitable for unassisted solar‐to‐chemical conversion, offering a versatile route toward next‐generation terrestrial and space energy systems.
nc30efedc22d6: Flexible Photovoltaics In article number e06763, Ho Kwan Kang, Sung‐Min Lee, Won Jun Choi, and co‐workers present a flexible InGaP/GaAs/InGaAs triple‐junction solar cell encapsulated with ultrathin glass for operation in chemically aggressive and radiation‐rich environments. The platform enables both space photovoltaics and unassisted solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion, bridging space applications and electrocatalysis.
n91ded3f31a4f: Sulfide‐based argyrodite Li6PS5Cl (LPSC) is one of the most promising solid electrolytes for high‐energy all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) owing to its high ionic conductivity and favorable mechanical deformability. However, even trace moisture exposure under dry room conditions induces rapid and irreversible degradation, severely limiting scalable manufacturing. Beyond the widely recognized loss of ionic conductivity, the chemical consequences of moisture exposure on cathode remain poorly understood. Here, using synchrotron‐based transmission X‐ray microscopy combined with hard and tender X‐ray absorption spectroscopy, and high‐resolution X‐ray diffraction, we reveal that moisture exposure transforms LPSC into chemically reductive phases. These degradation products actively extract lattice oxygen from Ni‐rich NMC cathodes, inducing Ni reduction and cation disorder, and trigger irreversible surface reconstruction into spinel‐like phases. Importantly, we demonstrate a simple and process‐compatible regeneration strategy: a brief annealing treatment followed by controlled oxygen exposure selectively quenching reductive surface phases. This regenerated LPSC recovers 81% of its original ionic conductivity and restores cathode interfacial stability, enabling ASSBs to achieve 97% of the discharge capacity of the pristine LPSC and 95% capacity retention over 200 cycles. These results highlight moisture degradation of LPSC as a chemically driven interfacial failure mechanism and provide practical guidelines for mitigating degradation during manufacturing.
n0a141b778fb5: All‐Solid‐State Batteries The cover illustrates how moisture induced degradation of sulfide solid electrolytes retain reductive surface species that, when incorporated as catholytes, form unstable interfaces with Ni‐rich layered oxide cathodes and accelerate structural and chemical degradation at the surface. Subsequent O2 annealing removes these reductive residues, revives the electrolyte surface, and mitigates interfacial damage, enabling a practical regeneration strategy for moisture‐exposed solid electrolytes. More in article number e00010, Jongwoo Lim and co‐workers.
n5a854497bebe: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have exhibited astonishing progress in power conversion efficiency (PCE) along with a remarkable improvement in long‐term stability. A precise control on crystal growth, however, still remains challenging, particularly for poly‐crystalline perovskite films based on solution‐ and low temperature‐processing. Here in, we introduce a simple but effective strategy to regulate the crystallographic orientation of wide bandgap perovskite films (FA0.79MA0.12Cs0.09Pb(I0.85Br0.15)3; FA = formamidinium, MA = methylammonium) by utilizing lattice coherency with seed template, where MAPbBrXCl3−X not only serves as a kinetic controller for retarding crystal growth but also performs as a seed template to reshape the thermodynamic energy cost for regulating crystal orientation along face‐up (111) array by offering enthalpy‐driven reduced Gibbs free energy change. Consequently, perovskite films grown with the aid of a seed template exhibit outstanding crystallinity with the preferential orientation, while a weak crystallinity with a relatively random orientation is observed from the control sample. Noticeably, devices employing the (111)‐oriented ordered structure, in spite of its unfavorable charge extraction, eventually result in competitive PCEs and superior long‐term stability at the elevated temperature to those of (001)‐oriented ones, emphasizing the importance of a highly ordered lattice with facet control in governing the device performance.
nda3a1084e289: Perovskite Solar Cells Two interlocking crystal lattices dominate the illustration, capturing how crystallographic orientation is engineered in wide‐bandgap halide perovskites. The MAPbBrXCl3−X seed template, lattice‐coherent with FA0.79MA0.12Cs0.09Pb(I0.85Br0.15)3, retards crystal growth as a kinetic controller while lowering the Gibbs free‐energy change via an enthalpy‐driven route, steering the film into a uniform face‐up (111)‐oriented array. More in article number e06805, Yasemin Saygili, Hui‐Seon Kim, and co‐workers.
nbd3cf195bad5: Vapor‐assisted hybrid two‐step deposition, which combines thermally evaporated inorganic layers with solution‐processed organic halides to form halide perovskites, has emerged as a scalable and industry‐compatible route for textured tandem photovoltaics. However, this process is often hindered by reaction‐limited phase formation, particularly when compact, non‐porous, and highly crystalline inorganic layers formed by thermal evaporation restrict subsequent conversion, resulting in incomplete reaction and pronounced depth‐dependent heterogeneity. In this study, we introduce a strategy to regulate the inorganic precursor layer by incorporating localized heterogeneous nucleation sites. Sparsely distributed hydrophilic metal oxide species serve as effective nucleation centers during vapor deposition, enabling effective control over film morphology and crystal orientation from the early stages of growth. This tailored inorganic framework facilitates the subsequent incorporation of organic halides, alleviating reaction limitations and suppressing residual unreacted precursors. Consequently, the perovskite films exhibit improved stoichiometric uniformity and enhanced optoelectronic quality, enabling wide‐bandgap perovskite solar cells with markedly improved performance and operational stability. This work provides important mechanistic insight into crystal growth engineering of vapor‐deposited perovskite thin films.
n305291ae4d31: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) provide a practical route to bridge first‐principles accuracy with the spatiotemporal scales required for modeling complex energy materials. By learning potential‐energy surfaces from density functional theory (DFT) data, MLIPs enable atomistic simulations up to 104–106 atoms over nanosecond timescales, thereby extending access to phenomena inaccessible to ab initio molecular dynamics. This review presents a phenomenon‐oriented synthesis of MLIP development, spanning descriptor‐based models, Gaussian process frameworks with uncertainty quantification, equivariant graph neural networks, and foundation models trained on large‐scale datasets. We assess how architectural choices, training strategies (including active learning and multi‐fidelity approaches), and dataset design influence accuracy, transferability, and computational efficiency across representative energy systems. Applications in solid‐state electrolytes, battery electrodes, electrocatalysts, perovskite photovoltaics, and high‐entropy materials are discussed with both performance metrics and methodological rationale. While MLIPs capture qualitative trends and relative property variations, absolute predictions remain sensitive to DFT functional choices, dataset representativeness, and treatment of long‐range interactions. We address a structured validation framework linking model fidelity to experimentally relevant observables and system complexity. Also, we outline emerging directions including generative inverse design, autonomous discovery workflows, and foundation‐model fine‐tuning, highlighting opportunities and limitations for predictive deployment in energy materials research.
ne75ff2017810: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials The image illustrates how machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs), represented by a neural‐network display, explore the vast chemical space of the periodic table to accelerate atomistic simulations across key energy material applications — batteries, solid‐state electrolytes, electrocatalysts, and photovoltaics. More in article number e71046, Chang Woo Myung, Geunsik Lee, Kwang S. Kim, and co‐workers.
ncdbb077cf762: To overcome silicon anode instability, a hierarchical silicon/carbon composite fabricated from industrial waste via a scalable milling process is demonstrated. In‐depth post‐mortem analysis reveals how functional carbons—a CNT network and graphene shell—synergistically suppress degradation. This robust design delivers outstanding stability in practical full cells, offering a commercially viable pathway for next‐generation batteries. Abstract Silicon‐based anodes offer exceptional energy density but are limited by severe volume changes and poor electrical conductivity, hindering their commercial integration. Herein, a silicon/carbon composite is designed for seamless incorporation into conventional graphite anodes, addressing the industry's focus on boosting practical energy density. This composite is obtained by simple, scalable vibratory milling of industrial waste silicon with functionally distinct carbon materials, meeting stringent requirements for both performance and cost. This multiscale carbon structuring mitigates silicon delamination, ensures continuous electronic pathways during volume fluctuations, and stabilizes the electrode–electrolyte interface. Detailed post‐mortem analyses confirm that this hierarchical carbon network effectively suppresses silicon extrusion—accompanied by significant morphological changes—a common failure mode. When implemented as a ≈17.5 wt.% additive into graphite electrodes, the composite achieves an industrially relevant target capacity of 500 mAh g−1. It delivers outstanding performance under commercial‐level metrics, including a high areal capacity of 3 mAh cm−2, electrode density of 1.6 g cm−3, and active material ratio of 96.9 wt.%. In full‐cell configurations paired with a LiNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2 (NCM622) cathode, the system retains ≈78% capacity after 500 cycles, demonstrating its viability for real‐world applications. These results highlight the critical role of hierarchical carbon design for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries.
nb2ce9447ba0d: This review elucidates where the operational instability of perovskite‐based optoelectronic devices originates from by comprehensively exploring degradation phenomena from atomistic interactions to device scale. At thermodynamic equilibrium, the intrinsic stability of halide perovskites is reasonably good when considering the balance of intramolecular Asite covalent bonds, intermolecular A–X hydrogen bonds, and mixed ionic–covalent B–X bonding. Under operation, however, photoexcited or injected carriers become localized via trapping at surface and ionic defects and/or polaron formation in the soft Pb–halide framework, which induce Coulombic force to distort the crystal lattice and change atom‐to‐atom distances. Such effects lower ion migration barriers, enhance lattice distortion, and accelerate atmospheric reactions with ambient species, leading to quick degradation of perovskite crystals. In terms of device‐level stability, holerich conditions and interfacial charge accumulation in heterostructured architectures are identified as particularly detrimental, directly linking carrier localization to device‐level degradation. Based on these insights, we discuss composition engineering toward favorable large‐polaron formation, defect passivation to suppress trap‐assisted localization, and interfacial engineering within the heterostructured device. At the end, we propose advanced operation protocols that effectively relieve charge accumulation as key routes to realize durable perovskite optoelectronic devices.
n30d10ab09e22: Although perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have recently achieved high certified power conversion efficiencies (PCEs), operational instability remains a critical obstacle to commercialization. In particular, superoxide (O2∙−) generated at metal-oxide charge-transport layers rapidly decomposes perovskites by deprotonating the organic cations (FA⁺ and MA+) and therefore must be suppressed. Nevertheless, under operating illumination, the formation and diffusion of O2∙− are unavoidable as long as metal oxides are employed in PSCs. To address this, we introduce the natural antioxidant taurine at the SnO2/FAPbI3 interface to suppress O2∙− diffusion via chemical radical quenching. We elucidate the taurine-mediated O2∙− quenching mechanism through density functional theory (DFT) calculations supported by experiments. In addition, we find that I2 is concomitantly reduced to I- during the quenching process. This antioxidant interface prevents O2∙− induced perovskite decomposition under strongly oxidizing conditions. Moreover, the multifunctional groups of taurine form a chemical bridge between SnO2 and FAPbI3, reducing interfacial defect density, enhancing carrier mobility, and suppressing non-radiative recombination. Consequently, the taurine-buried interface enables an improved PCE with increased open-circuit voltage (VOC ) and fill factor (FF), while markedly enhancing the light-soaking and operational stability of PSCs.
n14a5063f42a6: Perovskite Solar Cells Metal oxide layers commonly employed in perovskite solar cells can generate superoxide radicals during photovoltaic operation conditions. These reactive oxygen species can subsequently diffuse into the perovskite lattice via iodine vacant sites while rapidly inducing perovskite degradation. Incorporation of taurine at buried interfaces chemically quenches the superoxide radicals, thereby enhancing the operational stability of perovskite solar cells. More in article number e05914, Byung Joon Moon, Jongmin Choi, and co‐workers.
nc0b8985d832b: The hygroscopic property of solid electrolytes has long been regarded as a critical weakness, as exposure to ambient humidity typically induces decomposition and a loss of ionic conductivity. In this study, we reveal a counterintuitive yet constructive role of trace water in enhancing ion transport in a gallium‐based pliable halide solid electrolyte. Controlled exposure of 2LiCl–GaF3 to trace amounts of water introduces oxygen into the structure and reorganizes the local environments around gallium and lithium. This oxygen‐driven structural reconfiguration forms Ga–O and Li–O linkages and diversifies the local environment of gallium by converting its coordination from sixfold to fourfold. It reduces the average Li–anion binding strength and flattens the Li‐ion migration energy landscape, resulting in enhanced Li‐ion transport. These changes collectively increase the ionic conductivity by more than two orders of magnitude, from 10−2 mS cm−1 to over 3 mS cm−1, while imparting amorphous and deformable characteristics to the 2LiCl‐GaF3 electrolyte. This study demonstrates that the interaction between trace water and complex anion frameworks can be harnessed to simultaneously tailor structural and transport properties, offering a new design strategy for high‐performance oxyhalide solid electrolytes.
nb00c8ca96798: This review provides a practical and in‐depth discussion of current collector engineering for Li‐metal batteries, emphasizing how the mass and volume introduced by modifications, together with the changes in Li inventory accompanying electrochemical processes, affect achievable energy metrics in realistic cell configurations. We compare major engineering approaches, including alloying and coating, crystallographic orientation control, and transitions from planar to three‐dimensional architectures, examining their impact on both initial energy density and long‐term retention. From these comparisons, we clarify key failure mechanisms and identify the stack‐level constraints that limit anode‐free Li‐metal batteries, including mass loading, volume occupation, electrolyte demand, and restricted Li inventory. To determine practical relevance, we introduce a quantitative energy density evaluation that benchmarks representative modification strategies against restricted Li inventory batteries. The analysis shows that although recent strategies enhance local plating and stripping behavior, they often reduce achievable energy density once realistic penalties related to volume, mass, and Li consumption are considered. These results establish clear criteria for identifying modifications that provide genuine practical benefit. Finally, we propose research directions that reduce geometric and material burdens while enhancing Li inventory retention, offering a perspective that supports the development of practical current collector designs for anode‐free Li‐metal batteries.
n2d052330358f: The poor stability of wide‐bandgap (>1.65 eV) perovskite top cells under light and heat remains a major challenge for commercializing perovskite/Si tandem solar cells. Here, we present a chloride additive‐mediated phase evolution strategy to fabricate thermodynamically stable, pure‐iodide wide‐bandgap perovskites with enhanced photo‐ and thermal stability. The incorporation of chloride additives effectively suppresses the formation of the orthorhombic secondary phase, while promoting the formation of the Cs2PbI2Cl2 2D Ruddlesden‐Popper intermediate phase. High‐resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) reveals that this intermediate phase undergoes a topotactic transformation into the cubic α‐phase, resulting in halide‐segregation‐free, phase‐pure perovskite films. Additionally, cation engineering of the chloride additives reduces thermally unstable methylammonium (MA) content below 5%, further enhancing thermal stability. The resulting pure‐iodide wide‐bandgap perovskite solar cells achieve power conversion efficiencies exceeding 21%, comparable to those of mixed‐halide counterparts, while exhibiting significantly enhanced photostability by maintaining 95.1% of the initial performance after 1000 h under ISOS‐L‐1I conditions. More importantly, devices with reduced MA content demonstrate excellent thermal stability by retaining 82.5% of its initial performance after 1000 h at 65°C under ISOS‐L‐2I conditions. These results highlight a promising pathway toward highly efficient and stable wide‐bandgap perovskite solar cells for tandem applications.
n360b1e6eacb7: As perovskite solar cells (PSCs) advance toward commercialization, achieving long‐term operational stability and high‐yield large‐area processing has become essential. These requirements are strongly influenced by the doping stability and film uniformity of hole‐transport materials (HTMs). Here, we introduce PDVB14, a PTAA‐based random copolymer incorporating planar divinylbenzene (DVB) units through compositionally reliable Buchwald–Hartwig C–N cross‐coupling. DVB incorporation increases backbone planarity and stabilizes the electronic structure by promoting more delocalized radical‐cation states, while short‐range electronic coupling supports efficient and stable charge transport across a broad doping window. When used as a hole‐transport layer, PDVB14 shows minimal performance dependence on dopant concentration, achieving a champion power conversion efficiency of 23.5% and retaining 20.6% at 1.0 cm2. It also delivers substantially improved thermal, light, and humidity stability compared PTAA. Dopant‐distribution mapping reveals highly uniform Li profiles across 6 × 6 cm2 films, demonstrating excellent compatibility with large‐area solution processing. This work provides a molecular design strategy that overcomes key structural and electronic limitations of PTAA, delivering a doping‐resilient and scalable polymeric HTM platform suited for next‐generation PSC manufacturing.
n8b94c29003df: All‐solid‐state Li‐ion batteries (ASSLIBs) require high‐performance anodes exhibiting high capacity, high rate capability, and long‐term cycling stability; however, existing anodes suffer from sluggish transport kinetics, particle pulverization, and unstable electrode–electrolyte interfaces. Herein, a SnSb anode overcoming these limitations via reaction‐driven coupled transport–nanostructure evolution during electrochemical cycling is reported. The transport evolution originates from the reaction‐driven formation of continuous mixed ionic–electronic conducting pathways and nanostructure evolution arises from repeated conversion and recombination reactions that induce stabilized nanocrystallization. This coupled evolution dynamically reconstructs mixed‐conducting pathways during lithiation–delithiation, suppresses particle agglomeration, preserves intimate contact with the Li6PS5Cl solid electrolyte (SE), and lowers interfacial resistance, enabling rapid and highly reversible electrochemical reactions. A SnSb|NCM811 full cell delivers an areal capacity of 28.97 mAh cm−2 at an ultrahigh cathode loading of 200 mg cm−2 and maintains ultrafast rate capability over 1000 cycles at 10 C. Using an optimized 30‐µm‐thick SE sheet, the full cell is projected to achieve gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 355.7 Wh kg−1 and 1017.4 Wh L−1, respectively. Pouch‐cell demonstrations highlight the potential of SnSb for high‐energy density ASSLIB applications and establish reaction‐driven coupled transport–nanostructure evolution as an effective design principle for next‐generation ASSLIB anodes.
n8b3794983969: To address the problems of facile reduction and deactivation of Pd species and the limitation of high Pd loading in the indirect oxidative carbonylation of methanol to dimethyl carbonate (DMC)...
nbacb4ba04329: Gold nanoclusters have long been limited in optoelectronic applications by sub-picosecond hot-carrier cooling. Here, electron-donating ligands spatially separate the frontier orbitals of Au22 nanoclusters, extending hot-carrier lifetime to nanoseconds and enabling high-performance, stable photodetectors. This work establishes ligand engineering as a general strategy to tune excited-state dynamics in metal nanoclusters, offering chemists a new materials design route for next-generation optoelectronics beyond conventional semiconductors.
n89e8ac68b1d8: Strain-release cycloadditions have emerged as powerful reactions for converting distorted ring systems into complex and otherwise hardly attainable organic molecular architectures. This Review encompasses the fundamentals of strain, its role in governing cycloaddition pathways, and offers a systematic examination of strained carbocycles and heterocycles, from bicyclo[1.1.1]butanes and 1-azabicyclo[1.1.1]butanes, housanes and aza-housanes, 2H-azirines and aziridines, azetidines, cyclopropanes, cyclobutanes, oxiranes, oxetanes, and strained alkynes and alkenes. Across these motifs, the general principles that dictate reactivity, the breadth of known cycloadditions and activation strategies, from Brønsted and Lewis acid catalysis to transition-metal activation, photocatalysis, and double strain-release mechanisms, are highlighted. Key opportunities, current limitations, and future directions are outlined.
nbb3af51a923a: This review focuses on recent advances of asymmetric hydrogenation in the strategic total synthesis of natural products and drug molecules, and outlines future perspectives for this field.
ne7b758fb2af0: This Tutorial Review establishes a unified framework connecting the fundamentals of solar vapor generation with materials and structural design, providing guiding principles for efficient, scalable, and sustainable water production.
n61f901993ff1: Dual-atom alloys (DAAs) embedded in metallic surfaces constitute an emerging catalytic platform fundamentally distinct from the widely studied carbon-supported dual-atom sites, as they enable intrinsic metal–metal cooperation within an active metallic environment. However, a systematic understanding of their structure–stability relationships remains elusive, mainly due to the prohibitive cost of exploring the vast space of compositions, crystal surfaces, and atomic configurations. Here, using Cu-based DAAs as a prototypical platform, we construct a library of 6804 candidate structures spanning nine crystal planes and two representative dual-atom configurations. Density functional theory (DFT)-calculated formation energies for 930 representative structures (13.7% of the library) are employed to train a physics-informed residual multilayer perceptron model combined with 5-fold ensemble learning. The model achieves high predictive accuracy with cross-validation R2 > 0.906 and demonstrates robust transferability across different crystal planes and structural motifs, outperforming conventional machine-learning baselines. Interpretable SHAP analysis indicates that electronic structure descriptors predominantly govern stability, with geometric compatibility contributing as a secondary factor. Systematic stability trends are identified, including a thermodynamic preference for diagonal configurations on the (100), (311), and (411) surfaces, linear-close configurations on the (110), (111), and (211) surfaces, and enhanced stability for noble-metal dopants, such as Au, Pt, and Pd. Electronic structure analysis further establishes a clear correlation between formation energy and the dopant d-band center, with greater stability achieved when the d-band center is located farther from the Fermi level. With the training on a limited number of DFT-calculated samples, this physics-aware and transferable machine-learning framework enables rapid and data-efficient prediction of dual-atom alloy stability. The approach is readily extensible to diverse crystal surfaces and alloy systems, providing a generalizable theoretical foundation for the thermodynamic screening and rational design of DAAs with high synthetic feasibility in energy catalysis.
n1e296c89bac2: Crystal facet engineering tailors a self-adaptive microenvironment for acidic OERs. The α-MnO 2 {100} facet forms a hydroxyl-rich interface that stabilizes Ir single atoms and lowers water-oxidation barriers, improving activity and stability.
ne57c01b2a31f: A contact-electrification-induced dielectric polarization mechanism enables unidirectional charge transfer for stable, low-crest-factor direct-current generation, thereby supporting robust self-powered operation of a multi-sensor IoT system.
n03dd40dd7715: The unstable ITO-SAM interface limits organic solar cell efficiency and stability. We introduce a molecular locking strategy using a vacuum-deposited InClx interlayer that triggers ligand exchange to form a robust multidentate In–O–P coordination network. This enhances SAM anchoring and coverage, delivering 20.4% efficiency in small-area cells and 18.8% active-area efficiency in modules, while enhancing device stability. This approach provides a generalizable interfacial platform that overcomes the efficiency-stability-scalability trilemma, paving a new pathway for advancing organic photovoltaics and beyond.
n89ccf33f7b56: Singlet fission in tetracene generates triplet excitons that are harvested by a metal halide perovskite through a ZnPc-mediated interface with energetics consistent with an interfacial hybrid charge-transfer (IHCT) pathway, enabling triplet sensitization and their contribution to photocurrent generation in perovskite photovoltaic devices.
n227b519af3e2: A monolayer photonic crystal integrated with a transparent manganese halide gel scintillator enhances the extraction of X-ray-excited light while preserving high spatial resolution. By combining X-ray computed tomography with structured-light scanning, the system enables a unified, spatially registered three-dimensional visualization of internal structures and external geometry.
n7e91b73ebf65: Lanthanide-doped nanoparticles with near-infrared-II (NIR-II, 1000–1700 nm) emission hold great promise for deep-tissue bioimaging, yet their luminescence efficiency is often limited by conventional sensitization pathways. Herein, we go beyond this conventional paradigm by introducing a Ca2+-formed band structure modulation in the host lattice to dramatically boost the NIR-II emission of lanthanide-doped nanoparticles. Rational doping of Ca2+ ions restructures the energy levels, enabling the probe to efficiently capture excitation energy and channel it toward NIR-II-emitting lanthanide activators. This Ca2+-induced band structure modulation mechanism not only enhances the absorption cross section but also accelerates energy transfer to the NIR-II-emitting states. As a result, the designed nanoprobes exhibit excellent photostability and a high quantum yield. In vivo bioimaging demonstrates that the resulting nanoprobes enable deep-tissue visualization with an improved signal-to-background ratio. This work establishes a sensitization strategy that goes beyond conventional approaches, positioning lanthanide-based NIR-II probes as promising candidates for advanced biological imaging.
ne7b79c7b67eb: Free-electron-based nanoscopy enables the study of optical excitations in materials with deep-subwavelength spatial resolution, with cathodoluminescence (CL) being one of the most useful signals. When combined with an optical collection system, CL measurements can access multidimensional information on light; yet the phase of the emitted optical fields has remained largely elusive. Here, we demonstrate a reference-free phase retrieval approach for far-field CL wavefronts using the Gerchberg–Saxton algorithm implemented with real-space and angular-space CL intensity data. Applying this approach to representative nanostructures, including a planar surface, nanosphere, plasmonic crystal, and nanowire, we reconstructed distinct phase distributions that revealed their underlying radiation mechanisms. This reference-free framework offers a robust and flexible route for retrieving the phase of electron beam-excited optical fields without relying on a reference wave, making it readily extendable to a wide range of nanostructures.
n47a7c3e613f4: Accessing crystal phases under nonequilibrium conditions is a central challenge for expanding the landscape of materials. Simple-cubic (sc) structures are considered energetically unfavorable in elemental solids and have previously been confirmed only in polonium. Here, we report the direct observation of a previously unrecognized sc-Ag formed under far-from-equilibrium conditions. Using electron beam irradiation inside a high-resolution transmission electron microscope as a trigger, we induced the radiolytic decomposition of silver iodide (AgI) and tracked the in situ formation of silver crystals in real time. Continuous imaging revealed that sc-Ag formation strongly depends on the polymorph of the precursor and occurs selectively from metastable γ-AgI. The sc-Ag exhibited unusually high chemical reactivity, undergoing gradual oxidation into silver oxide under high-vacuum conditions where conventional fcc-Ag remains stable. These findings demonstrate that irreversible crystal formation pathways can kinetically stabilize crystal structures inaccessible under near-equilibrium conditions and extend a previously inaccessible structural limit of metallic bonding.
neb234c21ae13: Dense TiO2 thin-film electrodes suffer from limited electrolyte penetration and restricted Li-ion transport, making the electrode architecture a critical parameter for efficient charge storage. Herein, glancing-angle deposition (GLAD) combined with reactive magnetron sputtering is used to engineer ion-accessible TiO2 nanocolumnar architectures without compositional modification or postprocessing. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations guided the selection of substrate tilt and azimuthal rotation conditions to control the column orientation, intercolumnar spacing, and open porosity. The predicted morphologies were subsequently validated by electron microscopy for the experimentally deposited thin films. Electrochemical measurements show that GLAD-engineered electrodes deliver up to approximately 4-fold higher areal capacitance than dense TiO2 films. ToF-SIMS depth profiling further reveals that Li species remain largely concentrated near the surface of dense films. In contrast, the GLAD-engineered nanocolumnar architecture allows for a more uniform Li distribution throughout the electrode depth. These results establish morphology-controlled ion accessibility as the primary origin of the enhanced electrochemical response.
n4d80e6efe44e: Two-dimensional halide perovskites host strongly bound excitons whose fine structure governs polarization selection rules and radiative recombination, yet spectral features in phenethylammonium lead iodide ((PEA)2PbI4) remain controversially assigned. Here, polarization-resolved low-temperature photoluminescence (PL) combined with first-principles G0W0+BSE calculations probes the intralayer and interlayer excitonic fine structure of this Ruddlesden–Popper perovskite. The low-energy multiplet is consistent with the intralayer excitonic fine structure governed by electron–hole exchange, crystal symmetry, and layer inequivalence in the two-layer unit cell, without requiring Rashba effects or exciton–polaron mechanisms as its primary origin. The weak doublet about 40 meV higher is best accounted for by interlayer excitons based on its energetics, splitting, and real-space character. Distortion-induced mixing of interlayer excitons with bright intralayer excitons provides a plausible explanation for the observed interlayer PL intensities and nearly orthogonal polarizations. These results support a layer-resolved excitonic picture encompassing both intralayer and interlayer states in (PEA)2PbI4.
n1bc9f897b04e: Silver bismuth sulfide (AgBiS2) quantum dots (QDs) are promising candidates for eco-friendly solution-based solar cells. However, structural defects in QDs hinder high efficiency. Controllable synthesis of AgBiS2 QDs remains challenging, often yielding crystals with surface and lattice defects that promote nonradiative recombination. Improving AgBiS2 QD quality before film formation is crucial, as synthesis-related imperfections often persist in devices and inherently limit effective passivation later on. This study presents a photoinduced surface reconstruction method for AgBiS2 QDs that achieves nearly perfect ionic ordering with lower lattice strain, leading to denser films and better band alignment with charge layers than the initial AgBiS2 QDs. Corresponding solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 9.71%, exceeding 8.16% for untreated solar cells. By enhancing AgBiS2 QD quality at the source rather than relying solely on downstream passivation, this approach offers a complementary pathway to high-performance QD solar cells.
na56287cc88e2: Anticounterfeiting technologies capable of enabling both visual authentication and machine-readable encryption are critically demanded. Here we present a wafer-scale and flexible tellurium nanowire (TeNW) platform with programmable localized orientation, enabling dual-mode anticounterfeiting based on polarization-encoded information. By employing a lock–shear and lift-off strategy, pixelated and highly aligned TeNW arrays with feature sizes down to 5 μm are realized on arbitrary rigid and flexible substrates, exhibiting dichroic ratios of up to 4.6 and stretchability exceeding 100%. Beyond passive optical security, the semiconducting nature of TeNWs allows these oriented arrays to function as active channels in asymmetric Schottky photodetectors, delivering broadband photoresponse (405–1064 nm), an anisotropic photocurrent ratio of 2.35, and an ultrafast response time of 430 μs under self-powered operation. Leveraging this capability, polarization-encoded information can be transduced into polarization-sensitive electrical signals, establishing a hardware-level security paradigm that physically encodes information in the material rather than in algorithms.
n6138ed783720: Stereochemistry underlies structure–function relationships across biology and materials science. Here, we investigate electron transport in oligopeptide stereoisomers using single-molecule experiments and computational modeling. Our results show that stereochemical modifications in tyrosine-based peptides lead to significant variations in molecular conductance and transport distance along the peptide backbone, associated with changes in aromatic side-chain interactions and electronic coupling. In alanine-based peptides, stereochemical modifications alter molecular conductance through secondary-structure interactions associated with β-turn conformations. Molecular dynamics simulations and quantum mechanical calculations reveal the molecular origins of these stereochemistry-dependent structural and electronic properties. Overall, this work shows that stereochemical modification of nonterminal amino acids provides a means to control electron transport through distinct mechanisms involving aromatic side-chain interactions and secondary structure. These results establish stereochemistry as a molecular design parameter for controlling electron transport in peptide-based electronic materials.
n075d9b648d12: Magnetoresistive effects are typically symmetric under magnetization reversal. However, nonlinear spin transport can give rise to unidirectional magnetoresistance in systems with strong spin–orbit interaction and broken inversion symmetry. Here, we report a large magnonic unidirectional spin Hall magnetoresistance (USMR) in a van der Waals antiferromagnet CrPS4 in contact with Pt, driven by the nonequilibrium magnon accumulation with a finite magnon chemical potential. In contrast to conventional magnonic USMR driven by magnetization fluctuations, this effect persists under strong magnetic fields and low temperatures. The magnitude of magnonic USMR in CrPS4/Pt exceeds that of YIG/Pt by more than 2 orders of magnitude and surpasses the electrical USMR in metallic Ta/Co bilayers by a factor of 2. Our results highlight magnon chemical potential gradients for nonlinear magnetoresistance in antiferromagnetic van der Waals heterostructures and open a route to magnon-based antiferromagnetic spintronic functionalities in two-terminal device geometries.
nd95c37a4ec19: Polymer thin films in wearable electronics undergo creep recovery during operation as on-body devices, resulting in unrecoverable strain that subsequently induces mechanical instability in the films. However, the creep recovery behavior of polymer thin films has not been investigated due to their intrinsic fragility and the difficulty in controlling ultralow loads for the films. We evaluate the creep recovery behavior of pseudo-free-standing polymer thin films as a function of creep stress, developing direct creep recovery testing with a feedback-based ultralow-load control system. Polystyrene (PS) thin films exhibit a sharp increase in unrecoverable strain with the onset of crazing. While poly(3-butylthiophene) (P3BT) thin films show a linear increase in the relative ratio of unrecoverable strain with increasing creep stress, poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) thin films exhibit a viscoelastic strain larger than unrecoverable strain. This work reveals the creep recovery behavior of polymer thin films and proposes a direct creep recovery testing method.
nb55bfa734a4d: Temperature can influence competing catalytic pathways differently, but its role in balancing electrocatalytic activity and stability remains underexplored. Now it has been shown that cooling water to near freezing selectively suppresses manganese dioxide dissolution, extending water oxidation lifetime and revealing anomalous subzero kinetics.
n191280d1777b: Defect engineering is promising to solve the photocarrier dynamics mismatch between rapid bulk recombination and sluggish surface oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in PEC water splitting but is limited by forming random or bulk defects. Herein, we adopt a phase and facet modulation strategy to construct a 2D defective spinel β-In2S3 photoanode with highly exposed, well-ordered indium vacancies (VIn). These VIn introduce a shallow acceptor level near the valence band (VB), which induces selective photohole capture to VIn shallow traps. The efficient and fast (∼0.13 ps) photohole transfer from the VB to the VIn state and the sharply elongated lifetime for photoholes accumulated at VIn, by facilitating band-edge exciton dissociation, induce separation efficiency nearly 100% even at low bias. Meanwhile, surface VIn lowers the OER barrier by boosting the conversion of *OH to *O and promotes surface reaction kinetics, enabling the photohole transfer efficiency to reach 95%. Thus, VIn simultaneously acts as photohole-capture centers and surface-active sites to optimize photohole separation and interfacial transfer dynamics. Through introducing and exposing ordered VIn to reaction interfaces, the β-In2S3-2D photoanode achieves a record-high photocurrent density of 9.7 mA cm–2 at 1.23 VRHE and an IPCE reaching 80% without hole scavengers. Such a regulation mechanism can guide reverse design of defective semiconductor photoanodes for efficient PEC conversion.
n09a1cbc0aeea: Adsorbate site hopping, defined here as surface-confined migration of adsorbed species or adsorbate equivalents between distinct sites, is a widespread phenomenon in heterogeneous catalysis and includes spillover between different surface phases. Because it enables communication between spatially separated functionalities, site hopping has often been viewed as a route to bifunctional catalytic synergy and, in some cases, to performance beyond constraints imposed by Brønsted–Evans–Polanyi relationships. However, its catalytic value is conditional rather than universal. Downhill migration to a stronger binding site may increase local barriers for subsequent transformation or introduce site-regeneration penalties, while kinetically accessible hopping may remain irrelevant if it does not reduce the energetic span of the catalytic cycle. In addition, apparent rate enhancements assigned to site hopping can arise from other modes of intersite communication, including desorption–readsorption, subsurface or bulk diffusion, ion–electron intersite coupling, catalyst restructuring, or changes in active-site identity. This Perspective develops a thermodynamic and kinetic framework for distinguishing these processes and assessing when site hopping becomes catalytically consequential. We discuss driving forces, hopping barriers, coverage and dynamic surface effects, kinetic signatures, and diagnostic pitfalls, with the aim of clarifying when site hopping can be used as a catalyst design principle.
nd471b55536b6: 8,12-Guaianolides are a class of sesquiterpene lactones that exhibit diverse biological activities, which are often strongly influenced by structural variations, including the stereochemistry of the C8 oxygen substituent. Here, we report a concise, diastereodivergent approach to both 8α,12- and 8β,12-guaianolide scaffolds from santonin-derived triene 5 by combining engineered cytochrome P450 BM3-catalyzed allylic C–H hydroxylation with a photochemical rearrangement. The P450 BM3 mutant LG-23 selectively hydroxylates the C8α position of 5, whereas a single additional mutation, L437I, inverts the facial selectivity to favor C8β hydroxylation. Structure-guided mutagenesis and docking studies suggest that the β-methyl group of Ile437 remodels the active site and enforces a flipped substrate binding mode that directs the opposite C8 C–H bond toward the heme iron. The utility of this enzymatic stereochemical switch was demonstrated by the synthesis of the 8α,12-guaianolides xerantholide (1) and mikanokryptin (2) and the 8β,12-guaianolide 11,13-dehydroachalensolide (4). This study demonstrates that a single active-site mutation in P450 BM3 can switch the facial selectivity of C–H hydroxylation at one carbon center, providing a strategy for stereodivergent enzymatic oxidation in complex-molecule synthesis.
n7bd1ca9de2cc: Highly active water oxidation catalysts based on earth-abundant elements are strongly demanded for practical application of artificial photosynthesis. An iron complex with a chlorin ligand derived from chlorophyll-a demonstrated the highest turnover frequency (= 21.3 ± 0.3 s–1) and turnover number (= 6920 ± 110) among homogeneous catalysts reported for photocatalytic water oxidation utilizing [RuII(bpy)3]2+ (bpy: 2,2′-bipyridine) and S2O82– as a photosensitizer and a sacrificial electron acceptor, respectively. The molecular nature of the Fe chlorin complex during the photocatalytic water oxidation was confirmed by dynamic light scattering analysis and electrospray ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry. Also, kinetic studies suggested that the rate-determining step is O–O bond formation via coupling of two high-valent iron–oxo species formed by three-electron oxidation of the mononuclear Fe chlorin unit with water. The high planarity of the chlorin ligand enables the high-valent iron–oxo species to approach another iron–oxo unit closely, thereby facilitating O–O bond formation.
n65546dc3d477: Present herein is a gold(I)-catalyzed asymmetric cascade reaction of 1-(1-alkynyl)cyclobutyl ketones. Upon activation by a chiral phosphoric-acid-tethered gold(I) complex, they undertake intramolecular 5-endo-dig cyclization, and the resulting oxocarbenium species engage in an asymmetric 1,2-alkyl migration to generate gold-containing cyclopenta[b]furan carbocations, which can be intercepted by a broad range of nucleophiles, including indoles, pyrroles, alcohols, and amines, providing efficient access to synthetically challenging tetrahydro-4H-cyclopenta[b]furans bearing vicinal bridged quaternary stereocenters with fair to high enantioselectivity. The intermediates can also participate in (3 + 2) annulations with suitable 1,3-dipoles to afford polycyclic architectures with high molecular complexity. Mechanistic studies and density function theory calculations elucidate the key factors governing the catalytic pathways and stereochemical outcomes.
nb9a0fe453199: The incorporation of selected extraframework cations is a common approach to tuning the performance of zeolite catalysts in industrially relevant methanol-to-hydrocarbons (MTH) conversion processes, although the mechanistic origin of their effects remains incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the relationships between MTH and coking kinetics, the nature and distribution of coke deposits, and the positions of extraframework calcium and zinc species in the ZSM-5 catalyst, which promote alkene and aromatic formation, respectively. At comparable Brønsted acid site densities, enhanced aromatics formation over zinc-containing ZSM-5 is accompanied by a 2× higher intrinsic MTH activity and a 150× faster active site loss than over the calcium-containing catalyst. Photoelectron photoion coincidence spectroscopy shows that faster coke-forming kinetics over the zinc-containing catalyst is linked to enhanced formaldehyde formation via methanol dehydrogenation, triggering a cascade of intermediates, such as dienes and aromatics, a pathway inhibited in the calcium-containing catalyst. This also leads to a higher fraction of high-molecular-weight coke in the zinc-containing catalyst and a predominance of surface graphitic coke in the calcium-containing catalyst, as revealed by complementary thermogravimetric, microscopic, and spectroscopic analyses. Powder neutron diffraction indicates that coke preferentially occupies the channel intersections and extends along the straight channels in both catalysts. However, the average coke orientation differs as calcium-containing ZSM-5 comprises more distorted intrapore aromatic deposits, whereas zinc-containing ZSM-5 accommodates more planar aromatic coke. The confinement of coke in micropores is consistent with the preferential location of cations determined by high-resolution X-ray diffraction analysis, which shows that calcium occupies two sites in the sinusoidal channels, with one of these pointing toward the channel intersections, whereas the smaller zinc-associated density is found at sites in five- and six-membered rings between main channels, at the expense of occupancy of sinusoidal channel-based positions. Consequently, faster coke-forming kinetics linked to the dehydrogenation activity of extraframework zinc species, together with lower spatial strain at channel intersections, favor the formation of more condensed, planar-like coke in zinc-containing catalysts. Conversely, the larger size and higher channel occupancy of calcium sites destabilize aromatics and hinder coke formation in this key intersecting zone. These results show that extraframework species influence not only the reaction kinetics but also the local organization and orientation of confined coke, in part through steric constraints associated with their crystallographic location.
n78ac7891ccaf: The rhodium-catalyzed asymmetric hydroformylation (AHF) of vinyl ethers provides a powerful synthetic step to yield chiral aldehydes as products or intermediates for industrially relevant fine chemicals. Out of the 40 chiral ligands tested, the phosphine-phosphorodiamidite (S,S,RP,S)-BettiPhos L7 and the phosphine-phosphoramidite ligand L6 performed best in this transformation, combining high activity, regio- and enantioselectivity. Branched 2-aryloxypropionaldehydes (16 examples) were obtained with b/l-ratios ranging from 3.1:1 to exclusive branched products, and with enantioselectivities between 79 and 94% ee. Interestingly, for these substrates, the selective decomposition of the linear aldehydes to the respective arenols and acrolein via β-hydride elimination was observed. Branched 2-alkyloxypropionaldehydes (3 examples) were obtained with fair b/l-ratios (1.7:1–2.6:1) and good to high enantioselectivities (85–95% ee). The utility of this transformation was demonstrated by synthesizing the commercial herbicide (R)-Mecoprop on a gram scale in 69% yield and 91% ee via hydroformylation of 4-chloro-2-methyl-1-(vinyloxy)benzene, followed by oxidation. The catalytic system could also be used under slightly modified reaction conditions for reductive asymmetric hydroformylation to produce in one-pot chiral 2-aryloxypropanols. The synthetic potential was further explored by applying the tandem asymmetric hydrohydrazonemethylation (AHHM) followed by reduction, yielding γ-chiral N′-substituted acetohydrazides as shown for 6 examples. Hydrogenolysis of the crude product mixtures results in the corresponding chiral primary amines, as demonstrated in the synthesis of 2-phenoxypropanamine from (vinyloxy)benzene with an overall yield of 74% and 94% ee on a gram scale. Moreover, another tandem reaction—specifically, the asymmetric hydrosulfiniminomethylation (AHSM)—enables access to halogen-containing chiral primary amines, as demonstrated by the synthesis of 2-(4-chlorophenoxy)propanamine in an overall yield of 53% and >99% ee.
nd1125c45a8c2: Buried-interface engineering is critical for inverted perovskite solar cells, yet integrating anchoring, charge transport, electrostatic regulation, and defect passivation within single molecular systems often creates intrinsic trade-offs. Here, we use cavity-selective host–guest recognition to construct a modular, recognition-directed interface. The cavity of dipolar 4-tert-butylsulfonylcalix[4]arene (tBSCA) selectively accommodates the terminal phenyl group of substrate-anchored Ph-4PACz. Comparisons with a structurally related calixarene analogue and competing inclusion orientations identify a thermodynamically preferred Ph-4PACz-tBSCA configuration, distinguishing cavity-selective association from nonspecific interactions. This preferred configuration underpins a preferentially organized dipolar interface that retains Ph-4PACz-mediated anchoring and charge transport while enabling tBSCA to regulate interfacial electrostatics, reduce interfacial defect sites, and suppress defect-assisted halide migration and interfacial accumulation. The resulting devices achieve a PCE of 27.36% (certified at 26.74%), and a 110 cm2 module delivers a certified efficiency of 22.61%. These results demonstrate configuration-selective molecular recognition as a strategy for the modular organization of complementary functions at buried perovskite interfaces.
n053a91296ef7: Pure-water membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) represent a promising strategy to eliminate (bi)carbonate salt precipitation for electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2R). However, the absence of alkali metal cations fundamentally restricts CO2 activation and intermediate stabilization, thereby reducing catalytic performance. Here, we overcome this limitation by identifying the ionomer charge density as a key molecular-level parameter associated with pure-water CO2R. By comparing anion-exchange ionomers with varying charge characteristics, we reveal that high-charge-density ionomer (HCDI) introduces a favorable catalyst–membrane interfacial environment, enabling superior macroscopic CO2R performance. HCDI-enabled MEAs achieve >99% CO Faradaic efficiency at 100 mA cm–2 and sustain ∼92% at 1000 mA cm–2. In situ diagnosis and electrochemical characterization reveal that the HCDI-functionalized interface produces a substantial *CO signal, while concurrently suppressing hydrogen evolution. By decoupling cation effects from liquid electrolytes, these findings support interfacial ionomer charge density as a useful comparative parameter for pure-water CO2 MEA electrolyzers.
n6bade4f80897: Integrating alternative oxidation reactions (AORs) into photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems is promising for unassisted hydrogen production and value-added chemical synthesis, yet organic semiconductor (OS) photoanodes suffer from poor charge extraction and short carrier lifetimes. Here, we address this bottleneck by stabilizing long-lived hole polarons through macroporous tin oxide (mcSnO2) interlayers. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that accelerated electron extraction through mcSnO2 stabilizes hole polaron states, substantially prolonging carrier lifetimes. Consequently, the optimized organic photoanodes outperform bare counterparts by more than 5.5-fold, retaining 74% of their initial photocurrent over 15 h for iodide oxidation and 61% over 35 h for ascorbic acid oxidation. Furthermore, integrating this robust organic photoanode with an OS-based photocathode enables the first bias-free organic PEC tandem cell coupling hydrogen evolution with AORs, delivering a remarkable solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 1.4%. These findings establish interfacial carrier lifetime engineering as an effective strategy for realizing high-performance and durable organic PEC systems.
n40622435b3df: A triazine–heptazine homojunction in porous carbon nitride nanotubes enables efficient charge separation and oxygen activation, enhancing visible-light-driven H 2 O 2 production and selective benzyl alcohol oxidation to benzaldehyde.

n7346fcd5e078: Interface engineering has emerged as a critical strategy for advancing perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs), enabling remarkable improvements in the device efficiency, stability, and spectral purity. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of interface engineering in PeLEDs, beginning with the fundamental principles that govern carrier injection, transport, and recombination at heterojunctions between perovskite emitters and charge-transport layers. We then survey advanced characterization techniques, including photoelectron spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, and time-resolved optical methods, that elucidate interfacial energy-level alignment, defect states, charge dynamics, and degradation pathways. On the basis of these insights, we systematically discuss versatile engineering strategies, such as self-assembled monolayers, dipole interlayers, dimensional regulation, and passivation schemes, to mitigate non-radiative recombination, balance charge fluxes, and enhance operational stability. Finally, we highlight emerging applications spanning high-resolution displays, flexible lighting, and lasing while outlining key challenges and future directions toward commercial realization. This Review aims to offer a holistic framework linking interfacial design to device performance, guiding next-generation PeLED development.
n65cca399b7fe: The interfacial electron-transfer process acts as a pivotal kinetic determinant of electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency, governing the generation of excited-state emitters and thus dictating the intensity and stability of ECL signals. Currently, harnessing diverse nanomaterials has driven significant advances in the development of novel ECL luminophores and the activation of coreactants. However, most of these luminophores exhibit low ECL efficiency in aqueous media, and the intrinsic reaction and activation mechanisms remain ambiguous because of their complex structures and compositions. Notably, tuning electron-transfer pathways at the molecular/atomic level can not only enable efficient signal amplification but also facilitate the tracking of reaction pathways, thereby providing deeper insights into the fundamental mechanisms underlying ECL processes. This Review comprehensively summarizes advances during the past five years in tuning interfacial electron transfer to enhance ECL. Furthermore, we highlight progress in electron-transfer-mediated signal amplification strategies for highly sensitive ECL biosensing and bioimaging applications. Finally, we propose and discuss the challenges and perspectives associated with improving the ECL efficiency through the modulation of electron transfer processes. Precise regulation of interfacial electron transfer holds substantial promise for advancing ECL theories, clarifying reaction mechanisms, and expanding the scope of ECL-based bioanalytical applications.

ne736f6de4e25: Dual-anion regulation induces covalency-driven amorphization in Li-Zr-Cl electrolytes, promoting Li+ transport, oxidative stability, and mechanical compliance. n7385a583557b: Curvature couples polarization, crystalline defects, and interfacial electrostatics in freestanding ferroelectric oxides. Here, we examine bent epitaxial Pb(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3/SrTiO3/Pb(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3 (PZT/STO/PZT) membranes using atomic-resolution electron microscopy, strain and polarization mapping, relative projected-potential reconstruction, and molecular dynamics simulations. The tensile-side PZT remains comparatively lattice-continuous and accommodates bending mainly through polarization rotation and domain reorganization. The compressive-side PZT exhibits dislocations, slip-related lattice offsets, surface steps, and localized strain concentration. Curvature-series observations and images across U-shaped and N-shaped regions indicate that the defect-rich region follows the local compressive stress state. Bending also breaks the approximate electrostatic symmetry of the two PZT/STO interfaces: the tensile side shows weakened negative interfacial contrast, whereas the compressive side shows a dislocation-associated increase in relative projected potential. These results identify curvature as a variable for selecting polar versus plastic relaxation pathways and modulating interfacial electrostatic landscapes in flexible ferroelectric heterostructures.
nd8372d4936c1: Upconverting lanthanide-doped particles are widely used as nanoscale temperature sensors, particularly in biological and photonic environments. However, extending their functionality to simultaneously measure temperature and light intensity remains a challenge, as the luminescent response is highly sensitive to both the environment composition and its temperature. In this work, we combine deep-learning methods with large-scale spectral data sets to investigate the reliability of Er/Yb-doped particles to function as dual sensors. Spectral data are collected from single particles levitating in vacuum and ensembles of particles in application-relevant wet and dry media. Although traditional ratiometric methods reliably retrieve temperature irrespective of the environment and specific experimental apparatus, they fail to disentangle the complex dependencies needed for dual sensing. Our trained models overcome these limitations, accurately predicting both temperature and laser power despite environmental variability. This approach opens a new route toward robust, data-driven sensing with upconverting particles in complex or fluctuating conditions.
n973fa9c05764: Flexible photonic devices and soft microlasers have attracted increasing attention for wearable sensing, biomedical monitoring, and deformable optoelectronic systems. Their mechanical compliance enables intimate contact with soft biological tissues, allowing optical signals to be modulated by external mechanical stimuli. Such characteristics make flexible laser-based platforms particularly suitable for mechanical sensing and physiological signal detection. In this work, we present a flexible microlaser array-based photonic platform designed for mechanical sensing and pulse monitoring. By integrating microscale laser emitters into a soft, transparent matrix with a microstructured architecture, the device maintains stable laser emission while responding to external pressure and dynamic strain. The optical response of the microlaser array exhibits sensitivity to mechanical perturbations, enabling the detection of periodic signals associated with the human pulse. This work highlights the potential of flexible laser photonics as a versatile tool for noninvasive mechanical and physiological sensing in wearable healthcare applications.
nba03913388a3: Using two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) ferromagnets in spintronic devices can enhance their performance through well-controlled vdW interfaces and reduced power consumption. Cr2Te3 appears as a promising candidate because of its strong perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, but the Curie temperature is limited to 180 K. In this work, we use annealing in air to uncover the magnetic phase diagram of Cr2Te3. We correlate magnetic properties with layer stacking and the interlayer distance; both depend strongly on the annealing temperature. In particular, disorder in layer stacking plays a key role in the magnetic properties of Cr2Te3 and more generally of vdW ferromagnets. By annealing at 375 °C, we can eventually raise the Tc of Cr2Te3 up to 303 K in the epitaxial Cr2Te3/WSe2 vdW heterostructure with in-plane magnetic anisotropy. This work provides a simple method to control the magnetic properties of 2D ferromagnets and incorporate them into spintronics devices.
n5ec1c3f27341: Silicon anodes enable high-energy-density Li-ion batteries but face reversibility challenges when operating under extreme temperature and charge-rate conditions. Now, a liquid electrolyte design results in interface protection and reduced electrode expansion during such operation, while also having lithium plating tolerance.
nb2bc4b44a338: Cathode interlayers play a pivotal role in improving the performance of organic solar cells. Yao, Zhang, Zhang, Wang et al. show a stepwise solvent treatment to achieve a vertically aligned cathode interlayer, enabling a certified efficiency of 20.65% in binary organic solar cells.

nb70f07fba36a: Stacking-controllable 2D In2Se3 grown by chemical vapour deposition reveals a strong dependence of ferroelectricity on stacking order. na37558c52271: By creating permanent cavities of well-defined size and shape within a fluid, porous liquids bring the precise control over gases afforded by microporous solids to the realm of liquids.
