n465e258842c4: Silver-catalyzed ethylene epoxidation is a cornerstone of the chemical industry, yet the operando surface structure of Ag nanoparticles and the identity of selectivity-governing active sites remain elusive. Here, we integrate machine learning potentials, stochastic surface walking global optimization, molecular dynamics simulation, and statistical analysis to resolve the surface landscape of Ag nanoparticles approaching experimentally relevant sizes under reaction conditions. Oxygen-induced reconstruction transforms pristine Ag facets into a globally amorphous oxide layer composed of three types of locally ordered ring motifs interspersed with structural defects. A pentagonal motif (ring5), topologically required to accommodate nanoparticle curvature and absent in conventional slab models, dominates the surface across all investigated particle sizes. Its recessed central Ag atom acts as an electronic charge buffer that weakens the critical C–Ag bond in the oxametallacycle intermediate, conferring high intrinsic ethylene oxide selectivity. Microkinetic analyses confirm that the oxygen species of ring5 regulate ethylene oxide yield, peaking at a nanoparticle oxidation degree of O/Ag ≈ 0.3–0.4. This work establishes a statistical paradigm for decoding active phases on realistic catalyst surfaces through dynamic structural ensembles.
nc8456e98e64c: The complex structure of polyurethanes (PURs) presents a major barrier to their efficient recycling. Here, we report a chemoenzymatic cascade that enables the simultaneous recycling and upcycling of PUR through rapid alkaline pretreatment followed by urethanase-catalyzed depolymerization. Using in-house-synthesized model polyether- and polyester-based PUR elastomers, we establish that soft-segment chemistry dictates the composition, morphology, and accessibility of the pretreated residues, thereby governing the efficiency of the subsequent enzymatic hydrolysis. This insight enabled translation of the cascade to a commercial PUR elastomer, achieving >93% chemical conversion and recovery of up to 1 mM 4,4′-methylenedianiline (MDA) (97.2% purity), corresponding to a 40-fold increase over the nonenzymatic control, together with polyols obtained in 95% isolated yield that were directly reused for PUR synthesis. Mechanistic studies further show that alkaline pretreatment enhances substrate accessibility for the enzyme, and structural analysis of urethanase SP2 reveals a carbamate-specific hydrogen-bonding interaction that promotes urethane hydrolysis while minimizing esterase activity. The cascade was additionally applied to highly crosslinked commercial PUR foams and adhesives, demonstrating its versatility toward industrially relevant waste streams. Overall, this work establishes a mechanistically informed chemoenzymatic platform for PUR depolymerization and provides a strategy for converting chemically recalcitrant PUR waste into reusable molecular building blocks.
n48f8def67571: A modified colloidal atomic layer deposition at room temperature grows a vacancy-ordered Cs2SnCl6 shell epitaxially on CsPbCl3 nanocrystals, avoiding the core degradation and parasitic shell nucleation that accompany high-temperature routes. The resulting core–shell nanocrystals achieve an absolute photoluminescence quantum yield of 62% and retain 65% of their emission after six months of ambient storage and 30% after 48 h of exposure to added water.
n874a803e9337: Rechargeable magnesium (Mg) metal batteries are promising high-energy-density alternatives to lithium-ion systems, yet sluggish cathode kinetics hinder their development. Departing from the conventional host-centric view, we demonstrate that reversibility in Mg batteries can be governed by electrolyte-derived reaction chemistry. Here, we harness trace water to impart controlled electrolyte reactivity, enabling electrolyte-derived Mg/Cl-containing species to participate in cathode activation. In tunnel-type MnO2, the regulated electrolyte induces lattice expansion and improves electrochemical reversibility. In organic cathodes, improved rechargeability is consistent with a stabilizing role of Cl– in anion-coupled redox. Because polar-solvent chemistry can irreversibly passivate Mg metal, a Sn/MgCl2 artificial interface suppresses parasitic anode reactions while preserving cathode activation. This strategy enables reversible electrochemistry across oxide, organic, and conversion cathodes, including α/γ-MnO2, methylphenothiazine, tetrathiafulvalene, and hybrid I2/O2 systems. These findings establish electrolyte-derived chemical activation as a guiding principle for regulating cathode reaction pathways in magnesium batteries.
n7b18684a7f4e: Leveraging oxygen redox in lithium-rich layered oxides paves the way for increasing the energy density of lithium-ion batteries, whose practical implementation is plagued by poor stability. Although a uniform Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is suggested to improve cycle stability, the synthesis–structure relationship governing domain formation remains underexplored. Here, we show that Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is derived by the precursor structure according to the degree of transition-metal separation. Through a comparative investigation of the synthesis mechanism, we reveal the templating effect that more clustered transition-metal oxide precursors lead to more localized Li2MnO3-like ordering in the final cathodes, a tendency also observed with a different lithium source. Furthermore, it is corroborated that cathodes with more dispersed Li2MnO3-like ordering derived from less-ordered precursors exhibit improved electrochemical stability with a mitigated voltage decay. Our findings highlight the significance of precursor design and engineering for structural regulation of high-performance lithium-rich layered oxide cathodes.
n8d648f4076f8: The rational combination of multiple electrolyte additives is a promising strategy for constructing stable interphases in lithium-ion batteries. However, unintended additive interactions can alter the preferential reduction/oxidation pathways at electrode surfaces, compromising cell performance. Specifically, an electron-deficient boron-embedded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from LiBOB promotes the reduction of the electron-rich nitrile moieties of SN, disrupting fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)-driven SEI construction. Based on this mechanism, SN was replaced with triisopropanolamine borate (TPAB), which mitigates transition metal dissolution through its amine moiety while forming a robust borate-based cathode electrolyte interphase. Moreover, TPAB combined with LiBOB avoided detrimental side reductions at the anode–electrolyte interface. The FEC-LiBOB-TPAB combination creates thermally stable interphases on the Gr-Si anode and LiNi0.91Co0.08Al0.01O2 cathode (4.8 mAh cm–2), enabling 68.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 45 °C and 1C.
n03850d8c938a: Polymer film capacitors are fundamental to modern power electronics, yet low permittivity restricts their energy density. By employing a micro-structured blade, we generate intense local shear flow fields that exert hydrodynamic tension to drive a coil-stretch transition. This process drives an α-to-β phase transition and templates the growth of oriented, polar-phase-rich crystal structures. Furthermore, we develop a stage-wise regulation strategy using binary solvents to orchestrate evaporation dynamics, effectively trapping these metastable shear-induced conformations before relaxation. Effective across the PVDF copolymer family, this method enables P(VDF-HFP) films to achieve a high energy density of 20.05 J/cm3, a 44% improvement over conventional casting. This work provides a general, non-chemical pathway for manufacturing high-performance functional polymers through multi-physical field synergistic regulation.

n80fcdd851a13: An atomically precise, ligand-capped Cu49 nanocluster is demonstrated to efficiently catalyze the semihydrogenation of alkynes at room temperature. nb91102874037: While polyester waste represents a valuable carbon resource for chemical production, its upcycling typically involves multiple steps for polymer depolymerization, intermediate separation, and subsequent conversion. n8662555b8320: Although organosilicon compounds containing different carbon substituents are ubiquitous in synthetic chemistry, their preparation is challenging. Laboratory synthesis commonly relies on the sequential substitution of tetrachlorosilane or tetraalkoxysilanes, producing complex mixtures that require demanding purification. This arises from limited control over nucleophilic substitution in functionalized silanes containing three or four (identical) leaving groups. Here we introduce an experimentally straightforward and reliable procedure for the preparation of both hetero- and homoleptic silanes using an overlooked monobromination of primary and secondary hydrosilanes. An equimolar amount of elemental bromine converts a Si–H bond into an Si–Br bond without ‘overbromination’. This step also shows exceptional functional-group tolerance to existing substituents at the silicon atom. Unsaturated moieties as well as heteroatom and heteroaryl groups are compatible. When performed in an iterative fashion, multihydrosilanes can be selectively converted into secondary, tertiary and quaternary silanes with two, three or four different carbon substituents in high yields. These functionalized silicon building blocks are relevant to synthetic chemistry as well as applied chemistry materials.
n2f6e6b14dbd3: The stepwise installation of carbon substituents at silicon starting from tetrachlorosilane or tetraalkoxysilanes is burdened by chemoselectivity issues, typically affording product mixtures. n617dd9db8a0f: Advances in dynamic covalent chemistry have dramatically broadened its use in polymer research. Cyclic disulfide bonds are a widely used, versatile platform for engineering dynamic polymers. The resulting polymers leverage the dynamic character of exocyclic linkages associated with cyclic disulfide bonds, along with modular, tailorable chain-end functionalities to enable self-healing and chemical recycling. This review summarizes recent advances in dynamic polymer chemistry based on cyclic disulfide bonds that have enabled new design principles for the development and innovation in advanced polymers. We highlight living/controlled polymerization strategies for cyclic disulfide monomers, covering the principal polymerization strategies and mechanisms, and discuss the future challenges and prospective directions of the field in the context of emerging societal and technological demands.
nb67843be428e: Interlayer CO 3 2− polarizes the Ni–O–Fe motif in NiFe-LDH, inducing differentiated electronic responses at the Ni and Fe sites. This site-dependent electronics promote the early formation of Ni 3+ –O and *OOH, enabling ampere-level alkaline OER.
nc5a607337783: Rational molecular engineering of the perovskite/hole transport layer interface offers a promising route to simultaneously address inefficient charge extraction, defect-mediated recombination, and lead leakage in CsPbI3–xBrx perovskite solar cells. Herein, we introduce 2,2′-dinitro-9,9′-spirobifluorene (DN-SBF) as an interfacial molecular bridge to tackle these challenges. DN-SBF optimizes energy level alignment, establishes π–π interactions, and forms exciplexes with Spiro-OMeTAD, thereby facilitating interfacial charge transport. Meanwhile, DN-SBF passivates undercoordinated Pb2+ through multiple coordination modes, including robust bidentate chelation formed by adjacent nitro groups, effectively passivating defects and suppressing non-radiative recombination. Importantly, multipoint coordination immobilizes leachable Pb2+, substantially mitigating lead leakage and improving film biocompatibility. As a result, DN-SBF-engineered CsPbI3–xBrx devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 22.40% along with significantly enhanced operational and environmental stability. This work highlights the potential of versatile molecular bridges to concurrently enhance performance, stability, and eco-friendliness, which may contribute to the development of more sustainable perovskite photovoltaics.

ned9501745b95: Transition metal fluorides (TMFs) are promising conversion-type cathode materials for high-energy lithium–metal batteries owing to their exceptionally high theoretical energy density, making them attractive for demanding applications such as electric aviation. However, their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish conversion kinetics, pronounced voltage hysteresis, and poor electrochemical reversibility. Understanding the structural and chemical evolution of TMFs and the electrode–electrolyte interphase formed during cycling is essential for improving their performance. Monodisperse nanocrystalline TMFs are ideal model systems for high-resolution transmission electron microscopy because their uniform size, morphology, and electron transparency enable representative nanoscale characterization. Here, we investigate a reproducible colloidal synthesis of monodisperse, single-crystalline CoF2 nanorods and elucidate the mechanisms governing their formation to achieve precise control over particle size and aspect ratio. By independently varying reaction time, temperature, precursor composition, and ligand chemistry, we identify the key factors controlling precursor decomposition, burst nucleation, phase selection, and anisotropic crystal growth. These insights provide a transferable framework for the controlled synthesis of a broad range of transition metal fluoride nanocrystals.
n4598f3ccb9e9: In anode-free Li metal batteries, a bare current collector must be converted into a reversible Li metal anode during the first charge, making Li nucleation decisive for reversibility. However, how current collector microstructure governs Li nucleation and growth remains poorly understood, since prior studies focused on single-crystal surfaces to identify favorable crystallographic orientations, leaving grain boundaries unexplored. Here, we identify grain boundary density and character in copper current collectors as key regulators of Li deposition uniformity. Systematic annealing decouples grain size from surface chemistry, revealing that deposition uniformity improves with copper grain coarsening but saturates as disordered boundaries are eliminated during grain growth, leaving predominantly low-energy configurations. Atomistic simulations show disordered boundaries impose high barriers to Li adatom migration, whereas ordered boundaries and adjacent low-index terraces provide low-barrier pathways for redistribution. Copper foils engineered beyond this threshold sustain uniform Li plating across diverse electrolytes and improve cyclability in anode-free cells.
n9f4039694a62: Light-emitting diodes (LEDs) based on colloidal InAs quantum dots (QDs) have emerged as promising light sources for the short-wave infrared (SWIR) range. However, their development is limited by relatively low photoluminescence quantum yield as well as intrinsic device design challenges. Zirconium-doped indium oxide (InZrO) was used as the bottom transparent electrode owing to its significantly higher infrared transparency compared to the commonly employed tin-doped indium oxide (ITO). These two key innovations pushed the EL beyond 1500 nm, with external quantum efficiencies of 3.0, 1.2, and 0.6% at 1093, 1198, and 1547 nm, respectively.
n677d8e82fc56: Conventional carbonization of semi-coke induces excessive ordering of aromatic skeletons, producing dense graphitic structures that hinder Na+ intercalation and suppress low-potential plateau capacity. Here, we develop a rapid thermomechanical coupling sintering strategy using moderate pressure to drive π–π interactions and topological reconfiguration of aromatic units. This process suppresses excessive graphitization while constructing interconnected, twisted pseudo-graphitic domains with abundant closed nanopores. At 1000 mA g–1, PTR-HC reaches 80% SOC in ≈14.4 min and retains 90.1% of its plateau capacity, enabled by abundant Na+ storage sites and rapid diffusion pathways. Kinetic analyses reveal accelerated Na+ transport and a thin, NaF-rich solid-electrolyte interphase with fewer organic components. In situ XRD and Raman attribute slope capacity to surface/defect adsorption and intercalation and the plateau capacity to quasi-metallic Na clusters in closed pores. This work establishes pressure-driven topological engineering as a promising strategy for upgrading semi-coke into fast-charging hard carbon with high plateau-capacity retention.
nadb66549bf6c: Interfacial losses at the perovskite/C60 and C60/metal contacts limit inverted perovskite solar cell performance. Here, we introduce a vacuum-evaporated molecule with giant spontaneous orientation polarization, 6F-2PI, for simultaneously tailoring both interfaces. Incorporating 6F-2PI increases the work function of perovskite, reducing the conduction band offset at the perovskite/C60 interface, which facilitates electron extraction. Concurrently, its phthalimide moieties passivate defect states, suppressing nonradiative recombination, as evidenced by a 0.03 eV recovery in quasi-Fermi level splitting. At the C60/metal interface, 6F-2PI also delivers efficient charge extraction, improved interfacial contact, and thermal resilience. Moreover, its hydrophobic fluorinated units prevent moisture ingress. Consequently, this dual-interface modulation boosts PCE from 18.5% to 22.5% with exceptional device stability, retaining over 90% of its initial efficiency after 2000 h under ambient conditions. Furthermore, this framework exhibits universal compatibility across both vacuum-deposited and solution-processed devices and simplifies processing for mass production.

n37d5bb016408: The bacterial surface represents the primary interface between pathogens and hosts, yet its chemical and architectural complexity challenges conventional classification. This Review examines structural organization, molecular composition, and biogenesis of bacterial surface components across the Gracilicutes and Terrabacteria clades, linking mechanistic detail to pathogenic function. We describe lipid diversity, integral membrane protein biogenesis, and lipoprotein processing at the inner membrane and how these components support surface remodeling, secretion, and virulence. We then examine the peptidoglycan layer and its role in immune recognition and surface protein display, teichoic acids and their contributions to antimicrobial resistance and immune evasion, and S layers, whose crystalline arrays mediate adhesion and immune modulation. The outer membrane section covers lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis, outer membrane protein biogenesis and folding, lipoprotein trafficking, and contributions to pathogenicity, while the mycobacterial section addresses the mycolyl-arabinogalactan-peptidoglycan complex and virulence factors. We discuss bacterial capsule diversity, biosynthesis, and use as vaccine antigens, along with adhesive surface structures such as fimbriae, pili, and curli fibers and their roles in colonization and biofilm formation, before covering secretion systems types I through XI and their contributions to virulence. This Review provides a framework for understanding how bacterial surface diversity shapes infection and identifies chemical vulnerabilities for therapeutics.
n3f072c4ef5be: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer exceptional structural resolution for investigating how local environments govern catalytic behavior and, ultimately, for controlling these effects through catalyst design. Yet, atomic dispersion does not imply a single or fully defined catalytic environment. The behavior of atomically dispersed active centers is shaped by a hierarchical local environment comprising persistent and transient contributions, while also being influenced by an extended reaction environment that intersects with the local environment in controlling reactivity and can become integrated into it. Establishing these boundaries and understanding how these contributions evolve and interact are central challenges in the interpretation and design of SACs. Here, we critically examine how local environments are generated and controlled, experimentally and theoretically resolved across spatial and temporal scales, transformed from synthesis through operation and deactivation, and linked to catalytic performance through structural, energetic, and electronic descriptors. By integrating aspects that are often considered separately and highlighting those that remain insufficiently addressed, we provide a roadmap toward the predictive, environment-driven design of SACs and a deeper understanding of catalytic phenomena.
n98cc28f955b7: Regenerated cellulose (RC), derived from natural cellulose through dissolution and regeneration processes, has emerged as a sustainable, versatile, and cost-effective material for advanced electronic devices. With unique hierarchical structures, abundant hydroxy groups, and excellent mechanical and thermal properties, RC allows extensive customization of its characteristics, offering biocompatibility, flexibility, processability, and environmental friendliness. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in RC-based electronics, focusing on its multiscale molecular configuration, dissolution and regeneration mechanisms, and functionalization and engineering strategies. It first provides a detailed molecular-level analysis of RC structures and formation mechanisms. The principles and strategies of cellulose dissolution and regeneration are then discussed, with emphasis on solvent systems and structure-regulating mechanisms essential for processing control. Functionalization strategies are categorized into direct modification and hybridization with functional materials. Notably, the hybridization approach involves the development of conductive, semiconductive, and insulating RC composites, evaluated from the perspectives of material selection, interfacial design, and processing techniques. Subsequently, engineering approaches to enhance mechanical strength, electrical conductivity, and optical transparency are explored. Applications of RC in sensors, actuators, circuits, energy harvesting and storage devices, and electromagnetic shielding devices are highlighted, demonstrating its potential to drive sustainable innovation in electronics. Finally, future directions are proposed to address remaining challenges, paving the way for RC to contribute to eco-friendly, high-performance electronic devices.

n8f2204474093: Hydrogen is a promising energy carrier due to its clean and versatile nature, offering opportunities for decarbonizing diverse sectors. Hydrogen utilization in many applications relies on identifying and understanding materials with exceptional hydrogen storage and transport properties. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive investigation of the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of hydrogenation reactions in ternary ABO3 perovskites using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML) screening. We performed DFT simulations for a diverse range of perovskites featuring a variety of A-site cations (Ca, Sr, Ba) and B-site cations (Co, Fe, Mn, Ce, Ti, Zr) across various phases (cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, and hexagonal). By computing all data at the same theoretical level, we establish a consistent framework to compare how crystal phase, lattice-site chemistry, and host electronic structure govern hydrogen incorporation and diffusion. Therefore, we identify hexagonal SrMnO3, cubic SrFeO3, and hexagonal BaFeO3 as particularly promising candidates, combining favorable hydrogenation thermodynamics (ΔG < 1 eV) with low rotation and hopping barriers (<0.2 eV), while orthorhombic phases, although thermodynamically preferred, suffer from proton trapping, highlighting the importance of phase engineering toward cubic/hexagonal frameworks. Ab initio molecular dynamics further support this phase-dependent kinetic picture by showing relatively facile H diffusion in cubic SrFeO3 but much slower proton motion in orthorhombic BaCeO3 under the same conditions. By incorporating spatial and electronic descriptors with the DFT data into our ML models, we further develop a mechanistically motivated ML model based on structural and electronic descriptors to screen hydrogenation thermodynamics across 111 ternary ABO3 compositions. This model led to the identification of two additional promising candidates, hexagonal BaPdO3 and cubic BaSnO3, which were subsequently validated by DFT calculations. These findings provide a foundation for the rational design of ABO3 perovskites and demonstrate the potential of ML-driven frameworks with chemical insights to accelerate materials discovery in energetic and catalytic applications.
n84be227f2011: The propagation of both catalyst diffusion and reaction fronts in a polymeric chemically amplified resist (CAR) is evaluated by time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) depth profiling, and is compared with the propagation of catalyst diffusion fronts in inert resist analogues. We report that catalysts display accelerated and highly non-Fickian dynamics in the reactive CAR, even when located well behind the propagation front, while simple Fickian diffusion is observed for the same conditions in inert resist analogues. The complex catalyst dynamics of reactive systems is attributed to two key factors: (1) Transient free volume following deprotection events, which is a long-hypothesized acceleration mechanism acting on the diffusion front; and (2) a newly identified plasticization process induced by inert, nonvolatile byproducts of catalyst photoactivation. We propose a physics-informed model of enhanced catalyst diffusion due to the independent contributions of these two processes, and demonstrate that this model coupled to a first-order reaction provides a reasonable prediction of both the diffusion and reaction fronts. Our study presents a critical evaluation of mechanisms that control the spatial extent of reaction in CARs, and suggests that quantitative models of the patterning process should account for the impact of nonvolatile catalyst activation byproducts.

n91d94e745e84: Are ether electrolytes inherently hazardous? ne37abb50eb58: Next-generation two-dimensional electronics require robust insulating layers that effectively control current without compromising device performance. n0d952b2b1d7b: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are a class of crystalline, porous networks constructed by polymerization of organic building blocks. This approach enables control through catalyst-to-monomer ratios and allows the rapid synthesis, within hours, of imide-, imine-, hydrazone- and sp2-carbon-linked COFs with high crystallinity and porosity. The method further supports catalyst reuse and 1,000-fold scale-up, producing COFs with benchmark proton conductivity, establishing hydrogen-bonding catalysis as a versatile route for scalable COF synthesis and applications. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are typically synthesized under harsh acid- or base-catalysed conditions. Here a hydrogen-bonding catalysis strategy based on reusable benzimidazole enables the rapid and scalable production of COFs with high crystallinity and porosity, offering a general route to imide, imine, hydrazone and sp2-carbon-linked COF synthesis.
nf0562d26e0df: Porosity has long been considered a property exclusive to solids, yet a new class of materials now combines permanent, well defined pores with the ability to flow. n819e845d5be8: The performance of energy storage devices utilizing multilayered materials is governed by the complex interactions between electrolyte ions and the electrode. nca948f974a8a: A large number of publications, using diverse production techniques, are demonstrating the potential of metal halide perovskite thin-film devices. na1cf152b01fc: The electrochemical carbon monoxide oxidation reaction (COOR) is an attractive anodic alternative to the oxygen evolution reaction, offering a route to lower the energy demand of electrosynthesis while utilizing abundant industrial waste gas. na2ef69e2788a: Integrating dry carbon electrodes (CEs) into inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) offers a solvent-free, scalable route to low-cost photovoltaics. nc8d8f7d0533e: Two-dimensional/three-dimensional (2D/3D) mixed tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free photovoltaic absorbers, but uncontrolled crystallization produces excessive low-n phases that impede charge extraction due to a quantum confinement effect. n3f9ff6cc68a9: Two-dimensional infrared (2DIR) spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for probing the structure and picosecond dynamics of complex, condensed-phase systems at the molecular level. In electrolytes and ionic liquids, where physicochemical properties arise from the interplay between solvation and ionic interactions, 2DIR spectroscopy provides unique insights into intermolecular interactions and dynamical processes that are often inaccessible to conventional spectroscopies. This review highlights seminal and recent advances in understanding the behavior of these systems using 2DIR spectroscopy, with particular emphasis on spectral diffusion, vibrational relaxation, and chemical exchange dynamics. The review also describes how complementary information from the vibrational modes of solvents, salts, and external probes enables detailed characterization of ion–ion interactions, hydrogen-bonding networks, and solvation environments, providing a molecular framework of the structure and time evolution of these charged systems. Moreover, particular attention is given to the dynamics of distinct molecular moieties and to the role of specific anions, cations, and solvent environments in governing behavior on femtosecond to picosecond time scales. Finally, the review describes current challenges, including the limited availability of intrinsic vibrational reporters and experimental constraints, and key open questions in electrochemical and energy-relevant systems that remain despite an extensive number of studies in the area.

n0204b953e2c2: The incorporation of noble metals into iron oxide nanomaterials represents an effective strategy to tailor their redox and structural properties through metal-oxide interactions. In situ grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GI-XRD) during heat treatment under H2 provides insight into the evolution of these effects, showing (i) suppression of the hematite minor phase already after Pd impregnation and (ii) magnetite major phase lattice expansion during H2 treatment, both occurring exclusively in the presence of Pd. Magnetic measurements reveal an overall magnetization increase upon Pd incorporation, with a nonlinear dependence on Pd loading reflecting the balance between enhanced iron reducibility and lattice disorder. ncc10780a8982: Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and low-cost option for scalable energy storage; however, their practical reversibility is limited by nonuniform Zn plating/stripping and dendritic growth. n2e01c45604e0: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) offers a sustainable route to hydrogen production, yet its practical deployment is limited by trade-offs among activity, stability, and precursor cost of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. nd3add93a99bc: Polymer coatings are widely used to stabilize silicon anodes, yet repeated volume changes can fracture the coating and accelerate continuous SEI reconstruction. nd7bb92b5f0b0: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. Thus, the triplet-state lifetime is a key parameter in solid-state upconversion.
n7217e9742006: Extensively fluorinated aramid polymers fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticle tubes with continuous internal lumens. Stabilized by F–H–F interactions, these abiotic channels enable ultrafast and highly selective water transport across membranes, surpassing natural aquaporins while maintaining excellent salt rejection.
n36c28ff1dc93: Marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) techniques have the potential to remove legacy emitted carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it durably in ocean reservoirs. While the ocean’s vast surface area and buffering capacity offer benefits for scaling removal, monitoring remains challenging. This comprehensive review of marine carbonate system observing and monitoring technologies finds that mCDR processes span multiple scales, often at the edges of existing platform and sensing capability. While some mCDR observing and monitoring is possible today, challenges will arise as experiments and operations expand. Leaps forward in assessing the novel scales of mCDR processes will emerge from low-energy, low-cost, highly durable sensors; innovative deployment platforms; cooperative sensing networks; dedicated model validation programs; and decision support tools. This review is intended to serve as a guide to the history, ongoing innovation, and transformative vision of future marine carbonate system observing and monitoring informed by mCDR.
n20dda3652070: The palmierite oxides are a promising family of ion conductors, and understanding how compositional modification affects their structure and, in turn, their ionic conductivity is pivotal for unlocking high ionic conductivity in these solid electrolytes. Here, we investigate the Sr3V2-xMoxO8+x/2 series (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.4), establishing a solubility limit at x = 0.2, and demonstrating that Mo-substituted compositions exhibit bulk O2– conductivity approximately 2 orders of magnitude higher than the pristine composition at 600 °C. Combined X-ray and neutron diffraction refinement shows little change in the average crystallographic structure, prompting questions about its local structure and dynamics. Using ab initio molecular dynamics, bond-valence site-energy calculations, and 51V and 17O solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy supported by density functional theory calculations, we demonstrate that Mo6+ incorporation generates a new oxygen environment consistent with the formation of a charge-compensating interstitial O3 site. While V5+ remains tetrahedrally coordinated throughout the series, Mo6+ exhibits both MoO4 and distorted trigonal bipyramidal MoO5 coordination polyhedra, with the latter arising from the occupation of O3. This O3 site is proposed to bridge neighboring MOn polyhedra along the ab-plane, shortening the O2– jump distances and shifting the conduction mechanism from a 3D cooperative rotational mechanism to a 2D interstitial-based one.
n87b19c66d964: Incorporating multiple anions into perovskite-type frameworks provides a handle to design innovative lattices and trigger exotic properties. Inverse Lieb lattices have been receiving substantial interest as hosts for d-wave altermagnetism. One mixed-anion system in which these lattices have been experimentally realized is layered oxychalcogenides. By employing a high-pressure, high-temperature synthesis method, we introduce Na2Mn2OS2 as an additional member of this family of compounds. Na2Mn2OS2 adopts an antiperovskite-derived structure, consisting of layers of face-sharing MnO2S4 octahedra. Magnetization and neutron diffraction data reveal that the phase undergoes magnetic ordering below 144 K. The low-temperature magnetic structure has zero net magnetization and is invariant under a combination of rotation and time reversal, thereby fulfilling the symmetry criteria to be considered as an altermagnet candidate. Electronic band structure calculations demonstrate that the phase contains spin-polarized bands, providing further evidence that Na2Mn2OS2 can be described as an altermagnet. An electrochemical investigation of this compound was performed, aiming both to tailor the physicochemical properties of the material through desodiation and to yield a possible Na-ion cathode material. While there are indications of Na-deintercalation, the charge compensation mechanism appears to involve irreversible sulfur oxidation rather than manganese oxidation, thus preventing the application of Na2Mn2OS2 as a positive electrode for Na-ion batteries.
n8453c634fa76: Material discovery is the foundational process for fundamental investigations and useful applications of functional and structural materials. It is the prerequisite for all downstream processes including property determination, synthetic optimization and scale-up, doping, defect engineering, morphology control, and surface and interfacial tuning. Through extensive experimental and, more recently, computational exploration, the number of yet-to-be-discovered thermodynamically stable compounds in low-order phase spaces has rapidly shrunk. However, new materials are needed to foster advances in established and emerging applications, particularly those related to energy storage, conversion, and efficiency. Thinking beyond equilibrium phase diagrams, a much larger phase space of metastable compounds exists if such phases can be synthetically accessed. This Perspective highlights the role of reactive molten-salt ion exchange (MSIX) as a technique for metastable inorganic material discovery. We discuss the thermodynamics, kinetics, crystal chemistry, and atomic-scale characterization of reactive molten-salt ion exchange. Emergent phenomena in ion exchange such as interdiffusion and the mixed-ion effect and challenges associated with characterizing mixed-ion and heterogeneous systems receive extra attention. In consideration of the breadth of MSIX, fundamental principles and general reaction schemes are used where possible with specific examples extensively referenced. MSIX is contextualized by comparisons to adjacent fields that involve molten salts, ion transport, and metastable materials. Opportunities and missed opportunities associated with computational approaches to molten-salt reactions and metastable materials are discussed. Unique prospects for in situ diffraction and NMR crystallography are highlighted along with future directions, including extensions to solid-state ion exchange (SSIX).
n44d654c3e182: Metal–organic cages (MOCs) with unconventional topologies remain rare owing to the challenges associated with controlling coordination-driven self-assembly. Herein, we report the self-assembly of two unique Pd(II)-based coordination cages–peanut-shaped cage (C1, M18L14) and hemicage (C2, M12M2L22), from semiflexible tetratopic pyridyl ligands incorporating 9,10-dihydroanthracene and benzene backbones, respectively. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies reveal that cage C1 adopts a rare peanut-shaped structure comprising two interconnected cavities and both inward- and outward-oriented Pd(II) nodes, generating a highly electron-rich confined environment. In contrast, C2 forms an unprecedented boat-shaped architecture assembled through the cooperative incorporation of 90° and 180° Pd(II) acceptors within a single discrete cage. Despite their amorphous and nonporous nature, these assemblies demonstrate exceptional dual-capture performance toward volatile iodine species. Notably, C1 achieves iodine uptake capacities of 2.62 g g–1 under static vapor-phase conditions and 1.21 g g–1 under dynamic flow conditions, together with efficient CH3I adsorption of up to 1.05 g g–1 at 75 °C. Spectroscopic investigations and theoretical calculations reveal that the adsorption process is driven by synergistic charge-transfer interactions, polyiodide formation, electrostatic stabilization, and cavity confinement. Furthermore, both cages display excellent retention capability and recyclability, highlighting their potential as robust materials for radioactive iodine sequestration and environmental remediation.

n7bac2472b80c: Nanoparticle-induced local coordination compression couples with charge redistribution at FeN 4 /ZnN 3 S 1 sites, optimizing ORR energetics and enabling high-performance liquid and quasi-solid-state zinc–air batteries.
nb4b44fe42d17: Nonuniform deposition, interfacial instability, and dendrite growth at metal anodes drive capacity fade and increase the risk of short circuits, limiting their practical deployment in high-energy-density batteries. In the metal-anode...
n2c58b2d06982: Light-induced phase segregation limits the efficiency and stability of wide-band-gap mixed-halide perovskites. This work demonstrates that multi-site molecular regulation can cooperatively manage Frenkel defect-pair dynamics, thereby suppressing phase segregation. This stabilization is achieved by thermodynamically suppressing Frenkel defect-pair formation and dissociation while kinetically restricting subsequent halide redistribution.
ne2b86c450632: Nanopore protein sequencing has advanced from a theoretical ambition to a practical technology, overcoming major challenges in protein unfolding, transport and signal detection to achieve single-amino-acid and post-translational modification sensitivity. With both full-length and peptide-based approaches progressing towards commercialization, the field is now focused on scaling throughput and refining analysis tools to unlock a new generation of single-molecule proteomics.
nc78d4c42fe9f: Two decades on from the first atomic-scale devices, atom-based silicon quantum computers have progressed from proof of concept to scalable quantum processors that are rapidly gaining commercial traction. What remains is largely a matter of industrial-scale engineering and 3D integration.
nd96a615d3ec9: As the journal turns 20, we reflect on the journey nanoscale science has undertaken over the past two decades and how nanoscience-enabled technologies have had a real-world impact.
n3b7306b098f3: Quantum dots — semiconductor nanocrystals whose optical and electronic properties can be tuned by controlling their size, composition and surface chemistry — have found commercial success for display technologies. Their transition from nanophotonics research into an applied modern nanotechnology exemplifies the bottlenecks that many emerging technologies must overcome on the path to commercialization.
nb2f1eec7e23b: Curiosity-driven studies of lipid organization and lipid asymmetry in biological membranes led to scalable methods for making liposomes, efficient loading of drugs and ionizable cationic lipids. In turn, these advances led to lipid nanoparticles enabling the RNA medicine Onpattro and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, and they are now facilitating gene therapies that can potentially treat most human diseases.
n2dc08f16a75e: Single-atom catalysis has reshaped heterogeneous catalysis by shifting its central focus from surface and interface to isolated atom-centred active sites. This transition establishes a new paradigm for understanding reactivity, integrating experiments and theory, and advancing heterogeneous catalysis from empirical observations toward a more predictive and precise science.
nf1ff5a986198: Spin-transfer torque magnetoresistive random access memory has emerged as a leading non-volatile memory technology replacing embedded Flash in diverse fields including aerospace, automotive and healthcare applications.
nc6aa8f3cb4a1: After years of hype and research, there is still no graphene battery electrode in mass production, but researchers say the material shows promise for energy storage.
n2e47fb53617f: Tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides display interesting therapeutic properties; however, methods for their synthesis are limited. Now a Rh-catalysed process enables their synthesis through the development of a dual-function directing group that promotes C–H activation and C–N bond formation. The method provides access to a range of macrocycles, including pharmacophores of micitide 982 and tryglysin.
n30d6e5e89e89: Chiral allylic amines are key building blocks in the synthesis of bioactive molecules. Now a regio- and enantioselective method for their synthesis is reported. The Ni-catalysed process proceeds through homologation of enamines by cross-coupling with alkynes, forming a range of chiral allylic amines in good yield and with excellent enantioselectivity.
ne6813bddcde6: Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) have emerged as a highly desirable system for grid storage applications due to low-cost, high-energy density, and safe operating conditions. While AZMB studies often focus on functional mitigation of dendrite formation and the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), corrosion remains a more ambiguous yet crucial limiting factor in anode performance. Specifically, recent work points to persistent chemical corrosion as a major source of resting capacity loss in AZMBs. In this work, we present a wide-ranging mechanism for galvanic corrosion based on fundamental electrochemical thermodynamics and kinetics, highlighting the key roles of battery components, electrolyte conditions, and other contributing factors. Importantly, this mechanistic framework also applies when plating and stripping Zn on the anode, offering additional insight into the ever-elusive mechanistic origins of HER during those operating regimes. We then propose several promising avenues of inquiry and methods for further predicting, understanding, and mitigating corrosion in AZMBs.
n646b78aa0dd7: Triangular metal-oxo nodes are widely employed as catalytic motifs in metal–organic frameworks. Photocatalytic N2 fixation using the all-iron nodes can be switched off by replacing them with all-chromium nodes. However, the two nodes bind N2 in the opposite order to their activity. The present contribution shows that the electronic structure of the metal, which governs the small-molecule binding to the framework, determines the magnetic exchange topology of the [MIII3(μ3-O)] node. Combining broken-symmetry and non-collinear DFT, Hamiltonian-based reconstruction of Mössbauer spectra, and quantitative modeling of temperature-dependent magnetic susceptibility, one finds that FeIII exhibits a genuinely frustrated triangle of comparable antiferromagnetic interactions, whereas CrIII features an asymmetric dimer-plus-monomer governed by unusually strong biquadratic interaction, placing it outside the conventional Heisenberg regime. The distinct electronic structure is reflected in markedly different magnetic topologies and N2 binding strengths, rationalizing the contrasting photocatalytic activities of the two frameworks. These results establish magnetic exchange topology as an experimentally accessible descriptor of chemical function in trinuclear MOF nodes.
n318b3a927aa9: A supported NiGa alloy promoted the RWGS reaction via a hydrogen-assisted CO 2 reduction mechanism, achieving 36.5% CO 2 conversion with 95.2% CO selectivity.
n6f9cb1bf74cb: The one-pot conversion of concentrated glucose solutions to 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) is highly sought after by industries; however, due to poor selectivity, product instability and difficult isolation, it remains a challenge....
nf8412247aa79: Single-atom alloys (SAAs) are an emerging class of heterogeneous catalysts that maximize atom efficiency by embedding isolated reactive metal atoms within a host metal surface, creating well-defined active sites. Atomic isolation imparts unique catalytic properties, including high selectivity, resistance to poisoning, coking, and sintering, and in some cases the ability to circumvent conventional scaling relationships that limit traditional catalysts. This article focuses on progress in the SAA field since our 2020 review (Chem. Rev.2020, 120, 12044−12088.), while incorporating earlier foundational studies where relevant. We first examine the fundamental principles governing SAA formation, stability, electronic structure, reactivity, and selectivity, drawing on insights from experimental single-crystal model systems and theoretical studies. We then review the application of SAAs in a wide range of industrially important reactions, including hydrogenation, dehydrogenation, selective oxidation, water–gas shift, Fischer–Tropsch synthesis, and dry reforming, among others. Beyond thermal catalysis, SAAs demonstrate great promise in electrocatalysis and plasmon-driven chemistry. Their structurally simple active sites have also enabled the rational design of novel catalysts and promoters that challenge conventional catalytic intuition. Looking ahead, recent advances in computing, including machine-learning potentials, offer the opportunity to explore vast compositional spaces and discover new alloy chemistries for challenging reactions using the SAA concept.
neaeb3c1505d4: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) have emerged as promising electrochemical energy storage technologies for long-duration stationary applications. Although aqueous RFBs represent the most commercially mature class, they are inherently limited by a narrow electrochemical stability window and high temperature sensitivity. Nonaqueous RFBs (NRFBs) expand the accessible voltage and temperature ranges, offering a promising route toward high-energy-density storage for long-duration and extreme-environment applications. However, their practical deployment remains impeded by several challenges, including high costs, insufficient power density, limited cycling stability, and safety concerns. This review offers a systematic synthesis of recent advances in key NRFB components, encompassing solvents, supporting electrolytes, membranes, electrodes, and redox-active molecules. We also highlight emerging methodologies expected to accelerate development, including machine-learning-enabled screening, advanced characterization, and life cycle assessment. Finally, this review compares aqueous and nonaqueous systems from commercialization and sustainability perspectives. Collectively, this review aims to advance design principles and optimization strategies for NRFBs, providing guidance for next-generation low-cost, high-energy-density flow battery technologies.
nd38b8af0450d: Applicability and uncertainties of the BET analysis for porous materials, and its emerging alternatives.
n6590c73a60cf: Prussian blue analogues AxM[Fe(CN)6]1–y·zH2O (A = Na, K, M = Fe, Mn) possess a rich crystal chemistry that allows their use as insertion materials for batteries, water treatment, and smart windows, among others, applications. Despite being simple in appearance, their synthesis is complex and often results in defective, nonstoichiometric materials. These defects can be of neutral charge, such as interstitial water molecules, or charged, such as A+ vacancies or [Fe(CN)6]n− vacancies, whose presence implies charge balance by the remaining transition metal centers. In this work, a compound close to the Berlin green Fe[Fe(CN)6] nominal composition was synthesized, and its crystal structure, electrochemical properties, and electronic structure were investigated. Although usual characterization methods such as X-ray diffraction, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy agree well with the formation of Fe[Fe(CN)6], the material can only be intercalated to Na1.4Fe[Fe(CN)6]. This lack of capacity was hypothesized to arise from “hidden” [Fe(CN)6] vacancies. The charge balance associated with these vacancies implies partial reduction of the low-spin Fe, as confirmed by low-temperature 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy and further high-angular-resolution diffraction experiments. This study suggests that numerous materials previously described as “Berlin green” in the literature might actually be substantially hexacyanoferrate defective.
nfecfae089ada: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) fundamentally relies on a distinct disparity in surface chemical states between growth and nongrowth area. For SiO2/Cu patterned architectures, the oxidation of the Cu surface serves as a primary driver for the loss of selectivity as the ALD process proceeds. Herein, an alcohol-mediated AS-ALD process is proposed, utilizing alcohols with varying carbon chain lengths to precisely modulate surface chemical states to enhance selectivity of AS-ALD WOx film. A competitive-synergistic mechanism involving surface reductive capability and steric hindrance is identified as the governing factor for process selectivity. Results demonstrate that while the reducing ability of alcohols on oxidized Cu surfaces diminishes with increasing carbon chain length, their steric hindrance increases. EtOH was identified as the optimal pretreatment agent, yielding an exceptional selectivity exceeding 99.9% on SiO2/Cu patterned surface. Moreover, the alcohol-mediated AS-ALD process is successfully extended to other oxide systems with precursors bearing analogous ligands, demonstrating the generality of the proposed strategy. This work provides a versatile methodology for modulating surface reductive capability and steric hindrance to achieve high-selectivity AS-ALD.
n5b7da1a26edc: Alkali manganese oxynitridophosphates A1.1Mn2.9P3O8N2 (A = Na, Li) were prepared by one-step solid-state ammonolysis, where the lithium analogue is obtained directly rather than by alkali-ion exchange from the sodium compound. Both compositions crystallize in a previously unreported orthorhombic Pbcn framework, in which ordered O/N environments, unusual manganese coordination in MnO5N and MnO6N2 polyhedra, and alkali–manganese disorder are accommodated within the same structure. The proposed structural model is supported by complementary synchrotron X-ray and neutron powder diffraction, electron microscopy, solid-state NMR and XAS data, as well as density functional theory calculations. Magnetic susceptibility is consistent with predominantly Mn2+ and antiferromagnetic ordering below 35.1 K for the Li phase and 32.6 K for the Na phase. Although the Mn2+/Mn3+ redox couple lies within the accessible potential window of nonaqueous M-ion batteries, reversible alkali extraction is limited by the restricted migration pathways imposed by the framework. Overall, this work expands the compositional and structural landscape of oxynitridophosphates and highlights nitrogen incorporation in phosphate crystal chemistry as a route to unconventional coordination environments, new framework connectivities and functional properties.
n4b6cc05951ad: Colloidal germanium quantum dots (GeQDs) hold promise for solution-processable optoelectronics, yet their performance is often constrained by the limited reactivity of hydride-terminated surfaces and the insulating nature of conventional capping ligands. Here, we introduce a room-temperature selenylation strategy that harnesses the intrinsically weak and polarizable Ge–H bonds on freshly etched GeQD surfaces to drive Se–Se bond activation of diorganyl diselenides. This polarization-assisted concerted process proceeds without radical initiators or external stimuli, yielding robust Ge–SeR surface linkages that effectively passivate the GeQDs against oxidation while introducing a soft, polarizable chalcogenide-rich surface. The resulting RSe-GeQDs show notably improved optical properties and charge carrier mobilities compared to oleylamine-functionalized GeQDs. The direct, catalyst-free nature of this approach offers a versatile platform for the development of solution-processable germanium-based optoelectronic devices.
n9a6ea7e8b76f: Electrolytes composed of mixed solvents are of significant scientific and technological importance in lithium-ion and beyond-lithium-ion batteries, and more broadly across physical chemistry. Their emergence has highlighted the importance of multiscale phenomena, particularly the development of nanoscale solution heterogeneities. It is therefore essential to assess how these inhomogeneities and nanoscale aggregates influence solvation, transport, and electronic properties. Here we investigate the solution structure and transport properties of aqueous zinc sulfate electrolytes with acetonitrile (ACN) additives, where the addition of ACN leads to improved cyclability. Using complementary anomalous small-angle X-ray scattering, X-ray pair distribution function, electrochemistry, and NMR, we identify the presence of salt-rich-water-rich and salt-poor-ACN-rich nanoheterogeneities and, at higher ACN concentrations, liquid–liquid phase separation. We find that the size of zinc sulfate ion clusters in the water domains increases slightly upon ACN addition, while the ACN-rich domains grow much larger as phase separation is approached. The inverse Haven ratio, determined using the ionic conductivity and diffusivity, is much less than unity and decreases slightly upon addition of ACN, which shows ion–ion interactions. We speculate that the increased ion–ion interactions with increased ACN are a result of a reduction in free water, the increase in zinc sulfate cluster size, and/or an increase in solution tortuosity. This work highlights key phenomena to consider when engineering new water-organic-salt electrolyte systems and establishes a phase diagram for water–ACN–ZnSO4 that can guide advances, such as self-adaptive electrolytes.
n5620ea80d3d1: Wide-temperature-range combined heat and cold storage couples heating and cooling demand across 0–100 °C. A system-user-grid assessment identifies targeted deployment opportunities in urban complexes for energy, economic and grid benefits.
n9bf97f69680b: Aviation's climate impact goes beyond CO2, yet current policies such as the EU's ReFuelEU regulation push almost exclusively toward sustainable fuels, overlooking an alternative: permanently capturing CO2 from the air via DACCS while continuing to burn fossil jet fuel. Comparing long-term costs of both approaches, we find DACCS is 49%–69% cheaper than synthetic fuels and needs far less renewable electricity, suggesting that current policy may be locking aviation into a costlier decarbonization path than necessary.
n24a7fb176953: Methane pyrolysis can produce hydrogen while sequestering solid carbon, but efficient high-grade heat delivery and coking management remain challenging. This study shows that high-frequency magnetic induction directly and volumetrically heats molten salt bubbling beds with stable power delivery, providing a scalable route for methane pyrolysis while managing solid carbon formation. These principles have applicability more broadly to molten salt chemical conversion and thermal energy storage systems.
n71f3585b7a45: Efforts to improve carbon dioxide electroreduction have often focused on the catalyst. Now, by focusing on the gas instead, non-thermal plasma activation can unlock products that are not accessible through conventional electrocatalysis.
nf495575612b6: Integrating distinct weaving topologies within a single molecular network creates coupled deformation modes and adaptive adsorption behaviour, pointing to a shift from constructing molecular topologies to exploiting them for functions.
n860fed4f84de: Four-membered heterocycles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, yet valuable thietanes remain underexplored compared with widely studied oxetanes and azetidines. Now a one-step skeletal editing strategy is reported that directly converts oxetanes into thietanes using thiourea.
n8cf20cf25776: Research on enantioselective photocatalysis has so far been focused on molecular photocatalysts or large yet easily adaptable photoenzymes. However, both catalysis classes display deficiencies either due to their limited adaptability or their high molecular weight. Here we show that small peptides can bridge the gap between the currently used photocatalysts by combining structural flexibility and low molecular weight. We constructed a small peptide that displays a pyroglutamic acid at its N terminus for substrate recognition. At the C terminus, a thioxanthone-based amino acid was installed to harvest photons and to act catalytically by energy transfer. Two amino acids were sufficient to link the two components, resulting in a photocatalytically active tetrapeptide that was used both for photochemical deracemization and enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition reactions. Our results demonstrate that small peptides with a molecular weight below 750 Da can act as efficient molecular catalysts for enantioselective photochemical transformations.
neab46ce06322: Heteroleptic silylium ions with different substituents at the silicon atom are generally not accessible using established tools for producing such reactive intermediates because substituent exchange reactions occur in acidic media, leading to homoleptic silylium ions with three identical alkyl and aryl substituents, respectively. Here we report a broadly applicable route to heteroleptic silylium ions using halosilanes as silylium ion precursors, which are less prone to that scrambling process. While this deceptively simple method has failed so far owing to the lack of a suitable halide-abstracting agent, superhalophilic halogen-substituted silylium ions enable smooth halide abstraction from a diverse set of halosilanes at ambient temperature without substituent redistribution. Accordingly, this approach provides access to essentially any heteroleptic acyclic as well as cyclic silylium-ion motif from common halosilanes, including trialkyl-, dialkyl(aryl)-, alkyldiaryl- and triaryl-substituted congeners. Computational calculations reveal the mechanism of heteroleptic silylium-ion formation and the origin of the suppressed substituent-scrambling process.
n3a0704437377: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a major kinetic bottleneck in anodic water splitting because of sluggish adsorption and desorption kinetics of O-containing intermediates. Optimizing the adsorption strength of various O-containing intermediates in accordance with the Sabatier principle involves the precise tuning of the active-site electronic structure. Herein, we explore a p-block metal-assisted synergism regulation strategy in NiFe layered double hydroxides (LDHs) by introducing group-13 elements (Al, Ga, In) as dopants. Among various doped LDHs, In-doped NiFe-LDH shows the highest OER activity by demanding an overpotential value of 298 mV at 10 mA/cm2 along with enhanced intrinsic turnover frequency and long-term stability. X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals that In3+ preferentially occupies the Fe coordination sites, while valence-band X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (VB-XPS) confirms enhanced electronic coupling in the Ni–O–In framework. Density functional theory (DFT) additionally suggests that the In 5p orbitals strongly hybridize with the O 2p and Ni 3d states, establishing a Ni3d-O2p-In5p electronic interaction that regulates the Ni electronic structure and optimizes the adsorption energies of O-containing intermediates. The resulting d-p-p orbital hybridization offers an efficient pathway for charge delocalization and strengthens the M–O covalency, thereby accelerating the OER kinetics. This study elucidates the structure–activity relationship and identifies p-block metal-induced orbital hybridization as an effective strategy for developing high-performance oxygen evolution electrocatalysts, offering an alternative to conventional transition-metal modification approaches.
n0d483db6fb87: Understanding the correlated dynamics of multiple molecular rotators in crystalline supramolecular assemblies is essential for designing functional molecular machines, yet deconvoluting the motions of distinct components remains inherently challenging due to the limitations of individual techniques. Here, we report a synergistic approach that combines solid-state Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (SSNMR) and dielectric spectroscopy to quantitatively resolve multirotor dynamics in a family of isostructural supramolecular gyroscopic complex architectures composed of alkyl ammonium, crown ether, and metal halide hydrate. SSNMR unambiguously reveals both the tert-butylammonium cation and the 18-crown-6 macrocycle as independent rotators─a distinction often ambiguous in such systems. Crucially, by correlating SSNMR-derived dynamics of the crown ether with dielectric relaxation of the coordinated water molecule, we uncover their synchronized rotation across a wide temperature range, mediated by charge-assisted hydrogen bonding. These findings reveal a cooperative multirotor gyroscopic model featuring synchronous rotation of an integrated coaxial crown ether–water–ammonium trio-rotator, accompanied by correlated alkyl reorientation. This synergy validates the dielectric relaxation principle in a complex, multirotor crystalline environment where unambiguous peak assignment has been a longstanding challenge. This work establishes a generalizable methodology for dissecting complex, multicomponent dynamics in crystalline materials, directly bridging molecular-scale motion to macroscopic dielectric response.
n815edb2d6801: Phosphorus-mediated reactions that leverage the thermodynamic driving force of phosphorus(III) oxidation are crucial in all areas of the chemical industry. While substantial progress has been made in phosphorus(III/V) redox organocatalysis to develop catalytic alternatives, the rising field of redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis has revealed new modes of phosphorus-based reactivity in chemical transformations without requiring stoichiometric reductants. This review highlights key advances in redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis with a focus on fundamental phosphorus(V) reactivity, organized by the catalyst structure and emphasizing its role as a Lewis acid, Brønsted acid/base, nucleophile, superbase, or single-electron transfer agent. We close with remarks connecting established reactivity paradigms that will likely be applied to new generations of phosphorus(V) catalysts capable of solving modern synthetic challenges.
na500abd96e0f: Formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI3) perovskites are promising for high-performance solar cells; however, the low surface energy of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) impedes α-phase nucleation in inverted devices. Here, we report a formamidinium (FA)-solvent intermediate-mediated self-seeding crystallization strategy to enable quality α-phase FAPbI3. By employing N-formylmorpholine (NFM) as a non-toxic solvent, (FA···NFM)PbI3 intermediates are formed, thereby lowering the phase-transition barrier and promoting the spontaneous formation of α-phase nuclei at the early stage of crystallization. These preformed nuclei serve as intrinsic seeds, facilitating rapid nucleation and orientated crystal growth. Consequently, NFM-based devices achieve efficiencies of 26.41% and 26.56% using 2-methoxyethanol (2-Me) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) as primary solvents, respectively, with a 1 cm2 device reaching 25.47%. The unencapsulated devices retain 85% and 90% of their initial efficiencies after 1200 h illumination and 1400 h thermal aging at 85 °C, respectively.
n63eaef75d86b: Silicon anodes unlock higher energy density in Li-ion batteries but suffer from poor calendar life due to inadequately passivating solid–electrolyte interphases (SEIs). Here, we contrast the calendar aging behaviors of single- and mixed-salt locally superconcentrated electrolytes (LSCEs) against carbonate electrolytes. Mixed-salt LSCE cells retained 96% and 44% of precalendar capacity after one month and then after five months, while carbonate electrolyte cells retained 77% and 1%, respectively. The mixed-salt LSCE advantage is tied to the formation of a predominantly inorganic SEI, evidenced by nanoscale Fourier transform infrared spectromicroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and 3D time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry. After 5 months, however, perturbations to SEIs were evident in all cells, accelerating voltage decay and capacity loss by lithium inventory loss associated with SEI growth. These findings suggest that future electrolytes may benefit from strategies that continuously reinforce the SEI through controlled anion and solvent redox in LSCEs.
n43aedc67ebcd: Au/ZnO exhibits high catalytic activity for the selective aerobic oxidation of cinnamyl alcohol at room temperature. This is enabled by efficient O 2 activation at the Au–ZnO perimeter sites, in conjunction with a H 2 -free H 2 O 2 generation mechanism.
nafe452ce86d0: Operando nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unique insight into chemical changes in batteries during use but has largely been limited to custom plastic cells. Unfortunately, the metal casings that house commercial batteries distort and shield radiofrequency (RF) fields required for excitation and detection in NMR. Here, we use operando7Li NMR spectroscopy to study metal-encased batteries in both coin and pouch cell formats without modifying the cell or casing. We benchmark NMR spectra obtained from stainless-steel coin cells and aluminum-laminate pouch cells to plastic coin cells and show that casing composition, auxiliary hardware, and sample placement strongly influence observed shift, signal intensity, and line shape due to bulk magnetic susceptibility effects and RF attenuation upon interacting with cell parts. These effects are most severe in stainless-steel coin cells (and in particular 304-grade stainless steel) but can be mitigated through the use of Al spacers while retaining the stainless-steel caps and springs. In light of these considerations, we leverage operando7Li NMR to track lithium plating/stripping and monitor the accumulation of electrochemically inactive “dead” lithium (Li0) during galvanostatic cycling in coin and pouch cells. In pouch cells, the lean electrolyte volume allows us to resolve changes in the 7Li electrolyte signal during formation that are consistent with electrolyte redistribution and wetting. Taken together, these results demonstrate how to alter cell susceptibility to improve NMR signals during operando measurements in commercially relevant form factors while also establishing the cell design constraints that limit quantitative interpretation.
nad30fd7589e8: Most zero-dimensional hybrid metal halides enable emission in the first near-infrared (NIR-I) region (650–950 nm), and the shorter wavelengths result in poor photon penetration depth. Although a variety of mechanisms are involved in the explanation of such a broad band with a large Stokes shift, the exploration of the structural origin of the NIR optical activity remains challenging due to misconceptions about excitons and experimental limitations. A strategy that spatially confines 5s2 ions within edge-shared [Sb2Cl8]2– units with controlled lattice distortion is proposed to cause a Jahn–Teller effect (JTE) during the interconfiguration transition (3P1 → 1S0). A family of hybrid metal halides doped with Bi3+,In3+ or Bi3+/In3+ demonstrates that the fine interplay between the Jahn–Teller effect and spin–orbit coupling (SOC) takes into full consideration orbital degeneracy and electron flipping, thus boosting the photoluminescence quantum yield to 12%. TD-DFT calculations visualize the symmetry of the two lattices within a dimeric structure varying with specific modes, and the rational assignment of the energy gap (ground state: 3.69 eV; excited state: 1.22 eV) between 1S0 and 3P1 is highly consistent with the experimental findings (λex = 330 nm; λem = 1100 nm). Leveraging the (BTBAC)2Sb2Cl8 sample, electroluminescence pumped by a UV-LED chip yields a highly efficient NIR-II emission, and the phosphor displays diverse functions in night vision and anticounterfeiting.
n0b352334afcf: Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries are severely hindered by the shuttle effect of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) and uncontrolled lithium dendrite growth. The intentional introduction of ligand defects and oxygen vacancies reduces particle size, establishes a hierarchical porous structure, and amplifies local Lewis acidity. Consequently, the D-MOF-303 coating layer provides exceptional chemisorption and accelerated electrocatalytic conversion kinetics for LiPSs, while concurrently homogenizing lithium-ion flux to achieve long-term dendrite-free lithium plating. Benefiting from these synergistic merits, the resulting Li–S full cells exhibit high capacity retention over 500 cycles at 0.5 C, enhanced rate capability up to 3 C, and notable environmental resilience under high-humidity aging conditions. This work demonstrates the potential of coordination defect engineering in metal–organic frameworks for advancing high-energy-density and commercially viable energy storage technologies.
